title: Commerce Integrations Lead / Sales Engineer
description:
See something that should exist? Build it.
See a better way? Do it.

At Terrific, every role directly impacts how we grow from product to revenue to customer experience. We’re building the next generation of social commerce through live shopping powered by real-time data and AI.

And we believe customer data should belong to the brands who earn it — not third-party platforms.


Commerce Integrations Lead / Sales Engineer

LATAM · Full-time Contract · Remote
Product & Engineering · eCommerce · Integrations · AI
Start date: September 2026

Integrations & Technical Solutions Lead

LATAM or EMEA · Full-time Contract · Remote
Product & Engineering · eCommerce · Integrations · AI

See something that should connect? Build it.
See a process that should exist? Create it.

At Terrific, we’re building the next generation of social commerce—helping brands turn content, creators, live experiences and AI into commerce they own.

Our technology brings shoppable video, live shopping, interactive timelines, polls and product carousels directly onto a merchant’s website or app.

Now we’re looking for an Commerce Integrations Lead/Sales Engineer to help us connect Terrific to the wider commerce ecosystem—and build the systems that make those connections faster every time.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is not a role where you’ll inherit a finished playbook.

You’ll help write it.

You’ll work across Product, Engineering, Sales and Customer Success to solve the technical problems that determine whether a customer can launch, how quickly they see value and how easily we can support the next merchant.

One day, you may investigate how a global retailer’s cart works across multiple markets. The next, you may build a lightweight integration, help shape a live commercial opportunity, automate part of our technical-discovery process or prepare an app for a commerce marketplace.

You’ll work directly with teammates and customers across Latin America, Europe, Israel and the United States. You’ll have visibility into the full journey—from the first sales conversation through integration, launch and ongoing performance.

If you enjoy moving between technology, customers and commercial problems—and want the freedom to build rather than simply maintain—this role offers unusual room to make an impact.

WHAT YOU’LL BUILD

Terrific needs to connect with the platforms and tools merchants already use.

You’ll help us expand and improve integrations across:

  • Shopify

  • VTEX

  • Adobe Commerce/Magento

  • WooCommerce

  • Salesforce Commerce Cloud

  • BigCommerce

  • Tiendanube/Nuvemshop

  • Wix

  • PrestaShop

  • Shopware

  • Custom and headless commerce environments

  • Native mobile applications

You’ll also explore integrations with platforms such as Klaviyo, Attentive, Gorgias, Zendesk, Yotpo, Segment, Zapier, Google Merchant Center and Meta Commerce Manager.

Over time, you’ll help Terrific build a stronger marketplace presence, a more repeatable onboarding process and a technical integration layer that can scale across customers and markets.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

  • Investigating merchant websites, applications and commerce stacks.

  • Understanding how product catalogs, variants, carts and checkout flows work.

  • Assessing technical feasibility for active commercial opportunities.

  • Turning customer requirements into clear technical recommendations.

  • Building, testing and improving integrations across major ecommerce platforms.

  • Helping merchants move from signed agreement to their first live Terrific experience.

  • Working directly with customer engineers and internal commercial teams.

  • Supporting technical discovery, proposals, security reviews and proofs of concept.

  • Improving the reliability of product feeds, event tracking, cart actions and embeds.

  • Publishing and maintaining Terrific apps across relevant commerce marketplaces.

  • Building tools, scripts, automations and AI agents that make integration work faster.

  • Turning repeated customer friction into clear Product and Engineering priorities.

  • Creating the documentation and processes that will support future customers and teammates.

You won’t be expected to solve everything alone. You will be expected to take ownership, bring the right people together and move the problem forward.

WHO YOU ARE

You’re technical, curious and commercially aware.

You want to understand why something matters to the customer—not only how it works in the code.

You’re comfortable opening DevTools, tracing an API request, reading someone else’s implementation and building a practical solution. You can move from a technical conversation with engineers to a commercial conversation with Sales or a customer without losing the thread.

You communicate clearly, ask good questions and know when to challenge an assumption.

You don’t need every process to be defined before you begin. You like taking something that is currently handled differently each time and turning it into a system the company can reuse.

You also understand that speed and judgment matter in a startup. Sometimes the right answer is a full integration. Sometimes it is a simpler path that gets the customer live this week.

HOW YOU’LL USE AI

Terrific is AI-native by default.

We don’t treat AI as a separate initiative or an occasional productivity tool. We use it as part of how we investigate, build, document and improve our work.

In this role, you’ll have the freedom to use AI to:

  • Accelerate technical discovery and research.

  • Generate and test scripts.

  • Automate repetitive integration tasks.

  • Build internal agents and tools.

  • Improve documentation and knowledge sharing.

  • Monitor integrations and identify problems earlier.

  • Help non-technical teams access technical answers faster.

We’re interested in what you can build with AI—not whether you use a particular tool.

The goal is to create leverage for the whole company, not simply complete your own work faster.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • At least three years of hands-on development or technical integration experience.

  • Production experience with at least two major ecommerce platforms.

  • Experience working with APIs, product feeds, webhooks, authentication, carts or checkout flows.

  • Ability to read unfamiliar code, write working scripts and debug browser or network behavior.

  • Experience working directly with customers, merchants or external technical teams.

  • Clear written and verbal communication.

  • Good judgment about effort, risk and commercial value.

  • Comfort working independently within a distributed, international team.

  • Professional fluency in English.

  • Professional fluency in Spanish or Portuguese.

Experience with live shopping, social commerce, video commerce, marketplace apps or large international retailers is a strong advantage.

French is valuable for our EMEA accounts.

SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first months, you will:

  • Build a clear picture of Terrific’s current integration landscape.

  • Take ownership of live customer integration work.

  • Create a repeatable approach to technical discovery and feasibility.

  • Reduce the time between signed agreement and customer launch.

  • Improve how Sales, Product, Engineering and Customer Success work together.

  • Move new platform integrations into production.

  • Help define which marketplace and partner integrations we build next.

  • Introduce automations and AI-powered workflows that save the team time.

  • Create a roadmap for how Terrific’s integration ecosystem should grow.

Success is not following a process perfectly.

Success is leaving us with a better process than the one you joined.

WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

Many technical integration roles begin with a ticket and end when the ticket is closed.

This one begins with a customer opportunity.

You’ll see how technical decisions affect sales, launch timelines, customer experience and revenue. You’ll work across teams and countries, with direct access to the people making product and commercial decisions.

You’ll have meaningful freedom to decide how problems should be approached, which tools should be built and what Terrific’s integration function should become.

There is no process set in stone—and that is the opportunity.

REQUIRED

  • Based in Latin America—preferably Mexico, Argentina, Brazil or Colombia—or within a compatible EMEA time zone.

  • Available for a full-time independent-contractor engagement.

  • Able to work remotely with teammates and customers across global time zones.

  • Professional fluency in English.

  • Professional fluency in Spanish and/or Portuguese.

  • At least three years of hands-on development or technical integration experience.

  • Production experience with ecommerce platforms, APIs or merchant technology.

Terrific operates as a global company, and English is our primary business language. Interviews, documentation and regular internal communication will be conducted in English.

Required:
  • Deep experience in at least one of Terrific’s three commercial pillars — eCommerce, Marketing, or Media — and enough fluency across the other two to contribute credibly from day 1.
  • Terrific operates as a global company, and English is our primary business language. As such, all roles require fluency in written and spoken English.
Be part of the change that’s quietly reshaping how people discover and buy online.
Passionate about social media and e-commerce? Come build what’s next at Terrific.
Please note: We review every application carefully. While we may not be able to respond to everyone, we will reach out to candidates whose experience aligns with what we’re building.

This position is responsible for reviewing weekly and daily OR schedules as well as instrument reports from the current electronic instrument tracking system to determine and forecast the needs of the specific service line up to and including determining instrument need and tray conflicts and setting assembly priority. The SP Liaison position will review any and all conflicts with the OR Charge Nurse or Service Line Manager, performing daily rounds in the suite with frequency throughout the shift to help manage any instrument and supply issues or conflicts, as well as complete the needs list for the next day's cases. Serving as a fully functional technician in the Sterile Processing department as needed, this position must demonstrate advanced knowledge of sterilization techniques, surgical instruments, and have an in-depth understanding of the relationship between Sterile Processing and other departments within the hospital.

FLSA STATUS
Non-exempt

QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION
  • High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.)

EXPERIENCE
  • Four years of Sterile Processing experience in an acute care hospital
  • Service line experience preferred

LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS
Required
  • Sterile Processing certification: CRCST or CSPDT and
  • Certified Instrument certification: CIS or CSIS within 1 year

KNOWLEDGE AND ABILITIES
  • Demonstrates the skills and competencies necessary to safely perform the assigned job, determined through on-going skills, competency assessments, and performance evaluations
  • Sufficient proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing the English language necessary to perform the essential functions of this job, especially with regard to activities impacting patient or employee safety or security
  • Ability to effectively communicate with patients, physicians, family members and co-workers in a manner consistent with a customer service focus and application of positive language principles
  • Independently demonstrates the skills and competencies necessary to safely perform the assigned job, determined through on-going skills, competency assessments, and performance evaluations
  • Follows Universal Precautions by wearing the appropriate protective attire while working in the Decontamination area
  • Advanced knowledge of infection control, decontamination, and sterilization techniques
  • Knowledge and ability to operate, troubleshoot, and train staff on all departmental equipment including, but no limited to, sterilizers, washers, ultrasonic washers, and cart washers
  • Proficiency in utilization of basic computer programs such as Microsoft Office and electronic instrument tracking system, if applicable
  • Displays ability to manage time by completing assigned work and cleaning workstation at the end of each shift as a fully competent SPD Tech
  • Demonstrates advanced knowledge of sterilization techniques, surgical instruments. Completes departmental and institutional competencies within established required timelines
  • Reads the OR Schedule proficiently
  • Able to work independently, self-guided and motivated


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

PEOPLE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Serves as the primary representative/liaison of Sterile Processing department through a collaborative working relationship with Operating Room (OR) staff to identify process improvement needs for SPD to share with management. Assumes charge responsibility in the absence of the SPD Coordinator.
  • Demonstrates teamwork by responding positively to requests for assistance. Collaborates to foster healthy work relationships in the work environment. Seeks guidance from interprofessional health care team, when needed, and applies feedback to improve workflow outcomes.
  • Works collaboratively with the OR staff to provide timely sterile products, trays, and case carts, where applicable, based on previously identified needs, demonstrating consistency and continuous workflow between the OR and Sterile Processing. Drives recommendations for improvement of department scores for employee engagement.

SERVICE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Serves as the content expert by performing decontamination and assembling of complex surgical trays, individual and potentially customized instrumentation and equipment utilizing established count sheets. Consistently wraps or contains items appropriately according to size and type of instrument or equipment.
  • Performs, documents, and maintains all immediate use steam sterilization cycles ran within the OR suite.
  • Monitors, reads, documents, and interprets all parameters for all types of sterilizers to ensure proper function, i.e., Steam, ETO and Low Temperature Hydrogen Peroxide.

QUALITY/SAFETY ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Implements effective workflow with staff from the interprofessional health care team concerning patient safety to improve outcomes and the safe transition of care through effective assignment and shift handoffs and uses a structured format for regular communication with staff members and physicians, as appropriate.
  • Ensures the effectiveness of the sterilization process by using internal, external and biological monitoring systems appropriately utilizing established department protocols and sterilizer manufacturers’ instructions for use.
  • Utilizes appropriate cleaning detergents and agents by reading directions and MSDS sheets. Utilizes all department equipment according to manufacturers’ instructions for use and departmental policies and protocols.

FINANCE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Utilizes department resources, i.e., tracking system, to ensure completeness of trays, instruments, and equipment according to count sheets. Provides a daily location point of sterilized items ready for OR use.
  • Serves as primary contact for identified items needing repaired by OR staff. Communicates with instrument repair technician and/or coordinator responsible for repairs to ensure needed service in complete or in process.
  • Collaborates with OR preference card team or account sheets to identify changes needed to preference cards, preventing unnecessary items from being processed.

GROWTH/INNOVATION ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Presents areas of innovation, efficiency and improvement in patient care or unit operations using manufacturer’s instructions for use (IFUs) to the Sterile Processing team, in collaboration with SPD educator, as applicable.
  • Serves as the key resource for understanding and implementing the surgical equipment requirements of the applicable service line.
  • Represents the OR by supplying SPD-related information to Shared Governance Committee and department management. Completes and updates the My Development Plan on an on-going basis.


SUPPLEMENTAL REQUIREMENTS
    WORK ATTIRE
    • Uniform: Yes
    • Scrubs: Yes
    • Business professional: No
    • Other (department approved): No

    ON-CALL*
    *Note that employees may be required to be on-call during emergencies (ie. Disaster, Severe Weather Events, etc) regardless of selection below.
    • On Call* No

    TRAVEL**
    **Travel specifications may vary by department**
    • May require travel within the Houston Metropolitan area No
    • May require travel outside Houston Metropolitan area No



Work Shift:

3 - Night (United States of America)



Job Category:

Non-clinical

Houston Methodist Hospital is recognized by U.S. News & World Report as the No. 1 hospital in Texas and one of America’s “Best Hospitals.” As a full-service, acute-care hospital located in the Texas Medical Center and the flagship hospital of Houston Methodist, it has evolved into one of the nation’s largest nonprofit teaching hospitals and a leader in innovative medical research with a comprehensive residency program. Two of Houston Methodist’s primary academic affiliates are among the nation’s leading health care organizations: Weill Cornell Medicine and New York-Presbyterian Hospital. Houston Methodist also has affiliations with Texas A&M University and the University of Houston. Houston Methodist Hospital offers unparalleled care for thousands of patients from around the world.

title: Director Facilities - Norman Area
description:
This position is located in Norman area.

Job Summary: The Director of Facilities and Fleet is responsible for all areas of facility/property management and maintenance of agency owned properties and fleet. This position will also serve as point person for leased properties including lease negotiations and problem resolution. Other responsibilities include service contract management, physical site security and safety, janitorial, grounds maintenance, vendor relations, and supervision of all employees responsible for facilities. This individual will have direct supervisory responsibilities for facility contractors.

POSITION SPECIFIC DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Facility Operations & Maintenance

  • Assists in the development of and ensures execution of all maintenance programs relating to the interior and exterior conditions and appearance of the properties, assuring the highest levels of quality at the best value.
  • Responsible for communicating to all sites management approved standards and requirements for lobby, grounds, signage, offices, and common areas appearance and maintenance.
  • Responsible for arranging installation of interior and exterior signage. Work with Communications Department for graphic design signage standards.
  • Manage warehouse furniture and coordination of delivery.
  • Responsible for ordering furniture, other office equipment, or other FFE as identified in keeping with established design elements of each site.
  • Responsible for leadership of disaster recovery of physical plants at agency locations in coordination with executive leadership team.
  • Work closely with CIO in matters pertaining to technology infrastructure in facilities.
  • Prepare regular reports on facility operations, janitorial & maintenance for budgets and administration as requested.
  • Manage all agency relocations, including securing bids with vendors; coordination of moves with managerial staff; arranging for packing and unpacking; and other related relocation tasks.
  • Represent the agency with power utility companies. Periodically evaluate minimization of power consumption initiatives.
  • Establish and manage agency wide recycling and other green initiatives.
  • Oversee and coordinate the agency’s medical waste disposal processes.
  • Oversee staff responsible for ensuring proper conference room needs, resource scheduling and room setups are being completed in a timely fashion.
  • Oversee all maintenance and upgrades of security systems with vendors.
  • Oversee all agency storage facilities to maintain obstacle & hazard free areas.
  • Responsible for oversight of seasonal decorating of agency owned properties.

Service & Vendor Contract Management

  • Negotiate, select, and manage all service contracts for facilities; vendor negotiation of service agreements and day-to-day monitoring of vendor performance. Work with the General Counsel on contracts regarding the same.
  • Provide oversight of repairs and maintenance for all agency owned facility equipment including elevators, chillers, fire systems, parking lots, irrigation, lighting, heating and air conditioning, roofing, and other items.

Janitorial

  • Evaluate and serve as liaison with janitorial services vendors and make recommendations regarding appropriate solutions for agency needs.
  • Manage janitorial staff and oversee vendors to ensure that all tasks are performed on a timely schedule.
  • Centralize purchase of all janitorial supplies and cleaning equipment and maintain appropriate inventories.

Grounds

  • Ensure all leased and owned properties have arrangements in place for ice and snow removal.
  • Ensure all owned properties have adequate grounds maintenance.
  • Evaluate and oversee the replacement of landscaping and irrigation when needed.
  • Work with Communications Department to coordinate all internal and external signage needs.

Lease Management

  • Serve as point of contact for all rented space, oversee and validate that all issues and problems are resolved satisfactorily.
  • Facilitate lease negotiations for all rented space and work with General Counsel to finalize any lease agreements.
  • Maintain current lease documents ensuring original resides with agency Controller.

Fleet Management

  • Responsible for managing fleet leases.
  • Manage vehicle maintenance schedules to ensure compliance with established standards and timetables.
  • Oversee the vehicle training and road test with all new operators of agency vehicles.
  • Coordinate insurance coverage for authorized drivers of agency vehicles with the COO.
  • Coordinate all body repairs to agency vehicles with staff, insurance carrier, and vendors.
  • Coordinate all employee driving record verifications with Human Resources.
  • Coordinate the purchase, lease, or retirement of agency vehicles with Program Managers and the Finance Department.
  • Ensure best value for purchase of tires, gasoline, and auto repair.

Inventory Control

  • Provide for inventory control within agency established protocols.
  • Provide for agency supply control at new facilities then throughout all facilities.
  • Provide for effective use of basement space at Annex and Lapidus Center.

Employee Supervision

  • Supervise all facilities staff to assure quality work product and performance.
  • Work with HR to assure any necessary licensure or certifications are current for all facilities staff.

Physical Security

  • Work with executive management to determine proper level of security at all sites.
  • Retain security services for all owned buildings and other sites as needed for specific program.
  • Create and manage plan for ensuring employee and visitor access to facilities is in compliance with agency policies, procedures, and protocols.
  • Oversee acquisition of First Response Certificate for all sites.

Emergency response

  • Work closely with communication department to update, monitor and ensure leadership access to Emergency Response Team Manual

Site Safety

  • Leads and conducts quarterly safety meetings and any needed training with all Safety Officers.
  • Works with COO and CCO to provide safety and security agency-wide trainings or updates as needed, but at least twice annually.
  • Prepares quarterly Quality Improvement Report on Safety Committee activities.
  • Ensures the fire marshal reports occur on yearly basis.
  • Work with all agency building managers to ensure that security codes are changed on a scheduled and as needed basis and notify staff accordingly.
  • Oversee Agency Safety program executed at each site by assigned Safety Officer.
  • Provide annual risk assessment for physical site security.
  • Ensure facility safety checklist audits are completed according to prescribed schedule.
  • Works with CCO and the training department to assure training materials for safety and security are up to date and available for staff on the appropriate agency microsites.

QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or related field

EXPERIENCE:

  • 7+ years of experience in property management of multiple facilities.

PERFORMANCE COMPETENCIES:

  • Communication
  • Decision Making
  • Engagement
  • Initiative and Accountability
  • Interpersonal
  • Learning
  • Organizational Alignment
  • Quality of Work

KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES:

  • Knowledge of building systems, mechanical systems, and landscaping/grounds maintenance.
  • Knowledge of technical building infrastrucutre and code requeirements
  • Ability to work with the public.
  • Ability to maintain effective working relationship with agency employees.
  • Ability to maintain a professional manner at all times.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality.
  • Profecient in Microsoft Office Applications.

CERTIFICATIONS/LICENSES:

  • Must possess a valid Driver License and satisfactory driving record to use agency and/or personal automobile to travel to locations other than primary office.

SAFETY SENSITIVE JOB CLASSIFICATION:

This job is classified as a “safety-sensitive” position as defined by the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana and Patient Protection Act. Due to the “safety-sensitive” classification, an employee in this position would be subject to drug and alcohol testing, including random testing. Marijuana is one of the substances included in the drug panel screening. Possession of a medical marijuana license will not excuse you from the testing process or the consequences of testing positive for marijuana per the Family & Children’s Services Drug Free Workplace Policy, including possible revocation of a job offer or dismissal from employment.

title: Trukkikuski Föglöön, Ahvenanmaalle kalateollisuuteen, vakituinen työsuhde, AX- Föglö
description:
Haemme nyt trukkikuskia vakituiseen työsuhteeseen luonnonhelmaan Ahvenanmaan Föglön saareen (halutessasi määräaikaisuus on mahdollinen).

Työtehtäviin kuuluu trukin käyttö tuotannon ja varaston eri työvaiheissa, kuten tuotteiden siirtäminen, kuormien lastaus ja purku, sekä materiaalivirran sujuvuuden varmistaminen tuotantoalueella. Käytössä oleva trukki on vastapainoinen sähkötrukki (merkki: Linde). Työ vaatii hyvää tarkkuutta, oma-aloitteisuutta sekä kykyä toimia turvallisesti kiireisessä ympäristössä. Työskentelytilat ovat viileät, noin +2 – +6°C, joten valmius työskennellä kylmässä on tärkeää. Ajat trukkia myös hieman kaltevalla pihalla. Tarpeen mukaan voit osallistua myös muihin tuotantoa tukeviin työtehtäviin. Kalaneuvoksella pääset osaksi ammattitaitoista ja todellakin yhteen hiileen puhaltavaa "työperhettä".

Kenelle työ sopii?
Etsimme kommunikaatiotaitoista ja itsenäiseen työskentelyyn kykenevää henkilöä, joka ei pelkää tarttua toimeen. Aiempi kokemus trukin käytöstä on vaatimuksena tälle työlle. Saat toki kattavan perehdytyksen kyseiseen trukkimalliin sekä työympäristöön. Työ sopii luonnon läheiselle henkilölle, sillä työpaikka sijaitsee Föglön saarella, saaristomaisemissa. Puhuthan englantia, jotta kommunikaatio työporukassa sujuu ongelmitta.

- Työtunnit: täydet tunnit: 37,5h/vko
- Palkkaus: n. 13-14,50eur/h, kokemuksen mukaan
- Työehtosopimus: Elintarvikealan TES
- Työsuhde: Boltin kautta
- Aloitus joustavasti sopimuksen mukaan
- Roolissa on hyvä mahdollisuus edetä

Tietoa työskentelypaikkakunnasta ja käytännön järjestelyissä:
Föglössä ei ole kaupungin palveluita: saarella on K-extra, kirjasto ja kuntosali, ja muutoin kaupungin palvelut löytyvät esim. Maarianhaminasta, 35min lauttamatkan ja 30min ajomatkan päästä. Saarella pärjää myös ilman autoa, sillä työpaikka on lähellä majoitusta ja Maarianhaminaan pääsee bussilla. Halutessasi järjestämme sinulle majoituksen: majoitut tyypillisesti toisen työntekijän kanssa rivitalokaksiossa tai -kolmiossa, ja vuokra on n. 300-450eur, ja sisältää, tai ei sisällä sähköä / vettä, riippuen asunnosta (saat tarkan tiedon työtarjouksen yhteydessä).

Tietoa Kalaneuvoksesta:
Kalaneuvos on Suomen kalateollisuuden suurin toimija ja alan edelläkävijä kalanjalostuksessa, kalatukkukaupassa, kalan tuonnissa ja viennissä sekä kalankasvatuksessa. Kalaneuvos on valmistanut korkealaatuisia kalatuotteita jo yli 40 vuoden ajan panostaen tuotteiden laadun lisäksi nykyaikaisiin tuotantomenetelmiin sekä henkilöstön hyvinvointiin. Kalaneuvos-brändin alta löytyy laaja valikoima herkullisia kalatuotteita. Lisätietoja: www.kalaneuvos.fi

Haethan työpaikkaa pian: paikka täytetään heti sopivan henkilön löydyttyä.

title: Scrum Master
description:
We're looking for a Scrum Master who stays close to the team, holds a high bar for Agile practice, and can turn priorities into shipped, high-quality increments without losing momentum. You'll partner directly with a Product Owner and Delivery Manager, coach a self-organizing Agile team, and operate as a trusted voice across Exostar's delivery organization.

You will use AI tools yourself, daily, to run ceremonies, synthesize retrospectives, and keep documentation current. AI-native delivery is not optional at Exostar; it's how we work.

This role partners closely with the Product Owner, Delivery Manager, and Engineering Manager for the team(s) you serve, and operates within Exostar's Agile framework, supporting delivery teams building Exostar's identity, credentialing, and supply chain security platform for customers across the Aerospace & Defense and Life Sciences sectors.

What You'll Own

Agile Delivery Execution

  • Ensure all Scrum ceremonies (Daily Scrum, Sprint Planning, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective) are well-prepared, time-boxed, and outcomes-focused.
  • Facilitate events to uphold Scrum principles and promote transparency and team alignment.
  • Track and share delivery health metrics, including velocity, cycle time, and team health indicators, partnering with the Product Owner and Program Management for data-informed decisions.
  • Identify and remove blockers before they become delays; use a structured, time-bound escalation process for systemic issues.

AI-Native Scrum Mastery

  • Use AI assistants (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) daily to support sprint documentation, retrospective synthesis, and status reporting, not as optional productivity tools, as standard practice.
  • Champion AI-first delivery practices within the team: help the team adopt AI tools responsibly to accelerate ceremonies, documentation, and flow, consistent with Exostar's AI-First SDLC direction.
  • Apply AI tools within Agile ceremonies and delivery workflows beyond personal productivity: backlog grooming support, meeting notes, action-item tracking.
  • Stay current on responsible AI use, including data handling, safety boundaries, and disclosure, appropriate to an enterprise, regulated environment.

Stakeholder & Team Collaboration

  • Support the Product Owner in managing stakeholder interactions by helping maintain team focus and removing disruptions.
  • Coach stakeholders on Agile expectations and foster healthy collaboration boundaries.
  • Facilitate feedback loops within the Scrum Team during retrospectives and reviews to improve team dynamics and delivery processes.

Continuous Improvement & Mentoring

  • Lead retrospectives and collaborate with the Agile Coach and ACE team to assess Agile maturity and drive continuous improvement through tracked initiatives.
  • Guide development teams to higher Scrum maturity.
  • Mentor the team on Scrum values, Agile principles, and Exostar-specific processes; reinforce ownership through the Definition of Ready (DoR), Definition of Done (DoD), and Team Working Agreements.
  • Help build a productive environment where team members 'own' the product and enjoy working on it.
Qualifications: You are a great fit for this role if you:
Required
  • 7+ years of Scrum Master experience; works independently with minimal guidance, solves complex team and process problems by adapting existing practices to new situations, and is comfortable representing status, risks, and issues directly to management and stakeholders.
  • Hands-on daily user of AI assistants (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot); you use these yourself to run your own workflow, not just advocate for them.
  • Excellent knowledge of Scrum techniques and artifacts (Definition of Done, user stories, automated testing, backlog refinement).
  • Applies the INVEST model and supports vertical slicing and story sizing.
  • Skilled in facilitation techniques such as Planning Poker, Dot Voting, and Story Mapping.
  • Good knowledge of other Agile frameworks.
  • Excellent communication and servant-leadership skills.
  • Problem-solving and conflict-resolution ability.
  • Outstanding organizational skills.
  • Scrum Master certification is a must.

Preferred Qualifications

You are exactly who we are looking for if you:

  • Have experience leading or supporting a team through AI-adoption change management, distinct from personal AI tool use.
  • Are familiar with software development and Jira/Confluence-based delivery tracking.
  • Hold a degree in Computer Science, Business, or a similar field.
  • Have experience operating in a regulated environment (FedRAMP, CMMC, HIPAA, or equivalent), understanding how compliance requirements land in delivery cadence.

Why Exostar

  • AI-native delivery org: AI assistants are standard, not experiments; leadership actively backs and uses them.
  • Real compliance stakes: supporting FedRAMP Moderate and CMMC-aligned delivery for the Defense Industrial Base.
  • Mission-driven: securing collaboration infrastructure for Aerospace & Defense and Life Sciences.
  • We believe in employee development: internal promotion pathways, training, and educational assistance.

About Exostar

Exostar's cloud-based platforms create exclusive communities within the Aerospace and Defense, Life Sciences, and other highly regulated industries where members securely collaborate, share information, and operate compliantly. Within these communities we build trust. By analyzing community data, we provide insights and intelligence enabling organizations to make better, timelier decisions, mitigate risk, and operate more efficiently.

Exostar is an Equal Opportunity Employment Employer. The company provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital status, disability status or genetic information. Exostar is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all persons in all facets of employment including recruiting, hiring, compensation, promotion, training, benefits, transfers and working conditions.

title: Service Coordinator
description:
SUMMARY OF RESPONSIBILITIES

The Service Coordinator plays a key role in supporting service operations, serving as the central administrative link between residents, service teams, and vendors. This role is responsible for scheduling, work order management, vendor coordination, and resident communication to ensure timely and efficient service request completion.

The Service Coordinator works under the direction of the Service Manager and collaborates with Lead Technicians, ensuring that work orders are triaged correctly, residents receive timely updates, and vendors complete services efficiently. This position requires high energy, strong organizational skills, and the ability to handle a large volume of calls and system updates while maintaining excellent resident service.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES

  • Coordinate and manage service requests by accurately entering, scheduling, updating, and closing work orders, while assigning technicians and vendors for efficient routing and timely service.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for residents, managing service requests, scheduling, and follow-ups via phone, email, and resident tickets.
  • Respond to and manage resident service tickets, addressing resident inquiries, escalating urgent issues, and ensuring timely follow-ups.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with service teams and property operations to ensure a seamless resident experience and timely issue resolution.
  • Communicate with vendors and service teams, confirming work order assignments, verifying work completion, and resolving scheduling conflicts.
  • Monitor work order progress and follow up on outstanding service requests, escalating as needed to the Service Manager or Lead Technician.
  • Use Power BI and other reporting tools to track service trends, assess response times, and provide insights on operational needs.
  • Identify scheduling gaps, delays, or inefficiencies, bringing them to the attention of the Service Manager and/or Lead Technician.
  • Maintain accurate records in work order systems, ensuring compliance with company policies and reporting requirements.
  • Support the Service Manager and Lead Technicians with data entry, performance tracking, and service-related administrative tasks as needed.

Additional duties may be assigned as needed.

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Office-based role with a focus on high-volume resident communication and work order coordination.
  • Frequent phone, email, and system interactions, requiring strong communication and multitasking skills.
  • Extended periods of computer use, including data entry, scheduling, and reporting tasks.
  • Cross-functional collaboration with service teams, vendors, and internal teams to ensure resident and district needs are met.
  • Standard business hours, with occasional evening or weekend support as needed based on resident or operational demands.

REQUIRED EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • 1+ years of experience in an administrative, customer service, or operations support role.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
  • Experience managing work orders, scheduling, and coordinating service tasks.
  • Exposure to data tracking and reporting tools (Power BI preferred) for monitoring service trends and operational insights.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interact professionally with residents, service teams, and vendors.

PREFERRED EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • Experience in property management, real estate, or service operations.
  • Familiarity with work order and customer service management systems.
  • Bilingual in Spanish (reading & writing) preferred.
  • Knowledge of basic service and repair terminology (e.g., HVAC, plumbing, electrical).
  • Experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with high-volume resident or customer interactions.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE

  • Service Operations Support – Understanding of work order processes, scheduling, and vendor coordination.
  • Customer Service – Knowledge of resident needs, service expectations, and issue resolution best practices.
  • Data Tracking & Reporting – Exposure to analyzing service trends, response times, and work order efficiency using tools like Power BI.
  • Work Order & Service Systems – Familiarity with platforms for managing service requests and resident interactions.
  • Administrative & Clerical – Knowledge of data entry, record-keeping, scheduling, and workflow coordination.

REQUIRED SKILLS

  • High-Volume Communication – Ability to handle a large number of calls, emails, and resident inquiries professionally and efficiently.
  • Time Management – Strong ability to prioritize multiple service requests, administrative tasks, and scheduling in a fast-paced environment.
  • Data Analysis & Reporting – Basic proficiency in Power BI or similar reporting tools to track service trends and operational performance.
  • Attention to Detail – Ensures accurate data entry, scheduling, and tracking of work orders and service requests.
  • Problem-Solving – Quickly identifies service delays or issues and escalates them appropriately.
  • Vendor & Technician Coordination – Ability to schedule, track, and follow up on service tasks with efficiency.
  • Resident-Focused Approach – Committed to delivering excellent resident service and satisfaction.
  • Technical Proficiency – Familiarity with service management platforms such as Yardi, Facilgo, customer service software, or similar systems.
  • Collaboration & Teamwork – Works effectively with service teams, vendors, and internal stakeholders to ensure smooth service operations.

WORK STYLES & BEHAVIORS

  • Highly Organized – Ability to manage multiple priorities, keep detailed records, and ensure timely follow-ups.
  • Resident-Focused – Committed to delivering excellent resident service and a seamless resident experience.
  • Proactive & Detail-Oriented – Identifies service gaps, inefficiencies, or escalations and ensures timely resolution.
  • Dependable & Reliable – Follows through on assigned tasks with accuracy and consistency.
  • Tech-Savvy & Data-Driven – Comfortable using digital tools, reporting systems (Power BI), and work order platforms.
  • Strong Communication Skills – Able to interact effectively with residents, service teams, vendors, and internal teams.
  • Collaborative & Team-Oriented – Works cross-functionally to support service operations and resident needs.
  • High Energy & Drive – Thrives in a fast-paced, high-contact role with frequent calls, scheduling, and system interactions.
  • Adaptable & Resilient – Remains flexible and responsive in a dynamic work environment.

title: Clinical Supervisor - OKC/Norman Area
description:
OKC/Norman Area - The Clinical Supervisor will work in partnership with others as part of a structured inter-disciplinary team to provide clinical supervision. The Clinical Supervisor position is responsible for ensuring quality service and high professional standards by monitoring client welfare and clinical outcomes; transmitting knowledge, attitude and skills, enhancing & promoting professional development of the supervisee & evaluating the ethical, professional, and therapeutic competence of supervisee.

POSITION SPECIFIC DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Demonstrate advanced clinical skills and knowledge in CCBHC standards, treatment models, and culturally appropriate interventions for individuals with severe mental illness, co-occurring disorders, and trauma.
  • Oversee and coordinate clinical staff performance, service provision, and multidisciplinary teamwork to ensure fidelity to the CCBHC model.
  • Lead staff meetings, assign work, and collaborate with psychiatric, primary care, and other programs to support client needs.
  • Implement evidence-based practices, promote clinical competence, and maintain personal professional development.
  • Provide clinical supervision, case consultation, and crisis intervention; ensure integrated team-based care and quality outcomes.
  • Develop individualized supervision plans, offer immediate support in complex situations, and foster continuous learning and leadership among staff.
  • Ensure staff training in assessment, engagement, documentation, and treatment models; identify learning needs and provide constructive feedback.
  • Manage recruitment, orientation, scheduling, and performance evaluations; address performance issues promptly and maintain compliance with agency policies.
  • Monitor treatment progress, conduct utilization reviews, and implement quality improvement initiatives using data-driven decisions.
  • Collaborate with the Program Director on strategic planning, policy implementation, compliance, and reporting; assume administrative responsibilities when needed.
  • Provide clinical oversight to ensure service intensity aligns with client risk levels; adjust schedules for maximum utilization and manage crisis situations.

QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION:

  • A Master's degree in Social Work or its equivalent from an accredited school.

EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum 3-5 years’ clinical experience as a licensed professional.
  • Supervisory and program management experience preferred.

PERFORMANCE COMPETENCIES:

  • Communication
  • Decision Making
  • Engagement
  • Initiative and Accountability
  • Interpersonal
  • Learning
  • Organizational Alignment
  • Quality of Work

KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES:

  • Adaptability: The ability to adjust to changing priorities, unexpected situations, and new challenges while remaining productive and effective.
  • Interpersonal Skills: The ability to establish and maintain professional relationships with clients, families, caregivers, colleagues, and community partners.
  • Initiative: The ability to work independently with limited supervision and produce results in a timely, accurate and meaningful manner.
  • Cooperation: The ability to work effectively with others is important for successful multidisciplinary teamwork. This includes the ability to work cooperatively, to contribute positively to group dynamics, and to share knowledge and resources.
  • Multitasking: The ability to efficiently and effectively manage multiple tasks, projects, and responsibilities concurrently. This includes juggling multiple demands simultaneously and being skilled at adapting to changing priorities in a fast-paced work environment.
  • Clinical Judgment: The capacity to make sound clinical judgments and adapt therapeutic approaches as needed based on clients' progress and changing needs.
  • Leadership: The ability to provide direction, set a vision, and motivate others to work collaboratively toward common goals. Leadership requires the ability to inspire trust foster a positive work culture, and guide others to reach their full potential
  • Decisiveness: The ability to make timely decisions, even when face with incomplete information or under pressure, while maintaining a commitment to sound clinical judgment.

CERTIFICATIONS/LICENSES:

  • Must be licensed as an LCSW, LPC, LMFT, LADC or other mental health professional
  • Must possess a valid Driver License and satisfactory driving record to use agency and/or personal automobile to travel to locations other than primary office and/or for the transportation of clients.

SAFETY SENSITIVE JOB CLASSIFICATION:

This job is classified as a “safety-sensitive” position as defined by the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana and Patient Protection Act. Due to the “safety-sensitive” classification, an employee in this position would be subject to drug and alcohol testing, including random testing. Marijuana is one of the substances included in the drug panel screening. Possession of a medical marijuana license will not excuse you from the testing process or the consequences of testing positive for marijuana per the Family & Children’s Services Drug Free Workplace Policy, including possible revocation of a job offer or dismissal from employment.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

May be required to work evening hours, weekends, and/or holidays.

Family & Children’s Services, Oklahoma’s leading community mental health center, has an opportunity for an energetic and caring Therapist/Counselor to work with Child Abuse and Trauma Services (CATS).

CATS Therapists provide trauma informed, evidenced-based practice interventions to children age 0-18 and their families who have experienced abuse, neglect, unplanned separation or other traumas. Family & Children’s Services works to heal hurting and abused children, strengthen families, and provide hope and a path to recovery for those battling mental illness and addiction. With nine citywide locations F&CS serves 1 in 6 Tulsans with a broad range of mental health programs and services.

CCBHC Model of Care

Family & Children’s Services works to heal hurting and abused children, strengthen families, and provide hope and a path to recovery for those battling mental illness and addiction. You will be working in an innovative and dynamic environment using a new transformative model of care Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC). title: Web Designer
description:
About You

You are a visually driven Web Designer who enjoys transforming product requirements, user needs, and brand direction into polished, engaging digital experiences. You have a strong eye for visual hierarchy, typography, composition, spacing, and detail, while understanding how your design decisions translate across responsive products and different digital touchpoints.

You are comfortable taking ideas from early visual exploration through high-fidelity, development-ready designs, working within established design systems and brand standards. You collaborate effectively with product, UX, and engineering teams, bring consistency to complex digital experiences, and maintain a high bar for visual quality, usability, and execution.

You Bring to Applaudo the Following Competencies

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Graphic Design, Web Design, Visual Communication, Interaction Design, or a related field is desired, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 4+ years of professional experience in web, visual, UI, or digital experience design.

  • Strong understanding of visual hierarchy, typography, color, composition, spacing, and layout.
  • Experience designing responsive experiences for web, mobile, and different screen sizes.

  • Experience working with design systems and reusable component libraries.
  • Understanding of usability and accessibility best practices.
  • Experience collaborating with Designers, Product Managers, Developers, and business stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain consistency across complex digital experiences.

You Will Be Accountable for the Following Responsibilities

  • Design visually polished and intuitive experiences for web, mobile, and kiosk platforms.
  • Translate business requirements, product direction, and user needs into engaging interface designs.
  • Develop concepts from initial visual exploration through high-fidelity mockups and interactive prototypes.
  • Apply brand standards and established design-system components consistently across digital products.
  • Create responsive layouts for multiple devices, screen sizes, and interaction models.
  • Collaborate with Product, UX, Engineering, and business stakeholders to refine requirements and design solutions.
  • Prepare design specifications, assets, interaction guidance, and documentation for development teams.
  • Participate in design critiques and incorporate feedback while maintaining a strong visual perspective.
  • Review implemented experiences and address inconsistencies between approved designs and the final product.
  • Support multiple teams and initiatives while managing priorities, deadlines, and feedback effectively.

  • 4+ years of Web, Visual, UI, or Digital Experience Design.
  • Strong portfolio showcasing polished responsive web and mobile interfaces.
  • Advanced hands-on proficiency with Figma.
  • Strong visual design fundamentals and responsive design experience.
  • Experience with design systems and development-ready design handoffs.
  • Advanced English proficiency.

About Us

We Are Engineered Different.

At Applaudo, talented people design, build, and scale meaningful, AI-powered solutions that create real business impact. As an AI-native organization, we collaborate across design, development, cloud, data, and artificial intelligence to turn ideas into scalable products that transform how companies operate, make decisions, and grow.

We are building a high-performance culture grounded in five values: Empowering Excellence, Collaborative Teamwork, Unsolicited Respect, Consistent Transparency, and Efficient Communication. These define how we work, how we support one another, and how we hold ourselves accountable.

Applaudo is a place for people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and work alongside strong teams they are proud to belong to. Joining us means being part of an organization that is evolving intentionally, investing in modern ways of working, and leading AI-native transformation at scale.

title: OCM / Training Lead – Japanese Speaking
description:
This is a full-time assignment supporting the program from the Explore phase through deployment and hypercare. The role requires substantial onsite presence at Japan-based sites, including support across multiple shifts during training delivery, cutover, and hypercare.

The OCM / Training Lead will work closely with the Program Manager, workstream leads, plant management, local HR, and training and communications teams.

Duration: 12 Months
Location: Remote
Travel Requirement: Requires 2–3 weeks of onsite travel to Japan per quarter
Work Authorization: U.S. Citizens only

Top Skills Required

  1. Shop-Floor Change Management – Experience supporting paperless transformation initiatives and transitioning operators, inspectors, planners, and technicians from paper, Excel, and legacy tools to real-time, system-driven processes.

  2. Multi-Language & Multi-Shift Training – Experience designing and delivering training programs across multiple manufacturing plants, shifts, and languages, including Japanese-speaking workforces.

  3. Knowledge Capture – Strong experience documenting critical business processes, logic, and institutional knowledge currently maintained in spreadsheets or held by key individuals.

  4. Adoption Measurement & Reinforcement – Experience defining adoption metrics, measuring user adoption through hypercare, and driving corrective actions to ensure successful implementation.

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Organizational Change Management (OCM) and Training Lead to support a large-scale manufacturing transformation program.

The program involves transitioning manufacturing operations from paper-based processes, Excel spreadsheets, and legacy tools to standardized, real-time, paperless SAP processes across multiple plants and business divisions.

The primary focus of this role will be managing the people side of transformation, including stakeholder engagement, communications, business readiness, role-based training, knowledge capture, and adoption measurement.

The successful candidate will support manufacturing personnel working across multiple shifts and sites and will play a critical role in ensuring successful adoption of new business processes and SAP technologies.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own and lead the overall change management and training strategy across multiple workstreams, plants, and business functions.

  • Conduct change impact assessments by role, business division, and plant location.

  • Identify how new processes and systems will impact operators, inspectors, planners, warehouse personnel, maintenance technicians, controllers, and other end users.

  • Develop and execute stakeholder engagement and communication plans for executives, plant management, supervisors, and shop-floor employees.

  • Design and deliver role-based training programs, including:

    • Training curriculum

    • Hands-on system training

    • Work instructions

    • Quick-reference guides

    • Shop-floor dashboards

    • Quality inspection processes

    • Handheld terminal transactions

    • Planning processes

    • Maintenance execution

    • Costing processes

  • Lead the language strategy for end-user training content, with Japanese as a primary shop-floor language and support for additional languages as required.

  • Coordinate translation, terminology consistency, content review, and multilingual training materials.

  • Lead structured knowledge capture from key business users and SMEs.

  • Document critical business logic related to lot numbering, allocation, planning, inspection, and other undocumented business processes.

  • Establish and support a super-user/key-user network across plants and shifts.

  • Define business readiness criteria and conduct readiness assessments to support go/no-go decisions.

  • Define role-based adoption metrics and monitor adoption throughout hypercare.

  • Drive corrective actions where adoption data indicates that new processes or systems are not being effectively adopted.

  • Support the transition away from legacy tools and address workaround behaviors.

Batch Management & Traceability Experience – Preferred

Batch Management and traceability experience is preferred but not required.

This is primarily a change management and training role; however, understanding lot and batch processes will help the candidate develop more effective training and adoption strategies.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in Organizational Change Management and end-user training for enterprise system implementations.

  • Experience supporting at least 3 full-lifecycle ERP implementations, including at least 1 SAP implementation.

  • Demonstrated experience delivering change management and training to manufacturing shop-floor populations, including operators, inspectors, and technicians.

  • Strong experience designing and delivering role-based training curricula.

  • Experience developing:

    • Hands-on system training

    • Work instructions

    • Quick-reference guides

    • End-user training materials

  • Experience supporting users with varying levels of technical and system proficiency.

  • Experience managing training and enablement across multiple shifts and multiple manufacturing locations.

  • Strong understanding of structured change management methodologies such as Prosci/ADKAR, Kotter, or equivalent.

  • Experience conducting business readiness assessments and defining go/no-go criteria.

  • Experience defining and measuring adoption metrics beyond training completion rates.

  • Experience establishing and supporting sustainable super-user/key-user networks.

  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

  • Ability to effectively communicate with both executive stakeholders and shop-floor employees.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Business-level bilingual proficiency in English and Japanese.

  • Previous experience supporting change management initiatives in Japan or with Japanese manufacturing organizations.

  • Familiarity with Japanese workplace culture, consensus-building practices, and shop-floor communication norms.

  • Experience delivering multilingual training programs for multinational manufacturing workforces.

  • Experience managing translation quality and terminology governance.

  • Experience supporting the retirement of legacy tools and addressing user workaround behaviors.

  • Familiarity with SAP Digital Manufacturing, operator dashboards, SAP Fiori, and handheld terminal interfaces.

  • Experience with digital adoption platforms, in-application guidance tools, or SAP Enable Now.

  • Formal change management certification such as Prosci or equivalent.

Preferred knowledge includes:

  • Lot creation, splitting, merging, and identification processes.

  • Transitioning lot and batch processes from paper and legacy tools into SAP.

  • Batch status management and quality usage decisions.

  • Changes to operator, inspector, and warehouse workflows resulting from digital batch management.

  • Understanding the impact of lot and batch design on training timelines and content stabilization.

Highlights

LeadOCM and training for a SAP manufacturing transformation. Japaneselanguage skills preferred. Experience with shop-floor training, multi-shift delivery, adoption, and ERP/SAPimplementations required

description:
Senior All-Source Intelligence Analyst

At Celestar, a B&A Company, we foster and embrace a distinct set of values that we live by and instill in all aspects of our organization: dedication, commitment, partnership, trust, and recognition. We have incorporated these values into successful delivery for our customers since 1988. B&A believes in ensuring its employees feel deeply connected to B&A, recognizing successes and hard work, and providing continuous opportunities to learn and grow. Our people are entrepreneurial thinkers who combine mindset, vision, and experience to drive value – not only to us as an organization, but to the clients we support. We promote a collaborative culture with our clients and with each other as one team working towards a common vision. We’d love for you to join our team!

Job Summary

B&A is looking for a Senior All-Source Intelligence Analyst to join us at the National Guard Bureau in support of an important mission. In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with a great team while supporting…

Responsibilities

  • Conduct all-source intelligence analysis using classified, unclassified, publicly available, and geospatial information to assess, interpret, forecast, and report on national security issues, natural and man-made hazards, and other events impacting National Guard personnel, property, equipment, and operations.
  • Monitor NGB J2 Priority Intelligence Requirements (PIRs), Chief’s Critical Information Requirements (CCIRs), and Requests for Information/Assistance (RFI/RFAs), ensuring applicable requests are addressed within established timelines and status updates are provided to NGB J2 leadership.
  • Develop, review, brief, and publish classified and unclassified intelligence products, including Incident Awareness and Assessment (IAA), Homeland Defense/Security, Medical Intelligence, Cyber Intelligence, Information Operations, and Critical Infrastructure assessments, in accordance with DNI Analytic Tradecraft Standards.
  • Support all-hazard and contingency operations by coordinating with federal agencies, interagency partners, Joint Force Headquarters-State (JFHQ-State), and other National Guard stakeholders to identify intelligence requirements, assess federal IAA capabilities, and provide analytical and collection support.
  • Brief National Guard senior leaders and provide recurring intelligence reporting, including analytical products, Executive Summaries (EXSUMs), situational updates, and other products required by operational battle rhythms.
  • Deploy in support of contingency or emergency operations when required, including the ability to deploy within four hours of notification and support operations that may last 14 days or longer at locations throughout the United States.
  • Maintain the flexibility to support 24/7 operations, extended shifts of 12 hours or more, alternate work locations, and changing operational requirements, while also maintaining and updating NGB J2 IAA continuity procedures, SOPs, checklists, contact rosters, and related operational documentation.

Education and Experience

  • Master’s Degree in an area related to the labor category from a college or university accredited by an agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education, and twelve (12) years of experience.
  • OR Bachelor's Degree related to the labor category from a college or university accredited by an agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education and an additional five (5) years of related senior experience, for a total of seventeen (17) years, in lieu of a Master's Degree.

Required Skills

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • In-depth knowledge and understanding of the labor category activities required to meet mission requirements.
  • Mastery of qualitative and quantitative analytic methodologies and pursuing developments in academia or other fields that affect tradecraft methodology.
  • Ability to define comprehensive, new, or unique research approaches that enable rigorous assessments to address and contribute to high-level tasks.
  • In-depth analysis of analytic operations and knowledge management issues across organizational and intra-IC boundaries, and clearly articulates key findings.

title: Security Engineering Lead
description:
Espresso Systems builds foundational infrastructure to power tomorrow’s internet, where digital assets are able to move across chains as easily as info flows across the web. It’s the lead developer of the Espresso Network, the first base layer built from the ground up to provide rollups with the functionality they’ve always needed but never had: fast, secure finality for users’ transactions and seamless composability with other rollups.
Rollups today rely on infrastructure that wasn’t built with them in mind, resulting in their isolation and the fragmentation of users, developers and liquidity within the Ethereum ecosystem. This prevents rollups from achieving the seamless composability that’s essential to web3's vision. Espresso solves this by providing rollups with secure, real-time visibility into what’s happening on all integrated chains, including their own, empowering the apps to execute crosschain interactions immediately without waiting for slow settlement or trusting centralized sequencers.
The Espresso Network is currently live on mainnet in its initial release. In addition to fast confirmations and data availability, rollups seeking further decentralization can also opt to use the Espresso Network as a decentralized sequencer. As the first purpose-built base layer for rollups, Espresso supports a fast-growing ecosystem of interconnected chains regardless of tech stack, VM, or settlement layer—from established chains like Celo and ApeChain to emerging app-specific chains attracting their first users.
At Espresso Systems, we work with leading teams developing rollups and innovating around interoperability, including Offchain Labs, Polygon, Caldera, AltLayer, Cartesi, Across, Hyperlane, and beyond—all united in our mission to build a unified, composable ecosystem where rollups are free to achieve their full potential regardless of where they choose to settle.
The Espresso team comprises a diverse and passionate group of contributors from around the world. We are developers, designers, and researchers who have contributed in academia, open-source communities, policymaking, and beyond. We have raised roughly $60 million from leading investors in technology and crypto, including a16z, Greylock Partners, Electric Capital, Sequoia Capital, and Polychain Capital.
As a Security Engineering Lead on our team, you'll be leading the security and auditing efforts for Espresso's codebase leading up to, and beyond, launch. We are looking for an experienced security engineering and software auditing professional who can lead review processes of our design and codebase. Experience in the domains of EVM smart contracts and/or Rust distributed systems is preferred for this role.

Responsibilities

  • Lead security audits of (a subset of) the Espresso codebase
  • As a project leader, you will have mobility in how you choose to organize security and audit efforts
  • Dive into the code of a fairly complex distributed system, learning and developing an understanding of the system on the fly (with help from the engineering team that built it, of course)
  • Coordinate with several engineering teams to aid in your audit, raise concerns and communicate results, and guide the effort to harden the system based on your findings
  • Coordinate with, manage, and review the work of external security auditing teams, in certain cases
  • Suggest improvements to testing and engineering practices to promote more secure and maintainable code

Requirements

  • Solid grasp of software engineering principles, both low-level (e.g. language-specific best practices) and high-level (e.g. reliable software architecture, particularly in distributed systems)
  • If focused on Rust: ≥ 1 year experience writing Rust, particularly with async Rust.
  • If focused on Solidity: Multiple years experience writing smart contracts; experience with smart contract security audits or formal verification of smart contracts
  • Experience as an engineer or software architect in a security-critical industry
  • Be capable of describing the stakes, the challenges you've faced in building secure software, and the steps/processes you've taken to mitigate risk
  • Experience as an auditor, pentester, QA tester, etc.
  • Have a well thought-out approach to testing software and designing it to be testable/auditable
  • Ability to think adversarially, and identify potential reliability or security vulnerabilities even in software that is correct in common or “happy path” scenarios
  • Experience on the design and/or testing of distributed systems
  • Comfort diving into unknowns and asking questions

Preferred

  • Knowledge of relevant testing and static analysis tools (e.g. Foundry, Slither) is a plus
  • Blockchain knowledge/experience is preferred, but could also be include IoT, automotive, finance, etc.
  • Ideally, the candidate should have a general philosophy of software design that has been molded by experience working on security-critical systems

Benefits

  • Fully remote with flexible hours
  • Work alongside the brightest minds in the crypto space
  • Competitive salary + equity package
  • Regular team off-sites to international locations
  • Unlimited vacation policy
  • Top-tier health, dental, and vision coverage for US employees

title: Finance Coordinator
description:
FLSA Status: Full-time, Non-Exempt

Location: Sacramento, CA (On-Site Position – Not Remote)

Compensation: $25.00-$31.00 per hour

Post Date: September 2, 2026

Close Date: September 30, 2026

Report to: Sr. Director of Finance


To apply for this position: Please submit a resume and cover letter. Your resume will not be considered if a cover letter is not included.


About Community HealthWorks

Community HealthWorks (CoHeWo) advances health equity by helping individuals and families access the health coverage, care, and community services they need to thrive. We work at the intersection of healthcare and community support, partnering with managed care plans, health systems, community-based organizations, and government agencies to remove barriers to care.


Strong financial operations make this work possible. The Finance team helps ensure that organizational and program resources are accurately tracked, appropriately documented, and available to support the services our teams provide.

Position Summary


The Finance Coordinator supports the day-to-day financial operations of Community HealthWorks. Working under the supervision of the Director of Finance, the Coordinator assists with accounts payable, transaction entry, reconciliations, financial

documentation, revenue and contract tracking, invoicing, reporting, audit preparation, and other routine finance activities.


The role also coordinates check and payment requests connected to program needs. Current examples include housing deposits, housing assistance, flexible funding, and other approved housing-related or client-support expenses. These requests may come from CoHeWo program teams or external partners operating under agreements with CoHeWo. The Finance Coordinator helps make sure required documentation, approvals, and supporting information are complete before a check or payment is prepared for sign-off.


This is an in-person, non-supervisory role based at Community HealthWorks’ Sacramento office. It is well suited for someone who enjoys detailed work, organized processes, accurate records, and following a request through completion.


What This Work Looks Like


This role combines routine bookkeeping and financial administration with frequent coordination across the organization. Part of the day may involve entering transactions into QuickBooks, reviewing invoices, reconciling debit card activity, updating Excel tracking tools, organizing financial records, or preparing documentation for reports and audits.


Another part of the day may involve reviewing a check request from a program team or partner. Before the payment can move forward, the Finance Coordinator may need to confirm that the request includes the required supporting documents, approval, payment information, and other documentation required by the applicable process or funding source. When something is missing or does not match, the Finance Coordinator follows up with the appropriate person and helps keep the request moving.


Some work is predictable and recurring. Other requests may be time-sensitive, particularly when a payment is connected to a housing or other immediate program need. The Finance Coordinator must be able to respond with appropriate urgency while still following financial controls and documentation requirements.


A Day in the Life


You may begin your day by reviewing invoices, payment requests, messages, and upcoming deadlines. You might enter vendor invoices or debit card transactions into QuickBooks, reconcile activity against receipts and approvals, or update a revenue or contract-tracking worksheet.


Later, a program team may submit a request for a housing deposit or another approved program expense. You would review the request for required documentation and approvals, follow up if something is missing, and prepare the payment materials once the request is complete. You may also communicate with an external partner about documentation needed for a payment under an existing agreement.


The rest of the day might include preparing a bank deposit, organizing finance records, assisting with a funder invoice, gathering documents for an audit or report, or resolving a discrepancy with a vendor or coworker.


No two days will look exactly the same, but accuracy, documentation, follow-through, confidentiality, and timely communication are always part of the work.


What You’ll Do


Accounts payable, bookkeeping, and reconciliation

  • Enter debit card transactions, vendor invoices, and other financial information into QuickBooks.
  • Review vendor invoices for accuracy and confirm that required supporting documentation and approvals are in place.
  • Match invoices to applicable packing or delivery documentation, approval records, or other supporting materials.
  • Prepare debit card reconciliations and compile receipts and other supporting documentation in the required format.
  • Communicate with vendors and coworkers to resolve discrepancies, missing information, or other payment issues.
  • Prepare bank deposits and maintain related financial records.
  • Assist with annual 1099 preparation for applicable vendors and consultants.

Program, housing, and partner payment coordination

  • Coordinate check and payment requests for approved program needs, including housing deposits, housing assistance, flexible funding, and other housing-related or client-support expenses.
  • Review requests to confirm that required documentation, approvals, payment information, and supporting records are complete before checks or payments are prepared for sign-off.
  • Coordinate with CoHeWo program teams and external partners operating under agreements with CoHeWo when additional documentation or clarification is needed.
  • Maintain organized records of payment requests and supporting documentation in accordance with applicable finance, contract, program, and organizational requirements.
  • Balance timely processing with the need to follow established financial controls and approval processes.

Financial tracking, reporting, and records

  • Maintain revenue worksheets, contract records, and other financial tracking tools.
  • Assist with invoices to funders, donors, and other applicable parties.
  • Assist with preparation of monthly and quarterly financial reports.
  • Support annual audit preparation by gathering, organizing, and maintaining requested documentation.
  • Organize electronic finance, vendor, funding contract, and related records so information can be located when needed.
  • Maintain required paper records when applicable.
  • Assist with the development and maintenance of fiscal and financial policies, procedures, and workflows.
  • Perform other related duties as organizational and program needs evolve.

What Success Looks Like


Success in this role is not only about completing transactions. It is about making sure financial activity is accurate, supported, organized, and able to move through the appropriate process. Success includes:

  • Entering and maintaining financial information accurately and consistently.
  • Recognizing when an invoice, payment request, approval, or supporting document is incomplete or does not match.
  • Following up promptly and professionally when additional information is needed.
  • Keeping clear and organized records so transactions can be understood, reviewed, and supported later.
  • Managing recurring responsibilities and deadlines without losing track of time-sensitive requests.
  • Protecting confidential financial, client-related, vendor, and organizational information.
  • Knowing when to resolve an issue independently and when to ask the Director of Finance or another appropriate person for guidance.
  • Supporting program needs with responsiveness while maintaining required financial controls and documentation.

What Can Be Challenging About This Work


Finance work is detail-oriented and often deadline-driven. Some responsibilities are repetitive by design because accuracy, consistency, and documentation matter. There may be periods, particularly around month-end, reporting deadlines, audits, or increased program activity, when several requests need attention at the same time.


The Coordinator often depends on other people to provide complete documentation or approvals. A payment may be important to a program team or time-sensitive for a housing need, but Finance may not be able to move it forward until required information is complete. The role requires being responsive and helpful while also maintaining appropriate financial controls and being comfortable following up when something is missing.


Errors can affect reporting, vendor relationships, program operations, or the timing of a payment. The work therefore requires sustained attention to detail, sound judgment, and a willingness to slow down and verify information when something does not look right.


How CoHeWo Supports You


Employees are expected to ask questions and are not expected to learn Community HealthWorks’ financial processes, contracts, or program payment requirements alone. Support for this role includes:

  • Onboarding and training on CoHeWo finance processes, documentation standards, and approval workflows.
  • Guidance on QuickBooks, financial tracking tools, and organizational systems used in the role.
  • Regular supervision and access to the Director of Finance for questions, review, and problem-solving.
