title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
A B O U T B A N N E R S O L U T I O N S

Banner Solutions is a premier national wholesale distributor specializing in commercial door hardware, access control systems, and security hardware products across CSI Divisions 8, 10, and 28. As a leader in the commercial door and security hardware industry, we represent more than 260 manufacturers and deliver industry-leading service with a 98%+ same-day ship rate.

Our customers include Contract Hardware Dealers, Glass & Glazing Dealers, Building Material Suppliers, Electronic Access Integrators, Locksmiths, Institutional End Users, e-tailers, and retailers nationwide. Through our nationwide distribution network, deep product expertise, and strong manufacturer partnerships, we help customers secure and complete buildings across the country.

Banner Solutions is built on a culture of ownership, collaboration, and accountability. Our team members are empowered to make an impact while delivering the expertise, service, and reliability our customers depend on.

C O R E R E S P O N S I B I L I T I E S

The Senior Software Engineer — .NET / Integration / Automation will serve as a hands-on technical contributor within Banner Solutions' Chief Digital Officer organization, working directly with the Systems Architect to build and maintain the integrations, automation workflows, and AI-powered systems that run Banner's operations.

Reporting directly to the Systems Architect, this role is part of the CDO organization and operates across multiple platforms and business functions. The Senior Software Engineer will take architectural direction and independently carry substantial features or integrations through to completion.

This is not a ticket-driven role. The ideal candidate takes a well-framed problem, asks the right questions, makes the technical decisions that are theirs to make, and delivers working software — pulling the Systems Architect back in at the decision points that actually matter.

Integration & Systems Development

  • Build and maintain integration workflows connecting core platforms including P21 (ERP), Salesforce, Akeneo (PIM), Algolia, and Canals.ai — "make these three systems work together reliably" is a common problem here
  • Design and implement APIs, background jobs, and automation pipelines that handle real transactional volume reliably
  • Debug across system boundaries — trace problems through multiple systems rather than stopping at the code immediately in front of you
  • Ensure integrations perform well, fail gracefully, and are maintainable by the team over time
  • Write code with good testing instincts: how do we prove this works, what happens when it fails, and what edge cases are we missing?

AI-Augmented Development

  • Build integrations against LLM APIs — OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar — to power Banner's automation initiatives in areas including order processing, customer communications, and purchasing operations
  • Apply AI development tools fluently as part of daily work: to move faster, explore approaches, and think more thoroughly — while applying independent engineering judgment to what the tools produce
  • Contribute to automation workflows that reduce manual labor and improve operational consistency across Banner's distribution business

Technical Ownership & Judgment

  • Receive architectural direction from the Systems Architect and independently drive significant features or integrations through to completion
  • When something unexpected surfaces: investigate it, determine root cause, make the call if it's yours to make, and bring a clear recommendation back if it's architectural or business-related
  • Make normal technical decisions without asking permission — and recognize when a decision has crossed into territory that needs a conversation
  • Take business problems that aren't perfectly specified and turn them into working software, asking the questions that matter rather than waiting for a complete ticket

Q U A L I F I C A T I O N S

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent professional experience
  • 5+ years of professional software development in a production environment
  • Experience within distribution, supply chain, e-commerce, or similarly complex operational environments preferred
  • Strong C#/.NET — this is the core of what Banner builds
  • Solid SQL — read stored procedures, write good queries, and recognize performance problems at scale
  • Comfortable with Azure and cloud environments — Banner is actively moving workloads to the cloud
  • API design, background services, and multi-system integration development
  • Able to debug across system boundaries, not just the code immediately in front of you
  • Good testing instincts for real-world edge cases and failure modes
  • Already using AI development tools effectively as a genuine part of daily work

Preferred

  • Hands-on experience integrating against LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar) — rate limits, error handling, cost management, and applying them to real business problems rather than just experimentation
  • Experience with Epicor Prophet21 (P21) or a similarly complex distribution/wholesale ERP
  • Familiarity with Akeneo, Algolia, Salesforce, Canals.ai, or similar platforms
  • Experience building AI or automation workflows — document processing, workflow orchestration, or intelligent routing
  • EDI or supply chain integration experience

We'd rather hire a strong engineer who can learn our systems than narrow the pool for someone who happens to already know our exact stack.

Cultural Fit & Attributes

  • When something breaks: investigate it, prove what's happening, propose a fix that preserves intended behavior, and escalate only if it's architectural or business-related — not every problem needs to come back up
  • Takes well-framed problems, asks useful questions, and delivers working software rather than waiting for a complete specification
  • Comfortable making technical decisions independently, and calibrated about when a decision has crossed into territory that needs a conversation
  • Embody Banner Solutions' values ofCourtesy, Respect, Quality, Professionalism, and Discipline
  • Genuinely collaborative — works well with the Systems Architect, cross-functional teams, and business stakeholders
  • Balance speed and quality — moves fast without creating problems that slow the team down later
  • Comfortable across both backend and web code — not helpless when something crosses a layer

S U C C E S S M E T R I C S — F I R S T 1 2 M O N T H S

Success will be measured by the ability to take ownership of substantial work and deliver it independently, with technical judgment, engineering quality, and escalation calibration that earns the confidence of the Systems Architect.

The Senior Software Engineer will help ensure:

  • At least one significant integration or automation feature is delivered with minimal implementation-level direction
  • Problems are investigated and diagnosed rather than surfaced — escalations come with root cause analysis and a proposed solution
  • AI development tools are a measurable part of how this engineer works, accelerating delivery without compromising quality
  • The Systems Architect is confident handing a meaningful piece of the system to this engineer and trusting it will come back done
  • Technical decisions are made at the right level — autonomously when appropriate, escalated clearly when architectural or business-related
  • The team's codebase is left more maintainable, better tested, and more reliable as a result of this engineer's contributions

title: DIE CHASER
description:
Job Overview: The Die Chaser must ensure that our aluminum extrusion production processes run smoothly and efficiently. You will be responsible for delivering the dies listed for the extrusion press, preparing them for production promptly and efficiently, and retrieving dies back to the shop for polishing.

  • Deliver the dies to presses according to schedule and bring back extruded dies for caustic/storage.
  • Run the dies through the caustic solution to clean excess aluminum out of the die.
  • Cut off the remaining aluminum from the die, then break the die down using a die press.
  • Operate hand tools, including hammer and chisel.
  • Fill die ovens with production pick lists of dies promptly.
  • Die storage--die put away and retrieval--taking the dies out of storage.
  • Must handle short durations of high heat temperatures while staging dies into die ovens.
  • Comply with all safety guidelines and adhere to all policies, procedures, rules, quality, and customer service standards.

title: Clinical Director
description:
SUMMARY

Directs all clinical programs and services as part of the Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic Model.

EOE Statement

At HOPE, our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the community we serve. We embrace and encourage our employees’ differences in age, color, disability, ethnicity, family or marital status, gender identity or expression, language, national origin, physical and mental ability, political affiliation, race, religion, sexual orientation, socio-economic status, veteran status, and other characteristics that make our employees unique. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Responsible for review and implementation of written clinical program specific goals and outcome criteria that guide and support the provision of recovery-based services and fall within the CCBHC model.
  • Assists in the development, review, and outcome of all CCBHC and program monitors. Demonstrates the ability to oversee multiple programs simultaneously.
  • Responsible for monitoring program performance and ensuring budget goals are met.
  • Responsible for coordinating the development and implementation of new clinical programs and services, with the direction of the CCO.
  • Responsible for the supervision of clinical program directors.
  • Provides for coverage in directly overseeing all aspects of any program in the event of having a vacancy for any clinical program director.
  • Must maintain skill set of expert knowledge regarding all aspects of clinical documentation, CCBHC standards, service manual, levels of services, contracts, and specialty programs.
  • Responsible for ongoing knowledge of the course of treatment, needs, and special issues of program clients.
  • Assist in all program development, grant coordination, and budgetary needs for all current clinical programs. Works to expand and enhance all clinical programs in keeping with HOPE mission and philosophy.
  • Responsible for making recommendations concerning the number and qualifications of people needed to provide quality clinical services for the clinical programs.
  • Responsible for identifying and implementing staff training, consultation, education, and orientation needs of assigned staff to upgrade the skills needed to maintain quality program services. Oversees and coordinates all staff development needs for agency.
  • Assists CCO in clinical oversight of programs to ensure quality care is being provided and in compliance with all aspects of contract requirements, funding source expectations, and standards of practice.
  • Supports and promotes a service environment for individuals in need of behavioral health and/or co-occurring services that are recovery focused, welcoming, and attentive to the needs of individuals who may have experienced trauma in their lives. Attends annual core competencies training in relationship to individuals with co-occurring disorders or who have experienced trauma in their lives.
  • Utilizes and promotes the philosophy of Collaborative/Therapeutic Documentation to meet clinical record keeping documentation standards and ensure documentation is completed with the consumer to the extent possible and all documentation is completed on the same day of the date of service.
  • Assists with grant management as well as new grant proposals to expand clinical programs and aid in CCBHC oversight.
  • Responsible for recommendations on hours of operation of various therapeutic services program components and ensuring adequate staff coverage.
  • Responsible for ensuring that programs are delivered in a safe environment.
  • Initiates the development and revisions of agency policy and procedures.
  • Responsible for ensuring clinical CARF, DMHSAS, and funding source standards are met. Responsible for program/staff orientation and adherence to agency policy and procedures, CARF and DMHSAS standards and criteria, federal and state confidentiality rules and regulations, and any special funding source requirements.
  • Responsible for maximizing Title XIX (Medicaid) and other sources of third-party reimbursement.
  • Responsible for ensuring staff meet agency performance standards, to include reporting and record keeping requirements.
  • As needed and if eligible by licensure provides licensure supervision and/or on-site supervision for those staff who are candidates for licensure.
  • Responsible for establishing and maintaining professional working relationships with all agency directors and program staff and developing integrated service provisions between various programs.
  • Represents agency regarding clinical services to external agencies and providers. Responsible for maintaining community contacts with stakeholders and other agencies.
  • Participates as member of the agency Management Team, Clinical Team, and all other assigned meetings or needs of the agency as assigned. Will attend the majority of HOPE Board meetings.
  • May be required to work evening or weekend hours and must be reasonably available for agency needs beyond agency hours of operation.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Supervises all clinical program directors in the agency. Is responsible for the orientation, direction, coordination, and evaluation of these directors. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, orientation, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

QUALIFICATIONS To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

Oklahoma State license in a mental health field (LCSW, LPC, LMFT, and/or LADCMH) with two years’ experience in staff and/or program supervision; or

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATION

  • Required to maintain any required licenses.
  • May be required to obtain and maintain ODMHSAS Case Management certification.
  • May be required to obtain and maintain first aid and/or CPR Certification
  • Required to complete, Therapeutic Options or approved safety training and annual updates.
  • Required to travel and must possess valid Oklahoma license, meet HOPE insurance requirements, and provide motor vehicle record to the human resources office.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

Ability to read, analyze, comprehend, and interpret common professional journals, financial reports, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from consumers, regulatory agencies, or members of the community. Ability to write routine reports and correspondence and clinical writing/documentation in medical records chart. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to families, clients, and other employees of the organization, and community partners. Ability to effectively present information to top management, public groups, and/or boards of directors.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret graphs.

REASONING ABILITY

Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form. Ability to seek out supervisory assistance for additional training when needed and make application of techniques or other skills to meet essential job duties and responsibilities.

OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES

Knowledge of clinical treatment modalities and therapeutic processes. Diagnostic and assessment skills. Knowledge of the mental health service system. Ability to relate to persons with severe mental illness in a positive, helpful and constructive manner. Ability to establish effective and tactful working relationships with co-workers; to express ideas and facts clearly and concisely in written or oral form. Ability to operate computer software to collect and summarize data on persons served.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk; sit; and use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls. Duties require a large volume of handwriting. Must have vision enough to read typed or written data. Must have hearing and speech enough to communicate effectively with staff, clients, and the public in person or by phone.

WORK ENVIRONMENT The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee occasionally works in outside weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Family & Children’s Services works to heal hurting and abused children, strengthen families, and provide hope and a path to recovery for those battling mental illness and addiction. title: Conversational UX Specialist
description:
The Conversational UX Specialist owns the design quality of Omilia's conversational experiences within the Solution Optimization team. The role designs user-centric conversational flows and continuously validates and refines them using real interaction data — closing the loop between design intent and actual system performance. As the primary point of expertise for conversational UX inside Omilia, this person analyzes live conversational interactions to catch where design assumptions break down, drives fixes, and uses that analysis to improve business KPIs and overall solution quality across accounts.

Accountabilities

  • Act as the primary resource for conversational AI design, influencing and aligning cross-team efforts to ensure an optimal user experience and alignment with business KPIs.
  • Own the end-to-end quality of conversational UX design, ensuring flows are scalable, modular, and maintainable to support future business needs.
  • Drive solution optimization by analyzing conversational designs and interaction data to identify broken processes and deliver measurable performance improvements.
  • Ensure design decisions are technically viable by partnering with delivery teams and translating business needs into actionable, user-centric solutions.
  • Maintain benchmarking of core KPIs across features, services, and relevant domain/industry verticals to identify optimization opportunities and uphold best practice.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design conversational flows that are scalable, modular, and maintainable, enabling efficient adaptation to future business needs.
  • Translate complex business needs into actionable, user-centric design solutions that enhance user experience and achieve organizational objectives.
  • Present design concepts effectively to business teams and stakeholders, advocating for user-first principles while aligning with company goals.
  • Collaborate with project delivery teams to ensure design solutions are technically viable and optimized for the existing technology stack.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive documentation of design decisions, conversational systems, and user flows to facilitate team alignment and future design projects.
  • Track benchmarking for core KPIs across features, services, and relevant domain/industry verticals to compare performance and identify optimization opportunities.
  • Analyze existing conversational designs to identify broken processes, propose fixes, and implement optimized solutions.
  • Evaluate user interactions and conversation data to uncover areas for improvement, enhancing bot performance and user satisfaction.
  • Leverage insights from data analysis to drive continuous, iterative optimization of conversational experiences.
  • Stay informed about the latest trends, best practices, and principles in conversational AI design to deliver cutting-edge, accessible, and functional solutions.

Requirements

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Linguistics, Computer Science, UX Design, Psychology) or equivalent professional experience.
  • Proven experience in UX design and/or requirements analysis, design, and optimization of Conversational AI systems, with a strong understanding of conversational UX principles and best practices.
  • Skilled in crafting clear, engaging, and natural dialogue for conversational interfaces (copywriting proficiency).
  • Excellent command of spoken and written English.
  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in customer-facing roles.
  • A passion for user experience, with strong design sensibilities and deep empathy for end users.
  • Ambition, enthusiasm, and a growth mindset, coupled with strong analytical and creative thinking abilities.
  • Meticulous attention to detail and the ability to deliver high-quality work within tight deadlines.
  • Highly organized and capable of managing solo or collaborative assignments effectively.
  • Comfortable working in a fully remote, digital-first environment.

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience designing UX for AI-driven bots, including chatbots and voicebots, or familiarity with Generative AI solutions.
  • Experience with conversational automated dialogue systems (voice or chat-based); production-level knowledge of NLU/NLP solutions is a strong plus.
  • Proficiency in additional languages such as Spanish, French, and/or German.

Benefits

  • Fixed compensation;
  • Long-term employment with the working days vacation;
  • Development in professional growth (courses, training, etc);
  • Being part of successful cutting-edge technology products that are making a global impact in the service industry;
  • Proficient and fun-to-work-with colleagues;
  • Apple gear.

title: PhD in gas photonics - DTU Electro
description:
We are seeking a skilled and highly motivated PhD candidate for a 3 year position, in the fields of gas-filled hollow-core fiber lasers, ultrafast lasers, and nonlinear optics.

In this role, you will conduct cutting-edge research in ultrafast nonlinear optics using gas-filled hollow-core fiber platforms. You will develop advanced high-power near-infrared ultrafast laser sources and gas-filled fiber systems for fundamental studies and emerging photonic applications. The research will primarily be carried out in the GasLab at DTU Electro, which provides state-of-the-art infrastructure for exploratory gas-laser experiments and a collaborative environment for training and mentoring project personnel.

Our expectations of you
We expect the successful candidate to have:
  • A MSc degree in optics/photonics, optical engineering.
  • Interest and background with exploring unknown physics in the field of nonlinear photonics and ultrafast lasers.
  • Experimental experience with developing fiber lasers, with preference on gas-filled hollow-core fiber lasers.
  • The ability to work independently, and contribute creatively to research projects, and the ability to maintain an organized and safe work environment.
  • The candidate should be fluent in English, both written and spoken.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and terms of employment
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. The period of employment is 3 years.

The position is a full-time position. The starting date will be January 01, 2027 or according to mutual agreement

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Dr. Yazhou Wang (yazwang@dtu.dk) and Assoc. Prof. Christos Markos (chmar@dtu.dk).

You can read more about DTU Electro at .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU.

Application procedure
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 31 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:
  • A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
  • List of publications

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with the industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

title: ITSM  Architecture and Design
description:
We are looking for an experienced MOVEit L3 Engineer / Architect to lead the design, administration, support, and optimization of the MOVEit Managed File Transfer (MFT) platform. The role will be responsible for L3 production support, architecture, integrations, security, automation, performance, and platform governance across a global environment

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the MOVEit MFT platform architecture, design, implementation, and lifecycle management.

  • Provide L3 technical support for complex production incidents, service requests, and recurring issues.

  • Design and manage secure file transfer workflows for internal applications, external partners, vendors, and business users.

  • Configure and troubleshoot MOVEit Transfer / Automation, including workflows, jobs, schedules, notifications, and file-processing rules.

  • Design and maintain integrations using SFTP, FTPS, HTTPS, APIs, REST/SOAP, and other secure transfer protocols.

  • Develop and optimize MOVEit Automation workflows and scripting to automate file transfers and business processes.

  • Lead troubleshooting of performance, connectivity, authentication, certificate, encryption, and transfer failures.

  • Manage high availability, disaster recovery, backup, monitoring, capacity planning, and platform resilience.

  • Implement and maintain security controls, including encryption, access controls, authentication, certificates, audit logging, and privileged access.

  • Integrate MOVEit with Active Directory/LDAP, applications, databases, cloud platforms, SIEM, monitoring, and ITSM tools.

  • Perform platform upgrades, patches, migrations, configuration changes, and version upgrades with minimal business disruption.

  • Establish monitoring and alerting for critical transfers, failed jobs, storage utilization, system health, and SLA breaches.

  • Lead root-cause analysis (RCA) for major incidents and implement permanent corrective actions.

  • Define and maintain technical standards, architecture documentation, operational procedures, and knowledge articles.

  • Work with application, security, infrastructure, network, vendor, and business teams to deliver MFT solutions.

  • Provide technical leadership and mentoring to L1/L2 MOVEit support teams.

  • Participate in 24x7 on-call / escalation support for critical production services.

Required Technical Skills

  • Strong hands-on experience with Progress MOVEit Transfer and MOVEit Automation.

  • Strong understanding of Managed File Transfer (MFT) architecture and enterprise integration patterns.

  • Advanced knowledge of:

    • SFTP / FTPS / HTTPS

    • SSH and public/private key authentication

    • PGP encryption/decryption

    • SSL/TLS certificates

    • REST APIs / Web Services

    • Active Directory / LDAP

    • DNS, networking and firewall concepts

  • Experience with MOVEit Automation scripting and workflow development.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills across application, OS, network, authentication, and file-transfer layers.

  • Experience with Windows Server administration and enterprise infrastructure.

  • Knowledge of SQL/database connectivity and scripting/automation using PowerShell or similar technologies.

  • Experience with monitoring, logging, SIEM and ITSM platforms.

  • Understanding of security, compliance, audit and data protection requirements.

Architect-Level Expectations

  • Define the target-state MOVEit architecture and technical roadmap.

  • Evaluate and recommend solutions for scalability, HA/DR, security, performance, and integration.

  • Lead technical design reviews and provide High-Level Design (HLD) / Low-Level Design (LLD) documentation.

  • Assess new business requirements and translate them into secure and scalable MFT solutions.

  • Drive platform standardization, automation and operational efficiency.

  • Identify opportunities to reduce manual processes and improve SLA, reliability and supportability.

Act as the technical SME and escalation point for MOVEit across the organization

Preferred Certifications / Experience

  • Progress MOVEit / MFT certifications or equivalent product expertise.

  • ITIL certification is preferred.

  • Security certifications are an advantage.

  • Experience supporting global enterprise environments.

  • Experience with cloud/hybrid MFT architecture is a plus.

  • Experience with PCI, SOX, GDPR or other compliance requirements is desirable.

Key Success Measures

  • Reduction in recurring file-transfer incidents.

  • Timely resolution of L3 escalations and major incidents.

  • Secure and compliant file-transfer operations.

  • Successful platform upgrades, migrations and architectural improvements.

Effective knowledge transfer to L1/L2 support teams

title: Portfolio Architect - Information Technology
description:
Alberta Blue Cross® is an Alberta based organization dedicated to delivering exceptional customer experience and community leadership. We’re committed to providing the best health coverage to over 1.8 million members and take an active role in promoting wellness. We believe in what we do—and place trust in our employees to deliver our vision.


Working at Alberta Blue Cross® means having a career where you’ll be recognized for your contributions. We value diversity, encourage our team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance and provide opportunities for career growth.

OVERVIEW:

We have exciting opportunities for several Portfolio Architect roles to join our Enterprise Architecture team. Reporting to the Chief Architect, these are senior individual contributor roles accountable for owning the target architecture and modernization roadmap for defined technology or business portfolios, ensuring technology investments are coherent, sequenced, fundable, and aligned to enterprise priorities.

Current anticipated portfolio roles include Customer Portfolio Architect, Operations Portfolio Architect, Corporate Portfolio Architect, and IT 4 IT Portfolio Architect. Additional or adjusted portfolio assignments may be considered as organizational needs evolve.

The Portfolio Architect operates as the bridge between Enterprise Architecture direction and delivery execution, translating corporate and IT strategy, architectural guardrails, reference architecture target states, risk posture, and IT leadership priorities into practical roadmaps that delivery teams can execute against with confidence.

This is a strategic portfolio architecture role, not a solution design, development leadership, delivery management, product ownership, or domain architecture position. The role ensures initiatives advance Alberta Blue Cross as an integrated enterprise system rather than optimizing locally at the expense of customer experience, integration, cost-to-serve, security, operational resilience, or long-term sustainability.

While these are not people leader roles and do not include direct people-management accountability, they are senior architecture roles with significant influence across portfolio planning, investment alignment, delivery enablement, and formal architecture governance.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

  • Interpret corporate and IT strategy, Enterprise Architecture direction, business priorities, and portfolio context into practical architecture guidance.

  • Develop and maintain portfolio architecture views that clarify current state, target state, transition states, dependencies, risks, and sequencing considerations.

  • Assess impacts across business capabilities, platforms, integrations, data, security, operations, customer experience, regulatory obligations, and delivery readiness.

  • Prepare decision-ready options, recommendations, and implications for portfolio planning, investment sequencing, and architecture governance discussions.

  • Collaborate with IT leadership, EPMO, Finance, business stakeholders, Enterprise Architecture, Domain Architects, Solution Architects, and delivery teams to align plans and resolve ambiguity.

  • Provide portfolio guardrails and context to Solution Architects and delivery teams without taking ownership of detailed solution design, engineering, delivery management, or sprint-level decisions.

  • Identify and escalate material risks, unresolved trade-offs, duplication, dependency gaps, or drift from target state through established governance forums.

POSITION SCOPE:

  • Report to the Chief Architect as senior individual contributors within the Enterprise Architecture organization.

  • May be classified at the Manager or Director level depending on applicant experience, portfolio complexity, stakeholder scope, enterprise impact, and demonstrated seniority.

  • Support portfolios such as Customer, Operations, Corporate, IT 4 IT, or other portfolios aligned to enterprise priorities.

  • Exercise leadership through influence, architecture direction, stakeholder alignment, and decision framing rather than direct people-management authority.

  • Remain distinct from Solution Architecture, development leadership, product ownership, delivery management, and domain architecture roles.

  • Do not directly manage people, design detailed solutions, own sprint-level decisions, approve or reject solutions unilaterally, manage delivery teams, take over development work, or own formal governance outcomes.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

  • Accountable for the architectural coherence of the assigned portfolio, including alignment to enterprise strategy, principles, reference architectures, and approved guardrails.

  • Accountable for the portfolio target architecture and roadmap remaining current, actionable, and connected to business outcomes, investment planning, delivery capacity, and modernization priorities.

  • Accountable for making major architectural risks, dependencies, trade-offs, and target-state deviations visible to senior stakeholders and governance forums.

  • Accountable for enabling consistent, transparent, and traceable architecture decision support for portfolio planning, sequencing, ARB readiness, and formal governance outcomes.

KEY SUCCESS MEASURES:

  • Adopted portfolio architecture direction: Target architecture and roadmap are understood, current, and used by IT leadership, EPMO, Finance, Solution Architects, and delivery teams to guide planning and execution.

  • Improved investment and sequencing decisions: Portfolio priorities are supported by clear architectural rationale, dependency visibility, trade-off analysis, affordability considerations, and alignment to corporate and IT strategy.

  • Reduced architectural friction: Major risks, technical debt patterns, duplication, and target-state deviations are identified earlier, resulting in fewer late-stage escalations, avoidable rework, and unresolved delivery constraints.

  • Stronger governance readiness: Initiatives entering ARB or related governance forums have clear portfolio context, decision options, risk framing, and traceable alignment to enterprise principles and guardrails.

  • Clearer role alignment and delivery enablement: Stakeholders understand where Portfolio Architecture adds value, how it differs from Solution Architecture and development delivery, and how portfolio guardrails enable rather than duplicate delivery work.

WHAT YOU WILL HAVE:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

  • Experience in the life and health insurance industry is a strong asset, particularly where it includes exposure to customer experience, claims, benefits administration, regulatory obligations, data privacy, digital services, or insurance technology modernization.

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise architecture, portfolio architecture, technology strategy, solution architecture, or senior technology advisory roles; Manager or Director classification will reflect demonstrated seniority, scope, and enterprise impact.

  • Demonstrated ability to define target architecture, transition states, modernization roadmaps, and sequencing recommendations for complex portfolios or transformation programs.

  • Strong understanding of enterprise architecture practices, including architecture principles, reference architectures, governance, guardrails, technology lifecycle management, technical debt, risk, regulatory obligations, and operational constraints.

  • Experience with enterprise architecture tools or repository platforms is an asset, including use of these solutions to model capabilities, applications, technologies, roadmaps, dependencies, standards, risks, and architecture decisions.

  • Experience influencing senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams across IT, business, EPMO, Finance, architecture, product, and delivery groups without relying on direct reporting authority.

  • Ability to assess cross-domain impacts across business capabilities, applications, data, integration, digital experience, cloud, security, identity, platforms, operations, and customer outcomes.

  • Excellent communication, facilitation, executive storytelling, and decision-framing skills, with the ability to clarify trade-offs, role boundaries, risks, and recommendations for diverse audiences.

COMPETENCY MATRIX:

Portfolio Architecture

  • Description: Defines coherent target architecture, transition states, and roadmap direction for the assigned portfolio.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Maintains a current roadmap with clear transition states and an adopted portfolio architecture direction.

Strategic Influence

  • Description: Guides senior stakeholders through ambiguity, trade-offs, and decisions without relying on direct authority.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Builds stakeholder alignment, supports timely decision-making, and provides clear recommendations.

Investment Alignment

  • Description: Connects architecture decisions to business value, affordability, risk, delivery readiness, and sequencing.

  • Proficiency Level: Working to Advanced

  • Evidence: Provides decision-ready options, identifies dependencies, and establishes clear sequencing rationale.

Enterprise Systems Thinking

  • Description: Assesses impacts across capabilities, platforms, data, integration, security, operations, customer outcomes, and regulatory context.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Enables earlier visibility of risks and reduces architectural friction across the enterprise.

Architecture Tooling

  • Description: Uses enterprise architecture tools or repositories to maintain architecture knowledge, dependencies, standards, roadmaps, and decision traceability.

  • Proficiency Level: Working to Advanced

  • Evidence: Maintains reliable repository content, develops reusable architecture views, and ensures architecture decisions are traceable.

Governance & Role Clarity

  • Description: Applies guardrails, clarifies accountabilities, and enables governance readiness without duplicating delivery work.

  • Proficiency Level: Working to Advanced

  • Evidence: Supports clear ARB preparation and decision records while reducing role conflicts and duplication.

Executive Communication

  • Description: Translates complex architecture topics into concise messages for technical, business, Finance, EPMO, and executive audiences.

  • Proficiency Level: Working to Advanced

  • Evidence: Develops clear roadmap narratives, effectively frames risks, and provides leadership-ready recommendations.

BEHAVIORAL INDICATORS:

Strategic Thinking

  • Anticipates portfolio impacts, downstream dependencies, and long-term implications of architecture and investment decisions.

  • Balances modernization, customer outcomes, business value, risk, compliance, affordability, and sustainability.

Leadership

  • Provides calm, credible leadership when priorities, dependencies, stakeholder expectations, or trade-offs are unclear.

  • Leads through influence and clarity while enabling Solution Architects, product teams, and delivery teams to work within agreed guardrails.

Analytical Skills

  • Uses structured thinking to assess options, constraints, dependencies, risks, and transition paths.

  • Simplifies complex architecture issues into practical recommendations for decision-making.

Collaboration

  • Builds trust across business, technology, architecture, EPMO, Finance, product, and delivery stakeholders.

  • Resolves tension by focusing on enterprise outcomes, transparent trade-offs, and clear accountabilities.

title: Transitional Care Associate
description:
Primary City/State:

Phoenix, Arizona

Department Name:

Case Mgmt-Hosp

Work Shift:

Day

Job Category:

Clinical Care

A rewarding career that fits your life. Those who have joined the Banner mission come from all walks of life, united by the common goal: Make health care easier, so life can be better. If changing health care for the better sounds like something you want to be part of, apply today.

Are you passionate about making a meaningful difference in patients' lives? We're seeking a dedicated Transition Care Assistant with a Bachelor's Degree and experience in hospital/healthcare settings or a social work background to join our collaborative interdisciplinary team. In this vital role, you'll guide patients and families through the discharge process—from reviewing daily holdovers and attending multidisciplinary rounds with physicians, nurses, nutritionists, and pharmacists, to communicating discharge plans and providing crucial support every step of the way. As a valued team member, you'll experience the rewarding impact of direct patient interaction while building a strong foundation for professional growth in healthcare. If you thrive in fast-paced, engaging environments where your contributions truly matter and collaboration drives success, this is your opportunity to advance your career while making a real difference in patient care!

SCHEDULE:

  • Full Time / 40 Hours
  • Sunday-Saturday, 10 hour shifts.
  • Weekend rotations are required in this role.
  • Enjoy a flat rate $3/hour weekend shift differential when applicable.

LOCATION

  • Banner University Medical Center - Phoenix

University Medical Center Phoenix is a nationally recognized academic medical center. The world-class hospital is focused on coordinated clinical care, expanded research activities and nurturing future generations of highly trained medical professionals. Our commitment to nursing excellence has enabled us to achieve Magnet™ recognition by the American Nurses Credentialing Center. The Phoenix campus, long known for excellent patient care, has over 730 licensed beds, several unique specialty units and is the new home for medical discoveries, thanks to our collaboration with the University of Arizona College of Medicine - Phoenix. Additionally, the campus responsibilities include fully integrated multi-specialty and sub-specialty clinics.

POSITION SUMMARY
This position facilitates the safe and timely transition of clients from acute care to alternative levels of care such as skilled nursing facility, long-term acute care, inpatient rehabilitation, home infusion therapy, hospice and/or home care or community program. Facilitates discharge plan for the transition of care and services into the designated setting or service. Provides on-site or telephonic discharge arrangements to post-acute and community services.

CORE FUNCTIONS
1. Processes and facilitates the timely discharge/transfer of clients from hospital care to identified post-acute setting. Notifies care coordination team member(s) if patient or caregiver demonstrate or verbalize any inability/concern to be able to manage their post-acute plan or responsibilities.

2. Facilitates/ implements the care plan with proposed interventions in collaboration with healthcare team. Collaborates with all members of the healthcare team to implement, manage and communicate the transition of care arrangements.

3. Participates in performance improvement projects, Banner initiatives and performs data collection for measurement of projects as assigned.

4. Documents all interventions in the patient medical record both timely and accurately including all elements of the discharge plan. Performs transfer of accurate, pertinent patient information between all appropriate entities of the post-acute care continuum.

5. Assist and support patients and families in making appropriate arrangements for the post-acute plan. Performs follow-up calls to patients and providers as indicated and report any concerns to leadership.

6. Serves as an intermediary when providing community resources to patients, caregiver, and families. Discusses with patient, caregiver, and/or family maintaining clear communication regarding anticipated discharge date and potential care settings.

7. Maintains knowledge of Medicare, Medicaid and other program benefits to assist patients with transition of care planning and choices.

8. Employee has freedom to determine how to best accomplish functions within established procedures and implements the discharge plan under the delegated authority of a provider, licensed MSW, registered nurse or other licensed healthcare professional. Confers with supervisor/manager on any unusual situations and communicates plans and activities for patient discharge across the care continuum. Internal customers: Post-acute services team members and all levels of nursing management and staff, medical staff, and all other members of assigned facility interdisciplinary health care team. External customers: home health agencies, nursing homes, insurance providers, group homes, assisted living facilities, hospice, long-term acute care hospitals, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, volunteer agencies, county/governmental agencies and medical supply companies and others as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
A Bachelor’s degree in social work or related degree or a Licensed Practice Nurse, or a Licensed Respiratory Therapist required.

Must have knowledge of government/community agencies and resources, such as Medicare/Medicaid, long term care or other applicable resources/services. Must demonstrate effective communication and customer service skills, human relation skills and time management skills. Must be able to work flexible hours and work weekends on rotation. BLS required. (BLS is not required for employees working in the Insurance Division.)

Employees working at Banner Behavioral Health Hospital, BTMC Behavioral or BUMG, BUMCT in a Behavioral Health clinical setting that serves children must possess an Arizona Fingerprint Clearance Card at the time of hire and maintain the card for the duration of their employment. An Arizona Criminal History Affidavit must be signed upon hire. Employees working at BUMCS in a Behavioral Health clinical setting must possess an Arizona Fingerprint Clearance Card at the time of hire and maintain the card for the duration of their employment.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Previous experience in health care service setting, interacting with patients and families, usually obtained through work in social services, as a licensed practical nurse or in a discharge planning setting.

Additional related education and/or experience preferred.

title: Application Engineering Specialist
description:
Fenner Dunlop, a Michelin Group company, designs and manufactures the widest range of bulk material handling conveyor belts in the world. We strive to be the premier provider of the safest and most reliable conveyor belting and services to a variety of heavy industrial markets such as coal mining, hard rock mining, sand, gravel, wood handling, power generation, pulp and paper. Fenner Dunlop provides North American made belting, manufactured at our facilities located throughout the United States and Canada. For over 150 years, Fenner Dunlop has researched, designed, developed, manufactured, and tested its conveyor belting products, supporting nearly any type of conveyor application, and providing the right solutions to protect conveyor system investments in the harshest conveying environments.

We are seeking an Application Engineering Specialist to conduct on-site conveyor belt surveys and technical assessments in the field at customer locations. This position supports the sales organization by collecting accurate field information, evaluating conveyor belt and system conditions, strengthening customer relationships, and identifying opportunities for belt replacement, technical services, and related products. This role works closely with outside sales representatives, inside sales, distributors, technical teams, service personnel, and customers to document field conditions and provide the information needed to develop technical recommendations, quotes, and long-term customer solutions.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

The essential functions of this position include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Conduct conveyor belt surveys and inspections at customer locations, including manufacturing plants, mines, quarries, terminals, and other industrial facilities.
  • Inspect and document conveyor belt and system conditions, including belt specifications, belt construction, covers, splices, tracking, wear patterns, damage, conveyor components, and operating conditions.
  • Collect accurate field measurements and application information, including belt width, belt length, carcass type, cover gauges, pulley diameters, take-up configuration, troughing angle, conveyor layout, operating speed, capacity, and other relevant technical details.
  • Evaluate current belt performance and identify observed or potential failure points, maintenance concerns, abnormal wear, and opportunities to improve belt life or performance.
  • Gather available information regarding historical belt life, operating conditions, and competitive belt performance.
  • Inspect customer-owned belt inventory and document belt specifications, storage conditions, age, condition, and suitability for anticipated applications.
  • Assist with the field investigation and documentation of warranty claims, including photographs, measurements, operating information, product identification, and other relevant evidence.
  • Prepare complete, accurate, and timely survey reports containing photographs, measurements, observations, and technical information needed to support quotes, product recommendations, warranty evaluations, and customer follow-up.
  • Work alongside sales representatives and distributors during customer visits, conveyor inspections, technical reviews, product evaluations, and business-development activities.
  • Identify potential customer needs and communicate sales opportunities involving replacement belts, lagging, splicing materials, conveyor accessories, field services, or other related products and services.
  • Provide field information and observations to technical and sales personnel to support belt selection, application analysis, troubleshooting, and product recommendations.
  • Communicate professionally and effectively with customers, distributors, contractors, and internal personnel while representing the Company in a knowledgeable, safety-conscious, and service-oriented manner.
  • Document customer interactions and site findings using Company-approved reporting tools, templates, customer relationship management systems, and other business platforms.
  • Assist with customer and distributor training by sharing product knowledge, field observations, and recommended practices related to conveyor belt selection, operation, inspection, and maintenance.
  • Comply with all Company and customer safety requirements, including required personal protective equipment, hazard assessments, lockout/tagout procedures, confined-space restrictions, and site-specific safety protocols.
  • Travel domestically and internationally to customer, distributor, and Company locations, generally up to 50% of working time, including overnight travel.
  • Support other technical investigations, field evaluations, training activities, and analyses consistent with the responsibilities of the position.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned based on business needs.

Required Qualifications

  • Technical, mechanical, industrial, engineering, or maintenance-related education, training, certification, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Demonstrated mechanical aptitude and the ability to understand industrial equipment, conveyor systems, and technical applications.
  • Ability to accurately inspect, measure, photograph, document, and communicate technical field information.
  • Ability to read and understand technical specifications, product information, equipment documentation, and measurement instruments.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to interact professionally with customers, distributors, sales representatives, technical personnel, and contractors.
  • Ability to work independently in the field while maintaining timely communication and coordination with the sales and technical organizations.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, judgment, and follow-through.
  • Proficiency with standard business technology, including mobile devices, digital photography, email, Microsoft Office, reporting tools, and customer relationship management systems.
  • Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally, including overnight travel, up to 50% of working time primarily in the United States.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a valid passport for international business travel.
  • Valid driver’s license and the ability to satisfy applicable Company driving requirements when operating a motor vehicle.
  • Ability to satisfy lawful, job-related customer and Company site-access requirements, which may include safety orientations, training certifications, identity verification, background screening, drug and alcohol testing, respiratory-clearance evaluations, fit testing, and the use of required personal protective equipment. All requirements will be administered in accordance with applicable law, Company policy, and reasonable accommodation obligations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with conveyor belts, conveyor systems, bulk material handling, mining, aggregates, terminals, industrial maintenance, field service, or a related industry.
  • Experience conducting conveyor belt surveys or performing belt installation, splicing, inspection, troubleshooting, maintenance, or repair.
  • Knowledge of conveyor belt construction, covers, carcass types, splice methods, conveyor components, and common belt damage or failure modes.
  • Experience supporting a sales organization, distributor network, or customer-facing technical-service function.
  • Experience identifying customer needs and communicating product or service opportunities to sales personnel.
  • Experience preparing technical field reports, warranty documentation, inspection reports, or customer recommendations.

Physical and Work Environment Requirements

  • The following requirements reflect the physical activities and work environments that may be encountered while performing the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
  • Regularly walk through industrial and customer operating sites, including uneven, elevated, wet, dusty, noisy, hot, cold, or outdoor work areas.
  • Frequently stand, walk, bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, reach, and position measurement equipment in and around conveyor systems.
  • Ascend and descend stairs and ladders and access authorized conveyor inspection areas.
  • Safely lift, carry, push, or pull equipment and materials weighing up to 20 pounds.
  • Wear required personal protective equipment, which may include a hard hat, safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, high-visibility clothing, safety footwear, fall-protection equipment, or respiratory protection where legally permitted and job-related.
  • Travel by automobile and commercial aircraft and remain at customer locations for extended periods as business needs require.
  • Work around operating industrial equipment only when permitted by applicable safety procedures and site authorization.
  • Comply with Company and customer safety rules, security procedures, and site-access requirements.

What We Offer

At Fenner Dunlop, a Michelin Group company, we care about work/life balance as well as the health and financial wellbeing of our employees and their families. So, whether you're considering family planning, trying to decide how to best care for your family, or want to make a difference through volunteerism, you're sure to find Fenner Dunlop's competitive and comprehensive employee-focused benefits package helpful.

title: Roustabout
description:
The job of the Roustabout is to safely and efficiently perform all manual labor tasks throughout the rig. The Roustabout works under the direction/ supervision of the Crane Operator, but reports to the Rig Manager.
Assists the Crane Operator with offloading and back loading of supply vessels Performs housekeeping activities on the rig (excluding the rig floor) including washing, chipping and painting Assists Crane Operator with moving and relocating supplies, pipe and other equipment on the rig which involves attaching slings and cables to the object being moved. Assists the Derrickhand within the mud pit, mud pump and chemical sack rooms Performs simple maintenance and repairs to the plumbing and sewer systems When trained, relieves the floorhand on the drilling crew Performs other general labor duties as assigned  Essential Functions:  Attention span to stay alert and attentive for up to 12 hour tour while performing sometimes repetitive and monotonous tasks Able to work 14 days on and 14 days off, including holidays, weekends and or days and nights; and able to work and live with others in relatively close confines. Able to receive verbal and written instructions Must be able to maintain good footing while standing and walking for a minimum of 4 hours at any one time, including standing and walking on steel decking and grating or possibly on wet service ship decks in rough seas with waves pushing across the deck. Must be able to repetitively lift and carry items weighing upwards of 60 lbs up and down stairs and/or distances up to 150 feet. Must be able to exert a push or pull force of up to 120 lbs while holding the tag lines of equipment and pipe during loading and offloading procedures When working on a supply or cargo vessel, the Roustabout must be able to identify hand signals at a distance of 150 feet from the Crane Operator. title: Senior Director, Corporate Partnership Operations
description:
At Feed the Children, we recognize the value of outstanding people, and we are looking for compassionate changemakers to join our team. We pride ourselves on cultivating a collaborative workplace where employees experience productive and rewarding employment and feel engaged in our mission to end childhood hunger. Our passionate team shares a deep sense of purpose, and we dream big to solve complex problems and create positive impact in communities around the world.

Feed the Children is recognized by Candid with its Platinum Seal of Transparency and is accredited by the BBB Wise Giving Alliance. The organization has received a 4-star rating from Charity Navigator and is consistently recognized on the Forbes Top 100 Charities list.

We are currently in search of a Senior Director, Corporate Partnership Operations to join our Corporate Partnerships team! The Senior Director, Corporate Partnership Operations provides people leadership and strategic direction for the operations team, including oversight of processing of all in-kind donations, coordination with logistics and inventory management and compliance with the organization’s gift acceptance policy. The position is also responsible for pursuing new innovations such as leveraging continuous improvement techniques, AI and other tools to increase team efficiency and effectiveness, identifying new pathways for in-kind shipping and cold storage and expanding our strategies to be inclusive of our global footprint to maximize our mission impact. The Senior Director has responsibility for a portfolio of over $120+M in gift-in-kind product annually.

Note: The ideal candidate for this position will work hybrid from our corporate office in Oklahoma City, OK, however all qualified candidates will be considered nationwide.

Job Requirements:

Education

Bachelor's degree (BA, BS) or equivalent with emphasis in business, communications, or another related field is preferred.

Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in corporate partnerships, corporate sales/business development or operations, including senior-level responsibility for year-over-year revenue growth, especially for consumer packaged goods or donated products.

  • High proficiency in operational excellence, ensuring consistent project management, documentation of plans, deliverables, and outcomes with accuracy and accountability.
  • Experience setting strategy and assigning/aligning responsibilities based on team capacity, strengths, and client needs; able to establish clear expectations, timelines, and standards across the team.
  • Experience forecasting revenue; able to translate revenue/activation plans into operational requirements and proactively mitigate delivery risk.
  • Experience leading continuous improvement projects (e.g., Kaizen) that deliver measurable outcomes (e.g., cost savings, time, etc.)
  • Proven success overseeing multiple workstreams simultaneously while coordinating across internal teams; able to create alignment and efficiencies that improve implementation outcomes at scale.
  • Able to guide and elevate work produced by team members.
  • Strong negotiation, influence, and conflict-resolution skills; able to navigate complex stakeholder environments with professionalism and executive presence.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and SharePoint required
  • Any combination of education, training and experience which provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the essential functions of this job may be considered

Essential Functions:

Strategy and Planning

  • Lead strategy development for the Corporate Partnership Operations team, document annual plans, budgets and KPIs; collaborate cross-functionally to ensure alignment with key stakeholders including Corporate Partnerships, Logistics and Inventory Management, Marketing and Communication, Finance and others.
  • Collaborate with VP, Corporate Partnerships and Cause Marketing to build annual and multi-year GIK budget and growth plans, revenue and expenses, based on organizational growth and impact strategies.
  • Partner with US Mission impact to forecast program implementation support and needs tied to partner commitments; coordinate with Marketing & Communications, Finance, and Operations to anticipate constraints, align resources, and mitigate delivery risks as needed.
  • Identify areas of opportunity for continuous improvement and increasing operational efficiency while not sacrificing effectiveness. Leverage lean six sigma, KAIZEN or other tools (including technology) to streamline workflows and operations to save time, resources and ultimately drive impact.
  • In partnership with stakeholders including Corporate Partnerships and Logistics/Inventory Management, identify key projects for innovation including increased third-party donated services (e.g., shipping, cold storage) and build strategies to support and implement.
  • In partnership with VP, Corporate Partnerships and Cause Marketing, develop international GIK strategy, tactics and processes with International Operations
  • Identify emerging donated product industry trends, that help inform fundraising opportunities for Feed the Children the Children. Help to educate the full corporate partnership team on best practices in securing donated products through developing training and sharing trends.

Portfolio Management

  • Responsible for oversight of the donated product portfolio that supports Feed the Children’s community partner network, with a portfolio of $120+M in GIK. Focus portfolio growth on products that align with beneficiary needs and scaling program impact strategies.
  • Lead team in stewarding and growing the organization’s gift in kind fundraising approach; set portfolio strategy, engagement standards, and expectations for results.
  • Ensure the team maintains documented renewal plans, timelines, and solicitations in the CRM; coach account planning discipline and drive execution that grows gifts-in-kind (GIK) revenue and always sets the stage for future cash growth potential.
  • Ensure all partner activities/results are monitored and reported in a professional manner to internal and external stakeholders.
  • Monitor assignment of inbound donor inquiries to ensure alignment with gift acceptance policy and overall organizational goals and objectives.

Operational Fulfillment

  • Oversee donation processing and fulfillment, activation, and reporting, ensuring high-quality delivery, clear internal ownership, and a consistent partner experience from commitment through closeout.
  • Ensure monthly, quarterly and annual budget and KPI reporting is accurate and timely.
  • Collaborate to create alignment and efficiencies for partnership implementation by establishing playbooks, timelines, and cross-functional routines that improve speed, quality, and consistency across the portfolio.
  • Serve as operations lead on cross-functional team investigating all product diversions and product security issues.
  • Provide guidance and insights into new reporting and inventory technologies as needed (e.g., inventory management system, financial systems).

Leadership and Team management

  • Carry out supervisory responsibility in accordance and compliance with policies, procedures and applicable laws including: goal setting, coaching and development; training in job skills; planning, assigning and directing work; appraising performance; addressing complaints and resolving problems; hiring/onboarding as needed, and creating a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Model best practices in donor and stakeholder relationship management and execution.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Maintain regular attendance and punctuality which are critical in order to complete the day-to-day tasks of this position.
  • Carries out supervisory responsibility in accordance with policies, procedures and applicable laws including: training in job skills; planning, assigning and directing work; evaluating performance; addressing complaints and resolving problems.
  • Establish an environment of high performance and continuous improvement that values learning, a commitment to quality, welcomes and encourages collaboration, and fosters both intra and inter-departmental dialogue and respect.
  • Model the type and level of behavior, professionalism and personal leadership that is in accordance with the values of the organization.
  • Domestic travel required up to 15%.
  • Attend relevant and key Feed the Children campaign and organizational events as necessary.
  • Support events as assigned and perform other related duties as required.
  • Perform other related duties as required.

          About Feed the Children:

          As a leading anti-hunger organization, Feed the Children is committed to ending childhood hunger. For children everywhere, we believe that having enough to eat is a fundamental right.

          Feed the Children is a global movement focused on ending childhood hunger in the U.S. and around the world. Working alongside communities, we provide food, essentials, and opportunities to children and families who need them most so every child can survive and thrive.

          We are committed to helping families experiencing hunger and hardship so children have what they need to stay healthy, learn, and grow. By uniting people and inspiring action, we work to create a world where no child goes to bed hungry. Compassion has no borders. We believe that every child deserves a chance to thrive.

          Our Values:

          We are driven by a shared sense of PURPOSE. At Feed the Children, our commitment to the mission is at the heart of what we do and fuels our collective impact in the communities where we serve.

          We cannot achieve our bold vision without our talented PEOPLE. We are passionate about fostering a best-in-class workforce that is engaged, respected, and empowered to deliver results.

          We believe in CURIOSITY and continued learning. Success requires a culture of discovery, curiosity and continued learning to expand our knowledge, seek new perspectives and challenge the status quo.

          We know COLLABORATION is the only way to end childhood hunger. We cannot succeed alone. It will take all of us – our employees, donors, partners, volunteers – working together to accomplish our ambitious goals.

          We DREAM big. When we work together, we collectively reimagine what is possible. We dream big to solve complex problems and create deep impact in communities around the world.

          We VALUE every donor. We respect our donors’ intentions and promote responsible stewardship of the resources they entrust to us.

          Join Feed the Children and help create a world where no child goes to bed hungry.

          In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

          Feed the Children is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for positions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, political affiliation, pregnancy, military and/or veterans’ status, genetic characteristics, marital status or any other considerations made unlawful by applicable state, federal, or local law. Feed the Children welcomes and encourages applications from persons with physical and mental disabilities and will make every effort to reasonably accommodate the needs of those persons. Additionally, Feed the Children strives to provide an environment free from sexual exploitation and abuse and harassment in all places where relief and development programs are implemented. Feed the Children expects its employees to maintain high ethical standards, protect organizational integrity and reputation, and ensure that Feed the Children work is carried out in honest and fair methods, in alignment with the Feed the Children safeguarding and associated policies.

The core objective of your role is to introduce modern, state-of-the-art ML approaches that run alongside our existing infrastructure to create a powerful, hybrid architecture. This is a unique opportunity to tackle complex challenges in low-latency inference, massive-scale entity resolution, and continuous learning systems.

Note: Due to the highly proprietary nature of our systems, the specific deliverables, architecture, and exact technologies will be discussed in detail under an NDA during your first interview.

Key Responsibilities

  • System Enhancement & Innovation: Design, train, and deploy state-of-the-art Natural Language Processing (NLP) models to complement and scale our existing high-throughput data architecture.

  • Architecture Integration: Build robust integration layers that allow new machine learning predictions to work seamlessly alongside our established production systems.

  • Continuous Improvement Pipelines: Develop automated feedback loops and learning mechanisms that enable our systems to adapt, update, and improve over time with minimal manual intervention.

  • Production Deployment & Optimization: Transition models from research/evaluation into full production, optimizing complex models for strict low-latency inference and high reliability.

  • Quality & Evaluation Frameworks: Establish rigorous evaluation benchmarks, automated testing harnesses, and monitoring dashboards to guarantee the accuracy and stability of ML implementations.

Revised Required Skills & Experience

  • Advanced NLP & Deep Learning: Deep theoretical and practical understanding of core NLP tasks, such as entity extraction, text classification, and contextual understanding.

  • Transformer Architectures: Proven experience training, fine-tuning, and deploying modern transformer-based models and encoding methods for complex text tasks.

  • MLOps & Production Engineering: Strong track record of optimizing models for low-latency environments (e.g., batch inference, model distillation, hardware acceleration) and deploying them at scale.

  • Evaluation & Metrics: Expertise in designing ML evaluation frameworks, building gold-standard baseline datasets, and tracking performance metrics to identify and resolve edge cases.

  • Complex System Integration: Experience combining probabilistic machine learning models with deterministic or legacy software architectures, including confidence scoring and A/B testing rollouts.

  • Software Engineering Best Practices: Strong coding skills with a focus on writing clean, scalable code, creating technical documentation, and maintaining robust CI/CD pipelines for ML models.
