description:
PRN position only.

Competitive Pay!

Responsible for care of medical and psychiatric clients, be a liaison for hospital and structure emergency care for patients, participation in patient care teams, and assistance to management, as requested. Demonstrates knowledge of co-occurring disorders and appropriate interventions. Generally will treat over 20 patients daily.

PREFERRED EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:

  • Medical Degree with psychiatry specialty and a minimum of 5 years of psychiatry experience.
  • Previous experience in community-based mental health organization is desired.
  • Extensive experience diagnosing mental health problems with adult & children clients.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Appropriate credentials to practice psychiatry in Oklahoma.
No history of ethics or other professional violations

SPECIAL JOB DIMENSIONS:

Normal office hours, with some evening and weekend clinic hours for clients.

CCBHC Model of Care

Family & Children’s Services works to heal hurting and abused children, strengthen families, and provide hope and a path to recovery for those battling mental illness and addiction. You will be working in an innovative and dynamic environment using a new transformative model of care Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC). This model is characterized by innovative, team-based approach and whole person care for adults and children with a range of complex mental health and substance use challenges.

Utilizing multi-disciplinary teams, staff work collaboratively to provide a coordinated effort to enhance client recovery. Robust CCBHC services often result in better client outcomes and quality of care due to:

  1. Increased access to care and crisis services
  2. Expanded traditional community mental health and substance use services.
  3. Added Care Coordination and physical health screening for mental health clients
  4. Greater access to Social Services for clients’ economic and social needs
  5. Increased specialized services for veterans, those most in need, and those impacted by the opioid crisis.

Drug-Free Workplace Policy

This job is classified as a “safety-sensitive” position as defined by the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana and Patient Protection Act. Possession of a medical marijuana license will not exclude any applicant; however all employees are subject to the Family & Children’s Services Drug Free Workplace Policy.

title: Manufacturing Technician
description:
Starting at $18/hr. | Full-Time | Growth Opportunities

We are looking for a dependable, hands-on teammate to join our glass tempering production team. This role is a good fit for someone with manufacturing, production, construction, warehouse, equipment, or other physical work experience who takes pride in doing the job right.
Glass experience is not required. We will train the right person on our equipment, process, paperwork, and quality standards. What we need from day one is reliability, attention to detail, urgency, and the willingness to stay productive without someone standing over your shoulder.
This is a physical, fast-moving production environment. Successful teammates learn the machine, understand the process, prepare for the next order, notice quality concerns, and help keep the area moving. Over time, this role develops into a skilled production position involving machine operation, setup, adjustments, process knowledge, and support with equipment care.


This role may be a good fit if you:

  • Show up on time and take attendance seriously.
  • Like hands-on work and staying busy.
  • Take pride in quality and accuracy.
  • Can follow paperwork, measurements, and production instructions.
  • Notice when something looks wrong and speak up.
  • Want to learn equipment, machines, and production processes.
  • Can work without needing constant reminders.
  • Are comfortable with physical work in a manufacturing environment.
  • Want a long-term opportunity with growth and pay progression.

This role is probably not a good fit if you:

  • Prefer a job where you wait for someone to tell you every next step.
  • Are not comfortable with physical production work.
  • Struggle with consistent attendance or being on time.
  • Do not like repetitive work, quality checks, or following detailed instructions.
  • Prefer a slower-paced role without production expectations.
  • Are looking for a position where downtime means standing around.

Responsibilities include:

  • Moving and handling glass safely through the tempering process.
  • Operating and monitoring production equipment.
  • Reading work orders, measurements, and production requirements.
  • Performing quality checks throughout the process.
  • Preparing materials and staging upcoming work.
  • Keeping the work area clean, organized, and production ready.
  • Reporting safety, quality, paperwork, or equipment concerns.
  • Learning machine setup, adjustments, troubleshooting, and basic equipment care over time.

Qualifications:

  • Prior hands-on work experience in manufacturing, production, construction, warehouse, logistics, equipment operation, or a similar environment preferred.
  • Strong attendance and reliability required.
  • Ability to work at a steady production pace.
  • Mechanical aptitude or interest in learning equipment operation preferred.
  • Ability to read a tape measure.
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs. and stand, bend, reach, push, pull, and move throughout the shift.
  • Positive attitude, team mindset, and willingness to learn.

We are looking for teammates who want to build skills, grow with the company, and take pride in their work.

title: Head of DevOps
description:
At Semperis, our mission is to be a Force for Good. Starting with being a great place to work. We believe that when people feel valued, supported, and empowered, they do their best work. That’s why we focus on creating an employee experience rooted in purpose, growth, and balance. Semperis has been recognized as one of America’s Fastest-Growing Cybersecurity Companies by the Inc. 5000, a DUNS 100 Top Startup to Work For, and a multi-year Inc. Best Workplace awardee.

Head of DevOps

We're seeking a Head of DevOps to lead our DevOps function, managing a mix of team leads and individual contributors across a global organization. This is a senior leadership role for someone who sets technical strategy and organizational direction, while remaining sharp enough technically to dive into a hard problem, challenge an architecture decision, or mentor an engineer through a tough debugging session when it counts.

You'll own the DevOps roadmap and org structure, and be the escalation point for both people challenges and the toughest technical ones.

What You Will Be Doing

Organizational Leadership

  • Manage a team of managers and senior ICs, setting the org structure and growth plan for the DevOps function as it scales

  • Own hiring, performance management, and career development for both direct reports and, through them, the broader team

  • Coach team leads on how to manage their own people and technical decisions, rather than managing every engineer directly

  • Decide when to delegate ownership to a lead versus when to step in personally

Strategy & Technical Direction

  • Own the DevOps roadmap, translating business and product priorities into infrastructure and delivery capabilities

  • Set technical direction for cloud architecture, CI/CD, and platform reliability across Azure, Kubernetes (AKS), Istio, and GitOps workflows

  • Make tooling, budget, and build-vs-buy decisions for the function

  • Define KPIs, SLAs, and error budgets that connect infrastructure performance to business outcomes

Deep Technical Involvement

  • Get personally involved in the hardest technical challenges — critical incidents, contentious architecture decisions, persistent systemic issues — where your experience changes the outcome

  • Review code, infrastructure, and architecture decisions at a level of detail that gives real feedback, not rubber-stamp approval

  • Lead root-cause analysis on major incidents and drive long-term fixes

  • Mentor senior engineers and team leads directly on technical problem-solving, not just process

Leading Change

  • Identify friction in current workflows and lead the initiatives to resolve it, from diagnosis through adoption

  • Drive adoption of practices like GitOps maturity, Zero Trust, and observability standards across the org

  • Build change management capability into your leads so improvements scale without your constant involvement

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Serve as the primary bridge between DevOps and Engineering, Security, IT, and Product leadership

  • Partner with Security and Compliance on Zero Trust, PIM/RBAC, and WAF strategy and implementation

  • Represent DevOps in executive and cross-functional planning, backed by real technical credibility

  • Broker tradeoffs between teams with competing priorities

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of DevOps/SRE experience in SaaS or cloud-native environments

  • 4+ years in a senior leadership role, including direct experience managing managers or team leads, not just ICs

  • Strong hands-on background with Terraform/Terragrunt, Kubernetes (AKS), Helm, and Istio, with enough depth to review and challenge technical decisions directly

  • Track record of leading organizational change initiatives from strategic framing through execution

  • Proven ability to mentor senior engineers and develop other managers

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, particularly with Security and Product leadership

  • Experience with Zero Trust architecture, PIM/RBAC, and secure network configuration in Azure

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience scaling a DevOps or platform function through a management layer (i.e., building out team leads under you)

  • Experience with Kafka, event-driven systems, and distributed systems architecture

  • Background in identity, security, or compliance-heavy SaaS products

  • Experience presenting technical strategy to executive audiences

  • History of building internal platforms or tools adopted by other engineering teams

Why Join Semperis?
You’ll be part of a global team on the front lines of cybersecurity innovation. At Semperis, we celebrate curiosity, integrity, and people who take initiative. If you’re someone who sees the glass as half full, embraces challenges as growth opportunities, and values a healthy balance between work and life—we’d love to meet you.

**Semperis maintains office locations in several cities across the globe. Where the job description specifies a required location, candidates will follow our hybrid work model. This includes working up to three days per week and remotely the remaining days.

The information collected by the Semperis application is solely to determine suitability for employment, verify identity, and maintain employment statistics.

Applicants with disabilities may be entitled to reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act and/or other applicable state or local laws. A reasonable accommodation is a change in the way things are normally done which will ensure an equal employment opportunity without imposing undue hardship on Semperis. Position Summary:

Primarily focused on the management, coordination, and continual improvement of the Service Desk, Desktop Support, endpoint support, and related IT Service Management processes, the Service Desk Manager is a member of the Information Technology leadership team and plays a key role in the delivery of reliable technology support across Firelands Health. The position requires strong leadership, superior communication, sound judgment, and the ability to build effective relationships with clinical, operational, administrative, technical, and vendor partners. The person in this role plans, directs, and evaluates functions associated with Service Desk and Desktop Support, maintains a 24-hour, 7 day per week support operation, and ensures that service delivery practices support organizational priorities, patient care operations, cybersecurity expectations, and customer satisfaction. The Service Desk Manager leads subordinate staff, coordinates internal and external resources, manages service performance, supports hardware and software lifecycle needs, provides advanced escalation support, and generates and maintains appropriate documentation. Subject to call by stand-by staff.

What you will do:

  • Works collaboratively with Information Technology leaders, team members, clinical leaders, operational leaders, vendors, and business partners to assess, define, and continually improve Information Technology services, support capabilities, processes, and procedures.
  • Manages, optimizes, and leads the evolution of Service Desk and Desktop Support practices in alignment with IT Service Management principles and the ITIL framework, including incident management, request fulfillment, problem management, knowledge management, service level management, and change management support.
  • Plans, directs, coordinates, and evaluates the daily operations of the Service Desk and Desktop Support teams, ensuring adequate staffing, scheduling, on-call coverage, and support readiness for a 24-hour, 7 day per week healthcare environment.
  • Serves as the management escalation point for Service Desk and Desktop Support incidents, requests, complaints, and operational concerns; provides Level-4 Service Desk support and clear guidance to staff and system users when needed.
  • Reviews Service Desk metrics, ticket queues, customer feedback, call trends, first-contact resolution, aging tickets, recurring issues, service levels, and user satisfaction results; implements improvements that strengthen service quality, accountability, and customer experience.
  • Builds a functional, accountable, and customer-focused team; manages, mentors, motivates, and empowers Service Desk and Desktop Support staff to use best practices, demonstrate ownership, and provide consistent service excellence.
  • Evaluates employee performance; counsels and disciplines employees as appropriate; develops orientation, onboarding, continuing education, cross-training, and skill development plans for Service Desk and Desktop Support staff.
  • Coordinates hiring, onboarding, training, workload assignment, and performance expectations for Service Desk and Desktop Support staff; recommends applicants for hire in accordance with Human Resources and departmental procedures.
  • Ensures proper use and continual improvement of support tools, ticketing systems, knowledge bases, endpoint management tools, remote support tools, call handling processes, and documentation standards.
  • Manages, monitors, and reports on endpoint support and inventory status for assigned technology assets, including workstations, laptops, tablets, printers, scanners, phones, mobile devices, POS systems, A/V equipment, televisions, and patient or nurse communication tools as applicable.
  • Coordinates hardware procurement, deployment, replacement, maintenance, disposal planning, and vendor support activities for end-user and endpoint technology in partnership with other IT leaders and established purchasing processes.
  • Supports cybersecurity, privacy, and compliance expectations by ensuring Service Desk procedures follow approved standards for identity verification, access requests, endpoint support, incident escalation, documentation, least privilege, protection of confidential information, and appropriate use of approved artificial intelligence or automation tools.
  • Supports the responsible use of approved artificial intelligence, automation, and analytics tools within Service Desk and Desktop Support operations, including ticket routing, knowledge management, reporting, documentation, and support process improvement, while ensuring compliance with organizational policies, cybersecurity standards, privacy requirements, and human review expectations.
  • Participates in change management and supports the IT Change Advisory Board process as assigned; ensures Service Desk readiness for planned changes, go-lives, downtime events, service transitions, communication plans, and after-action follow-up.
  • Uses resources efficiently; tracks and reports progress on active work and assigned projects; manages concurrent priorities and coaches team members on effective work management, communication, documentation, and project support practices.
  • Serves as a liaison between users and technical personnel; manages user expectations, communicates service impacts clearly, and cultivates feedback for service, system, workflow, and support improvements.
  • Seeks and utilizes feedback from users, leaders, and team members to improve customer satisfaction, reduce repeat issues, strengthen knowledge content, and improve the support experience.
  • Puts organizational goals ahead of personal goals; manages fluctuations in work and schedule requirements effectively; demonstrates initiative, cooperation, sound judgment, and professional conduct.

What you will need:

Bachelor's degree in related field and three (3) years of equivalent experience, or Associate's Degree in related field and five (5) years of equivalent work experience, or seven (7) years of equivalent work experience required. Prior leadership, supervisory, or team lead experience in an IT support environment is preferred.

ITIL Foundation, HDI, CompTIA A+, Network+, Security+, Project+, Microsoft, or other comparable manager-approved certifications are preferred or may be required within a defined period based on departmental needs. Certifications required by the department must remain valid.

Demonstrates willingness, ability, and availability to attend leadership, technical, service management, cybersecurity, compliance, or other training as requested by the AVP, Information Technology or designee.

Detail and result oriented with strong leadership, coaching, delegation, decision-making, conflict resolution, and performance management skills.

Demonstrates advanced knowledge of IT Service Management frameworks and processes, including ITIL-based incident management, request fulfillment, problem management, change management, knowledge management, service catalog concepts, metrics, and continual improvement.

Demonstrates knowledge of basic project management and the ability to manage assigned initiatives, service transitions, go-live support needs, and concurrent operational priorities.

Demonstrates advanced troubleshooting judgment and the ability to coach others through structured problem solving, root cause identification, documentation, and appropriate escalation.

Demonstrates knowledge of healthcare technology environments and the ability to support clinical, administrative, business, and patient care operations with appropriate urgency and professionalism.

Demonstrates knowledge of computer systems and procedures, endpoint hardware, peripherals, mobile devices, printers, scanners, A/V equipment, communications tools, data handling, information management principles, and support documentation practices.

Demonstrates awareness of cybersecurity, privacy, access control, endpoint protection, phishing, social engineering, and incident escalation practices appropriate to the Service Desk function.

Demonstrates awareness of artificial intelligence, automation, and machine-learning-enabled tools as they relate to IT support, user assistance, knowledge management, productivity, cybersecurity risk, privacy, data protection, and responsible technology use in a healthcare environment.

Demonstrates initiative and the ability to work in a stressful environment, adapt to changing priorities, and make timely decisions that support patient care and organizational operations.

Demonstrates ability to grasp new and technical concepts quickly and stay current with technology.

Demonstrates analytical abilities, creativity, attentiveness to detail, and the ability to identify trends, service gaps, and improvement opportunities from data and user feedback.

Demonstrates ability to communicate effectively in both written and oral form with staff, peers, leaders, physicians, vendors, and end users at all levels of the organization.

Demonstrates ability to use computer systems, computer workstations, support tools, ticketing systems, productivity software, reporting tools, and related technology.

title: Director, Project Management
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Director of Project Management provides director-level leadership for FCS project management operations and portfolio governance. This role sets project management standards, directs the work of project management staff, oversees agency-level project execution, and ensures projects are aligned with organizational priorities, quality expectations, and available capacity. The Director has authority to guide project intake, prioritization, resource planning, risk escalation, reporting practices, and adoption of agency project management tools and processes. This position owns the PMO operating model and governance expectations while holding project teams accountable for consistent execution, timely communication, and completion of approved deliverables.

POSITION SPECIFIC DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Establish and maintain agency project management standards, governance expectations, templates, and lifecycle practices for agency-level projects.
  • Direct portfolio intake, prioritization, and resource planning in partnership with senior leadership to align project work with organizational goals and capacity.
  • Supervise, mentor, and evaluate project management staff; assign project work, monitor caseload balance, and support professional development.
  • Provide oversight and approval of project charters, scopes, work plans, risk plans, change control, status reporting, and closeout documentation for assigned projects.
  • Make director-level decisions within delegated authority regarding project approach, escalation timing, resource tradeoffs, and cross-department coordination; escalate issues with agency-wide impact to the VP/EVP/ELT as appropriate.
  • Lead cross-functional steering groups, workgroups, and stakeholder discussions to clarify decision rights, resolve barriers, and maintain accountability for project outcomes.
  • Monitor portfolio performance, KPIs, dependencies, risks, issues, and benefits realization; direct corrective action when project performance deviates from approved plans.
  • Drive implementation and monitor fidelity of project management governance across the agency, with specific accountability for consistent use of Asana or other approved project management software.

The Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) is seeking a Petrochemicals Analyst in India. This role will focus on the economic, financial and market aspects of the petrochemical industry in India and assist the team in accelerating a just transition from oil and gas in alignment with climate commitments, with an immediate freeze on the build-up of petrochemical infrastructure.

We are looking for an experienced economics and financial professional with sound knowledge of the petrochemical sector in India with preferred hands-on experience in financial analysis. They would be self-motivated, able to work independently, able to multi-task, set priorities and meet deadlines with limited direction while working remotely. They must also possess a commitment to IEEFA’s mission to accelerate the transition to a diverse, sustainable and profitable energy economy.

IEEFA is a rapidly-growing NGO/nonprofit that conducts research and analysis on financial and economic issues related to energy markets, trends and policies. Headquartered in the United States, IEEFA has a team of 70+ analysts and communications personnel located in 15 countries across the globe. IEEFA produces a significant volume of original research, as well as ongoing analysis and reports on issues affecting energy industries. Our major research reports, daily analysis, press coverage and other resources can be found on our website: .

  • Prepare forecasts and analysis of trends in the Indian agrochemical and textile sectors within the petrochemical
  • Collects economic data from established datasets and other sources, utilizing data collection and data science protocols
  • Utilizes statistical analysis and mathematical methodologies to develop data
  • Engage with relevant external stakeholders (e.g. regulators, banking institutions, investors, MDB’s) in India and abroad, and represent IEEFA at meetings
  • Collaborate with team members and work independently to research and write original, compelling, and professional reports and commentaries on India’s petrochemical industry
  • Drafting, formatting and proofing reports, submissions, press releases and presentations
  • Other duties as assigned

Knowledge and Skill Requirements

  • 2-4 years’ experience in economics / finance including at least two years of experience related to the petrochemical industry (agrochemicals) of India
  • A bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, public policy
  • Comprehensive experience analysing the industry growth’s impact on the economy, financial reporting, stocks, and investment portfolios
  • Proficient understanding of finance, public policy and quantitative analysis.
  • Understanding of policy and regulatory landscape in the petrochemical industry, with a focus on India
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, demonstrated through publications, reports, commentaries and liaising with regulators/ government stakeholders
  • High degree of technological proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, and demonstrated ability to learn new software and applications
  • Commitment to IEEFA’s mission to accelerate the transition to a diverse, sustainable, and profitable economy

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge and experience of ammonia and agrochemical sectors.

Full-time 12-month fixed-term employment contract with the option of extension by mutual agreement and a market competitive remuneration. Pay rates are also based on education, skill, experience level and internal equity.

About this role

Women in Recovery (WIR) Therapist provides direct, gender-specific individual and group counseling, family and relationship counseling services within a day treatment format to participants; with emphasis on recovery from substance abuse, role-modeling, women only groups, trauma, health and wellness, parenting and family reunification. Therapist maintains and cultivates relationships with external agencies, such as court personnel, ancillary service providers, referring agencies, etc.

Why you'll love this role

Women in Recovery (WIR) is an intensive outpatient alternative for eligible women facing long prison sentences. Therapist works closely with the criminal justice system and various community partners to ensure WIR program participants receive supervision, substance abuse and mental health treatment, education, workforce readiness training and family reunification services. This program changes lives but also carries far reaching benefits such as strengthening individuals and whole families that has lasting impact for generations, breaks the cycle of intergenerational incarceration and helps women become productive and responsible citizens.

WIR Therapists engage in helping women conquer their drug addiction, recover from trauma and acquire the essential economic, emotional and social tools to build successful and productive lives. WIR is designed for women who are dedicated to changing their lives and becoming positive, contributing members of our community.

Therapist requirements

  • A master's degree in social work, Counseling Psychology or its equivalent from an accredited school.
  • Knowledge and experience in individual, group and family therapy.
  • Must have or be under supervision as a Licensed Alcohol and Drug Counselor or have drug/alcohol treatment experience.
  • Knowledge and experience in conducting mental health assessment, diagnosis and treatment planning.
  • Must demonstrate a clinical family systems orientation, competency about motivational interviewing, stages/process of change, the elements of the stages/phases of recovery, and ability to work with diverse populations with multiplicity of problems.
  • Experience working with court systems and gender-specific treatment a plus.
  • Must possess a valid Driver License and satisfactory driving record and use personal automobile to travel to locations other than primary office. [Mileage reimbursement provided*]

CCBHC Model of Care

Family & Children’s Services works to heal hurting and abused children, strengthen families, and provide hope and a path to recovery for those battling mental illness and addiction. You will be working in an innovative and dynamic environment using a new transformative model of care Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC). This model is characterized by innovative, team-based approach and whole person care for adults and children with a range of complex mental health and substance use challenges.

Utilizing multi-disciplinary teams, staff work collaboratively to provide a coordinated effort to enhance client recovery. Robust CCBHC services often result in better client outcomes and quality of care due to:

  1. Increased access to care and crisis services
  2. Expanded traditional community mental health and substance use services.
  3. Added Care Coordination and physical health screening for mental health clients
  4. Greater access to Social Services for clients’ economic and social needs
  5. Increased specialized services for veterans, those most in need, and those impacted by the opioid crisis.

Possession of a medical marijuana license will not exclude any therapist applicant; however, all employees are subject to the Family & Children’s Services Drug Free Workplace Policy.

The Engineering Technician may work in indoor and outdoor test areas, test stands, laboratories, chambers, machine shops, cold and hot weather environments, heights, and confined spaces. They may work with or around Cryogenics (Liquid Hydrogen, Liquid Oxygen, Liquid Nitrogen, Liquid Helium), Gaseous Hydrogen, Gaseous Oxygen, Gaseous Nitrogen, Gaseous Helium, High Pressure Systems, Hypergols, Solid Propellants, Explosives, Other Toxic, Confined Space, Cleanliness Standards and Operations, Electrical Instrumentation and Controls Systems and Components Associated with Hazardous Operations, Mechanical Systems and Components Associated with Hazardous Operations, Safety Critical Equipment (Lifts, and Moves), Specialized Equipment, Large and/or Complex Facilities, Test Stands, Equipment, Special Test Equipment, and Test Articles, Specialized Handing, Transportation, Operation of One of a Kind Test Articles and Associated Components. Work is reviewed for technical adequacy (or conformity with instructions). (Examples of designs include: detailed circuit diagrams; hardware fittings or test equipment involving a variety of mechanisms; conventional piping systems; and building site layouts).

  • Extract and compille g a variety of engineering data from field notes, manuals, lab reports, etc., processing data, identifying errors or inconsistencies, selecting methods of data presentation.
  • Assist in design modification by compiling data related to design, specifications, and materials that are pertinent to specific items of equipment or component parts; developing information concerning previous operational failures and modifications, and using judgment and initiative to recognize inconsistencies or gaps in data and seek sources to clarify information.
  • Additionally, the position operates in unique, “one of a kind,” and/or hazardous research and test facilities, test stands, laboratories, chambers, equipment, and are required to have highly specialized skills that in many cases can only be obtained through specialized training, “on the job” work experience, and certification(s).

title: Senior devops engineer
description:
Job Description

We are looking for a hands‑on Dev Ops Engineer to operate inside a AWS native banking environment. You will own the build, automation, and operational tooling that delivery teams rely on everyday CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environment provisioning, configuration management, and the developer experience that surrounds them.

This is an engineering role first. You will spend the majority of your time in code and configuration: writing pipelines, building automation, hardening environments, and removing manual toil from the path to production. You will work alongside developers, architects, security engineers, and platform teams to keep delivery flowing reliably inside a regulated, PCI‑DSS environment.

Site Reliability Engineering experience is a strong advantage. You will use it to push the platform further by sharpening observability, improving incident response, reducing failure domains, and embedding resilience patterns into the way services are deployed and run.

What You Will Do Core Dev Ops Engineering Design, build, and maintain CI/CD pipelines that move code from commit to production safely and repeatably across the delivery estate. Automate AWS workload provisioning and configuration deployment using infrastructure as code, with environments that are reproducible, version‑controlled, and auditable. Build and operate the deployment automation, release tooling, and environment management that delivery squads depend on day to day. Harden the developer experience repository templates, pipeline templates, deployment patterns, and self‑service tooling that reduce friction without weakening control. Integrate security and compliance controls into pipelines and infrastructure secrets management, access control, change traceability. Translate business and technical requirements into scalable, automated delivery solutions that align to the AWS Well‑Architected Framework. AWS & Platform Engineering Work hands‑on across an AWS estate, integrating cloud‑native services with on‑premises systems where the banking environment requires it. Build and operate workloads across EC2, RDS (EBS, EKS, ECS, Load Balancing, Secrets Manager, KMS, and Service Catalog). Use AWS CDK as the primary infrastructure‑as‑code tool, with Cloud Formation, Ansible, and scripting languages applied where they fit best. Apply networking fundamentals routing, segmentation, security groups, DNS, TLS, and load balancing to design environments that are both secure and operable. Support the operational lifecycle of platform services the wider engineering organization depends on, including identity, messaging, and application server tiers where present. Site Reliability Advantageous Depth Identify and reduce failure domains across the platform, designing systems that contain blast radius and recover gracefully from partial failure. Apply SRE principles such as SLOs and post‑incident learning to improve reliability, performance, and the team's response to production issues. Enhance observability across environments through stronger monitoring, structured logging, useful alerting, and dashboards that surface what matters during an incident. Troubleshoot and optimize low‑latency, Java‑based applications in production, working alongside application engineers to resolve issues at the system level. Build automation that minimizes business impact during maintenance and failures, and that reduces the operational load carried by delivery teams. Collaboration & Mentorship Contribute as a strong technical voice in a cross‑functional team alongside Architects, Engineers, Business Analysts, Scrum Masters, and Security partners. Mentor engineers across the team on Dev Ops practice, AWS engineering, automation, and where applicable SRE principles through pairing, code review, and worked examples. Drive collaboration across squads, lifting the standard of automation, observability, and operational discipline beyond the immediate team. Champion delivery excellence secure, automated, observable, and repeatable as the default way of working. Requirements Essential Experience 7+ years hands‑on experience in a Dev Ops or SRE role, with a clear weighting toward Dev Ops engineering, automation, and CI/CD delivery. Hands‑on experience in AWS environment, preferably in financial services with PCI‑DSS compliant systems. Demonstrable track record implementing CI/CD pipeline automation across functional areas of a delivery organization. Strong AWS workload automation experience covering infrastructure provisioning and software configuration rollout. Practical experience implementing observability for hybrid and cloud‑based environments. Strong working knowledge of networking principles and protocols. Working understanding of the AWS Well‑Architected Framework and how to apply it in practice. Advantageous Experience Demonstrable experience with Site Reliability Engineering principles and practices in production environments. Troubleshooting low‑latency, Java‑based applications in an SRE context and infrastructure‑level performance investigation. Experience operating inside an audit‑heavy regulated environment beyond PCI‑DSS change control, evidence capture, segregation of duties. Ways Of Working A hands‑on engineer at heart most effective when the work is in pipelines, code, and configuration rather than in process documents. Pragmatic about automation: automates what matters, leaves what doesn’t, and knows the difference. Strong collaborator across engineering, security, and operations, with the ability to translate technical decisions into language non‑engineers can act on. Holds the line on operational and security discipline without becoming a blocker to delivery. Technical and Tooling AWS Services: EC2, RDS, EBS, EKS, ECS, Load Balancing, Secrets Manager, KMS, Service Catalog. AWS CDK. Observability tooling: AWS Cloud Watch, Splunk or App Dynamics, ELK. CI/CD platforms (Harness, Azure Dev Ops, Git Lab, or equivalent). Operating Systems: Linux and Windows Server. Preferred Python scripting. AWS Cloud Formation. Ansible. Bash scripting. Optional Zabbix monitoring. Keycloak. Active MQ. Web Logic 14c. Nginx. Beneficial Certifications AWS Certified Sys Ops Administrator (Cloud Ops Engineer). AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate.

The Operations Logistics Coordinator is a vital role within the hospital. In this position you can expect to collaborate closely with staff on the patient care units, helping with patient placement, transfers, and discharges throughout the facility. The ideal candidate will have health care experience and a familiarity with medical terminology as this is a vital position to our patient satisfaction.

This is a PRN Varied Shift position where you will be covering shifts as needed to help fill the department need.

Banner Wyoming Medical Center is located in the heart of Casper Wyoming. As the state's largest inpatient facility, Wyoming Medical Center is known and highly regarded for its cardiac and stroke services. With 249 beds and a level 2 trauma center, Wyoming Medical Center is proud to serve the entire state of Wyoming.

POSITION SUMMARY
This position is responsible for the coordination of internal movement of patients throughout Banner acute care facilities. The Operations Logistics Coordinator will be assigned a hospital or multiple hospitals each shift, in which they coordinate with the internal stakeholders of these facilities to procure patient bed assignments for patients coming from the Emergency Department, procedural areas, transfers from other facilities & from home, as well as the internal movement of patients when status changes occur. This position requires systems thinking, the ability to manage many conflicting priorities, excellent communication skills and proficiency with multiple computer applications. Serves as a liaison between both internal and external customers as well as providing ongoing support to the house supervisor of the hospitals to implement their throughput plan. Manages data as related to operations. Performs Utilization Management functions as required by the system.

CORE FUNCTIONS
1. Acts in conjunction with the house supervisor to manage daily throughput and support the command center for the hospital through surge management. Coordinates with internal personnel of the hospital such as staffing representative, unit leaders & procedural area leaders to manage patient movement. Coordinates with external personal responsible for transferring patient into the hospital from outside agencies to ensure timely acceptance. Maintains list of anticipated needs and projects the eb and flow of the hospital to plan throughput and manage resources.

2. Responds to the electronic orders for patient’s placement within the hospital by entering bed assignments into bed placement software timely and correctly. Files and archives completed, and cancelled orders per hospital processes. Completes multiple steps for the placement of each patient including electronic and verbal communications with the necessary stakeholders and updating multiple computer applications. Receives, verifies, and provides ongoing follow-up requests and referrals/orders.

3. Gathers all information for correct patient assignments and verifies accuracy of that information. Seeks clarification when inaccuracies occur. Follows through with resolving inaccuracies, communicates resolution in real time. Unresolved issues are escalated to appropriate nursing leadership for intervention. Prioritizes the safe transition of patients throughout the placement process.

4. Completes and distributes any ad hoc reports which are necessary for patient throughput management and communication. Collects and logs any data which may be requested, and other duties as assigned.

5. Facility based position with possible multi facility-wide impact on patient throughput, resource utilization and the patient experience. Coordinates with multiple stakeholders, manages conflicting priorities in an environment which may be fast paced and demand attention to detail. Efficiently balances requests for patient beds with available resources which may be limited and under tight deadlines. While providing excellent customer service to other Banner employees and providers of patient care and by maintaining excellent communication with impacted patient units.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
High school diploma/GED or equivalent working knowledge.

The position also requires skills and abilities typically gained with 0-2 years of experience in a healthcare office or hospital operations setting, and/or educational background. Must have medical terminology gained by either college credits of experience in a health care setting, excellent verbal and written communication skills, organizational skills and critical thinking skills. Must have the ability to work under tight time constraints and meet deadlines while working on a variety of projects under high demands.

Must be proficient with commonly used office software and equipment including but not limited to all Microsoft applications, hospital EMR and bed placement software.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Associate Degree preferred.

Additional related education and/or experience preferred.

POSITION SUMMARY
This position coordinates a smooth patient flow process by answering phones, scheduling patient appointments, providing registration of patient and insurance information, obtaining required signatures following established processes, procedures and standards. This position also verifies insurance coverage, validates referrals and authorizations, collects patient liability and provides financial guidance to patients to maximize medical services reimbursement efforts. This also includes accurately posting patients at the point of service and releasing information in accordance with organizational and compliance policies and guidelines.

CORE FUNCTIONS
1. Performs registration/check-in processes, including but not limited to performing data entry activities, providing patients with appropriate information and intake forms, obtaining necessary signatures and generating population health summary.

2. Verifies insurance eligibility benefits for services rendered with the payors and documents appropriately. Assists in obtaining or validating pre-certification, referrals, and authorizations

4. Enters payments/charges for services rendered and performs daily payment/charge reconciliation in a timely and accurate manner. Balances cash drawer at the beginning and end of the day and prepares daily bank deposit with necessary paperwork sent to centralized billing for record purposes.

5. Schedules office visits and procedures within the medical practice(s) and external practices as necessary. Maximizes reimbursement by scheduling patients in accordance with payor plan provisions. Confirms patient appointments for the following day as necessary and ensures patients are properly prepared for visits.

6. Demonstrates proactive interpersonal communications skills while dealing with patient concerns through telephone calls, emails and in-person conversations. Optimizes patient flow by using effective customer service/communication skills by communicating to internal and external customers, care team, management, centralized services and HIMS.

7. Assists in responding to requests for patient medical records according to company policies and procedures, and state and federal laws.

8. Provides a variety of patient services to assist in patient flow including but not limited to escorting patients, taking vitals and patient history, assisting in patient treatment, distributing mail and fax information, ordering supplies, etc.

9. Works independently under regular supervision and follows structured work routines. Works in a fast paced, multi-task environment with high volume and immediacy needs requiring independent decision making and sound judgment to prioritize work and ensure appropriateness and timeliness of each patient’s care. This position requires the ability to retain large amounts of changing payor information/knowledge crucial to attaining reimbursement for the services provided. Primary external customers include patients and their families, physician office staff and third party payors.

High school diploma/GED or equivalent working knowledge.

Requires knowledge of patient financial services, financial, collecting services or insurance industry experience processes normally acquired over one or more years of work experience. Requires the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously with minimal supervision and to work independently.

Requires strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills to effectively interact with a wide range of audiences. Strong knowledge in the use of common office software, word processing, spreadsheet, and database software are required.

Employees working at Banner Behavioral Health Hospital, BTMC Behavioral, and BUMG, BUMCT, or BUMCS in a Behavioral Health clinical setting that serves children must possess an Arizona Fingerprint Clearance Card at the time of hire and maintain the card for the duration of their employment. An Arizona Criminal History Affidavit must be signed upon hire. Employees working at Banner Scottsdale Sports Medicine, second floor must possess an Arizona Fingerprint Clearance Card at the time of hire and maintain the card for the duration of their employment.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS


Work experience with the Company’s systems and processes is preferred. Previous cash collections experience is preferred.

Additional related education and/or experience preferred

title: Clinical Counselor
description:
Position Summary

The Clinical Counselor is responsible for providing mental health and substance use disorder treatment services to individuals receiving services through a Kentucky-licensed Behavioral Health Services Organization (BHSO) and Alcohol and Other Drug Entity (AODE). The Clinical Counselor provides assessments, diagnoses, treatment planning, individual therapy, group therapy, family therapy, crisis intervention, and discharge planning in accordance with Kentucky regulations, Medicaid requirements, accreditation standards, and organizational policies.

The Clinical Counselor serves as a member of the interdisciplinary treatment team and supports a recovery-oriented, trauma-informed, person-centered approach to care.

Essential Functions

Clinical Assessment and Diagnosis

  • Conduct biopsychosocial assessments and comprehensive clinical evaluations.
  • Conduct substance use disorder assessments utilizing ASAM Criteria.
  • Complete diagnostic assessments utilizing DSM-5-TR criteria.
  • Assess risk factors including suicide risk, homicide risk, abuse, neglect, exploitation, and safety concerns.
  • Develop clinical recommendations and level-of-care determinations.

Treatment Planning

  • Develop individualized treatment plans with measurable goals and objectives.
  • Review and update treatment plans according to regulatory and payer requirements.
  • Coordinate treatment planning with clients, families, referral sources, and treatment team members.

Counseling and Therapeutic Services

  • Provide individual psychotherapy.
  • Facilitate group counseling and psychoeducational groups.
  • Provide family therapy and family education services.
  • Provide crisis intervention and stabilization services.
  • Deliver evidence-based treatment interventions including:
    • Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)
    • Motivational Interviewing (MI)
    • Solution-Focused Therapy
    • Trauma-Informed Care
    • Relapse Prevention
    • Recovery-Oriented Services

Substance Use Disorder Services

  • Provide outpatient substance use disorder counseling.
  • Provide Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) services as assigned.
  • Coordinate care with Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT) providers.
  • Assist clients with relapse prevention planning and recovery support services.
  • Collaborate with peer support specialists and recovery coaches.

Documentation Responsibilities

  • Complete all documentation within established timeframes.
  • Maintain accurate and complete clinical records.
  • Complete:
    • Assessments
    • Progress Notes
    • Treatment Plans
    • Treatment Plan Reviews
    • Crisis Documentation
    • Group Notes

title: Specialist, Social Media & Graphic Design
description:
The Specialist, Social Media & Graphic Design is responsible for growing and elevating Carnival Cruise Line's trade social media presence across Carnival-owned channels, travel advisor communities, and partner social platforms. As the primary owner of Carnival's Trade Facebook Page, dedicated Travel Advisor Facebook Group, and other trade-facing social channels, this role develops content that informs, engages, and connects with travel advisors while supporting brand announcements, promotions, events, and key trade marketing initiatives. This position owns the trade social media content calendar from planning through execution, identifying content opportunities, creating compelling social content, actively participating in advisor and partner communities, and driving audience growth through both organic and paid social media efforts. Working closely with Trade Marketing leadership, Consumer Marketing, Brand, Creative Services, Sales, Public Relations, and other cross-functional stakeholders, the role helps ensure a consistent and authentic voice while maintaining alignment with Carnival's broader brand campaigns, messaging priorities, and visual standards. Success in this role requires a strong understanding of the travel advisor community and a passion for delivering an engaging and responsive social experience. The position actively interacts with advisors across social platforms, responds promptly to questions and inquiries, and serves as a trusted resource for the community. Strong judgment, proactive thinking, excellent time management, and the ability to anticipate needs and act quickly are essential. Through ongoing analysis of audience feedback, performance metrics, and social media trends, the role continuously identifies opportunities to strengthen relationships, grow audiences, and enhance engagement.

In addition to social media responsibilities, this role serves as a Graphic Designer and creative resource for the Trade Marketing Creative Services team, designing and developing a wide range of marketing assets including social media content, digital advertising, presentations, sales materials, event collateral, email campaigns, and partner marketing communications. A strong portfolio and demonstrated expertise in graphic design and social media campaign management are essential. title: Data Scientist or Senior Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist or Senior Data Scientist

Bristol or London


About us


Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.


We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We ensure that whatever the building, its design is outstanding, and its operations meet the needs of the communities it serves.


We are as committed to providing an environment where everyone can realise their unique potential. So, in joining Hoare Lea, you will experience a business that enriches your knowledge, supports your wellbeing, and welcomes your individuality. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in our 9-day fortnight scheme, thriving community groups, varied social and networking events, and extensive professional and technical development schemes. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, an electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and 25 days of annual leave (increasing with service), alongside flexible and hybrid working.


Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.


About the role


Our multi-disciplinary software, product, and data team serves as a central hub of digital expertise and innovation, supporting projects across the company. We work collaboratively with engineers, consultants and other specialists to use data and technology to solve real-world problems and improve the services we provide to our clients.


We have an opportunity for a Data Analyst/Scientist or Senior Data Analyst/Scientist to play a key role in using data, analytics, statistical methods and data science to generate insight, support decision-making and improve our engineering services.


This is a broad analytical role. You will work across the full lifecycle of a problem: understanding stakeholder needs, exploring and assessing data, identifying appropriate analytical approaches, communicating findings and, where appropriate, developing statistical or machine-learning models or client-ready insights/tools. This is a role for someone who enjoys variety and has a critical eye for finding the right solution for the problem. Sometimes this may be exploratory analysis, a dashboard or a set of clearly defined metrics; in other cases, it may involve forecasting, statistical modelling, machine learning or building/working with AI.


It's an exciting time to join our Digital team. Working alongside a range of specialist engineers and consultants, you will be joining a collaborative, knowledgeable, highly engaged team, and offer a supportive, flexible, and high-performing work culture. In a time where building and energy resilience is ever more important, we are driving forward innovation to make an impact with data and technology.


You will have the opportunity to engage in a variety of high-impact projects, working on challenging problems for some of the UK’s most notable organisations, including the NHS and Oxford University. Our team has recently worked on creating data science-led for managing estates in hospitals, building energy forecasting models, and harnessing data on building performance to create better designed buildings of the future.


In this key and varied role, you can expect to:


  • Work with engineers, consultants, product teams and other stakeholders to understand their needs and translate sometimes ambiguous questions into well-defined analytical problems.
  • Develop and implement data-driven solutions to solve real-world business problems across the company.
  • Use SQL, Python and other analytical tools to investigate datasets, identify trends and relationships, test hypotheses and generate actionable insights.
  • Apply appropriate statistical techniques, forecasting methods, ML and AI approaches where they add value to the problem being solved.
  • Collaborate with the product and software engineering teams to turn analytical work into reusable tools, workflows and data-driven products where appropriate.
  • Develop reproducible and maintainable analytical code, following best practices, including version control, testing, and peer reviews.
  • Contribute to the development of analytical and data science capability across the business by sharing approaches, reusable methods and good practice


About you


To be successful in this role you’ll need:


Essential skills:


  • Experience applying data and analysis to real-world business, engineering or operational problems.
  • Strong analytical problem-solving skills, with the ability to take an initially ambiguous question and determine an appropriate analytical approach.
  • Ability to work on projects independently and own deliverables.
  • Strong proficiency in Python for data manipulation, analysis, visualisation and data science (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn).
  • Proficiency in data querying languages (e.g., SQL). Solid understanding of software engineering best practices (version control, unit testing, code review, etc.).
  • Strong experience with data visualisation frameworks (e.g., PowerBI, Streamlit).
  • Experience applying machine learning and AI, including generative AI, to real-world problems where it provides clear benefit.
  • Familiarity with statistical concepts and their application in data analysis.
  • Solid communication skills, capable of effectively engaging with and presenting findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Understanding of data governance, privacy, responsible AI and other relevant standards.


Desirable skills:


  • Knowledge of the engineering industry and its challenges.
  • Experience with one of the major machine learning frameworks (TensorFlow or PyTorch).
  • Knowledge of mathematical optimisation methods, such as linear, integer or constraint optimisation, and associated tools (e.g. OR-Tools).
  • Experience with MS Fabric or equivalent data warehousing solution.
  • Experience working in a cloud computing environment.
  • Familiarity with containerisation and deployment technologies (e.g., Docker, CI/CD pipelines).


For candidates joining at Senior level, we would additionally expect you to lead more complex or ambiguous analytical projects, shape analytical approaches and overarching priorities, work independently with senior stakeholders, review and support the work of others, and help raise analytical standards across the team.


How to apply


To apply simply complete a CV profile and submit your application.


If shortlisted, one of our recruitment team will be in touch to arrange an introductory call (about 30 minutes) to discuss the role and your experience in more detail. From there, successful candidates will be invited to attend a panel interview, either via Microsoft Teams or in person at one of our offices. We aim to provide feedback at each stage of the process.


Adjustments and accommodations


If there are adjustments or accommodations that we can put in place to help you participate and give your best at any stage of the recruitment process (whether relating to disability, neurodivergence or anything else) please let us know.


Data privacy


We have updated our terms and conditions for candidates, click here to find out more.


Recruitment agencies


We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners who assist us when required. We do not acknowledge speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on the list.

title: VITA Program Manager
description:
VITA Program Manager


Marksbury/Palmer WayPoint Center
400 East Fifth Street
Lexington, KY 40508


Description


The VITA Program Manager provides leadership for United Way of the Bluegrass’s Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program throughout UWBG’s service area. This position oversees the full administration of the program, including site operations, volunteer and Site Coordinator management, IRS grant compliance, quality control, financial oversight, data collection, and performance reporting.


The VITA Program Manager ensures that all program activities comply with IRS Publication 4671, IRS Publication 5683, 2 CFR Part 200, IRS Quality Site Requirements, federal grant allowability requirements, and applicable taxpayer privacy and data-safeguarding standards. The Manager serves as UWBG’s primary liaison to the IRS Grant Program Office and VITA/TCE Territory Office.


This position reports to the Director of Community Impact and works closely with VITA coalition partners, Site Coordinators, volunteers, the Community Investment Systems Coordinator, Finance, Resource Development, Marketing, the Volunteer Center, 2-1-1 Information and Referral, and the Bank On Coalition.


This is an IRS grant-funded position. Continued employment is contingent upon the continuation of the applicable grant funding and United Way of the Bluegrass’s ongoing receipt of those funds. If funding is reduced, delayed, or discontinued, the position may be subject to a reduction in hours, restructuring, or elimination.


Essential Functions


Program Administration and Operations

  • Oversee the administration, growth, and operational success of the VITA program across all UWBG-supported tax preparation sites.
  • Serve as the primary liaison between UWBG and the IRS Grant Program Office and as the primary point of contact for VITA/TCE Territory Office communications.
  • Recruit, train, schedule, and supervise Site Coordinators and volunteer tax preparers during each filing season.
  • Ensure all VITA sites comply with IRS Quality Site Requirements and Title VI nondiscrimination requirements.
  • Ensure all volunteers and employees complete required annual IRS certifications, including Volunteer Standards of Conduct, Intake/Interview and Quality Review, and the certification level appropriate to their assigned roles.
  • Manage site logistics, program supplies, and electronic filing and tax-preparation software administration in coordination with IRS-provided systems.
  • Coordinate with Marketing, the Volunteer Center, and 2-1-1 to promote free tax preparation services and recruit program volunteers.
  • Troubleshoot client, volunteer, and site-level concerns, including requests for off-season taxpayer assistance.
  • Maintain compliance with applicable taxpayer privacy, confidentiality, and data-safeguarding requirements.

Grant Compliance and Financial Management

  • Manage the annual VITA grant application and reporting cycle, including the October 1 through September 30 period of performance, in accordance with IRS Publication 4671.
  • Ensure all grant expenditures comply with the allowable-cost guidance contained in IRS Publication 4671, Appendix B.
  • Confirm that grant-funded expenses are direct, reasonable, properly documented, and incurred solely in support of the VITA program.
  • Maintain required time-and-effort documentation for all non-volunteer employees whose time is charged to the VITA grant.
  • Ensure timesheets and supporting records clearly distinguish VITA program time from time devoted to other duties or programs.
  • Track and document required matching funds and submit matching-fund documentation within established grant deadlines, including within 20 days of the award notice when required.
  • Partner with Finance to prepare accurate and timely SF-425 federal financial reports and Division of Payment Management drawdowns.
  • Ensure ongoing compliance with 2 CFR Part 200, the VITA Grant Terms and Conditions, applicable cost principles, audit requirements, and grant-monitoring obligations.
  • Maintain compliance with the grant’s Civil Rights Section requirements.
  • Maintain clear cost and time-allocation boundaries between VITA-funded activities and adjacent Financial Stability, AFI: Back On Track, or Financial Education and Asset Building programming.
  • Charge Financial Education and Asset Building costs to the VITA grant only when those services are provided in direct connection with VITA service delivery.

Data, Evaluation, and Reporting

  • Ensure the accurate and timely collection, entry, maintenance, and reporting of data for all VITA program activities.
  • Coordinate with the Community Investment Systems Coordinator to maintain complete and accurate program databases and records.
  • Track and report the number of tax returns filed, refunds generated, and Earned Income Tax Credit, Child Tax Credit, and other tax-credit dollars returned to the community.
  • Prepare VITA performance data, program narratives, and impact summaries for the Board, funders, community partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Prepare prior-year performance summaries and other data required for the annual VITA grant application.
  • Maintain organized and complete records to support grant reporting, monitoring, audits, and program evaluation.

Partnerships and Community Representation

  • Build and maintain productive relationships with local financial institutions, community organizations, VITA coalition partners, and participating tax-preparation sites.
  • Represent UWBG’s VITA program at community meetings, coalition events, and other activities as requested.
  • Convene periodic meetings with program partners and Site Coordinators to support planning, troubleshooting, communication, and continuous program improvement.
  • Collaborate with internal departments and external partners to expand access to free tax preparation services throughout UWBG’s service area.
  • Perform other related duties and support special projects as assigned.

title: Data Protection & Privacy Consultant
description:
Data Protection and Privacy Consultant

This is a chance to join a specialist consultancy supporting organisations with their data protection, privacy, risk and governance needs. You’ll play a key role in helping clients turn complex regulatory requirements into practical, business-focused solutions.

Role Overview

  • Location: Hybrid, minimum two days per week in the office
  • Package: £60,000–£70,000
  • Industry: Data Protection, Privacy & Consultancy

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Act as a trusted data protection and privacy advisor, becoming a key point of contact for clients and senior stakeholders.
  • Provide practical advice across UK GDPR, EU GDPR and other applicable international privacy regulations.
  • Lead and support privacy assessments, including DPIAs, PIAs, Legitimate Interest Assessments, legal basis reviews and special category assessments.
  • Help clients develop and maintain effective privacy programmes, governance frameworks, policies, contracts and privacy notices.
  • Deliver engaging training and awareness sessions covering data protection, privacy and emerging areas such as AI governance.
  • Use OneTrust to build, manage and improve privacy management processes, helping clients get maximum value from the platform.
  • Develop and maintain data maps, asset registers and Records of Processing Activities (ROPAs).
  • Assess privacy, data and cyber risks, helping clients establish clear mitigation plans and priorities.
  • Review client compliance positions and turn findings into practical action plans, targets and prioritised improvements.
  • Support the management and reporting of data breaches, including helping clients meet relevant ICO requirements.
  • Advise on data subject rights and access requests, guiding client teams through appropriate responses.
  • Support the creation of data retention schedules aligned with regulatory and business requirements.
  • Assess third-party and supplier risks, helping ensure appropriate standards and controls are in place.
  • Keep clients informed of significant developments in data protection legislation and regulatory guidance, including developments relating to AI.
  • Manage multiple client projects and engagements, keeping delivery, communication and expectations on track.
  • Build strong relationships with client teams, senior management and internal stakeholders, including at MD and C-suite level.
  • Take a consultancy-led approach to understanding different business models and translating their processes into effective privacy solutions.
  • Contribute to wider operational and risk management activities, identifying issues and ensuring appropriate controls are established.

Main Skills Needed

  • Degree-level education with 5+ years’ experience delivering data protection and privacy solutions.
  • Strong practical knowledge of UK and EU GDPR, with an understanding of other international data protection regulations.
  • Proven experience delivering privacy management programmes within organisations or consultancy environments.
  • Strong experience with OneTrust, ideally including relevant certification and hands-on implementation experience.
  • IAPP or equivalent professional certification.
  • Solid understanding of information governance and broader privacy disciplines.
  • Proven experience delivering DPIAs, PIAs, risk assessments and associated remediation activity.
  • Experience creating and maintaining data maps, asset registers and ROPAs.
  • Strong understanding of risk management frameworks and operational risk.
  • Excellent project planning, workload management and stakeholder coordination skills.
  • Confident communicating with senior stakeholders and presenting complex subjects in a clear, accessible way.
  • Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to provide pragmatic advice rather than purely theoretical guidance.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong client management skills, with a proven ability to understand business needs and deliver against expectations.
  • Good understanding of AI technologies, including LLMs, Generative AI and Agentic AI, and their data protection implications.
  • Willingness and ability to travel within the UK, Europe and internationally when required.
  • Leadership, mentoring or coaching experience would be advantageous, particularly where influence is achieved without direct line management.
  • Experience developing business cases, automating DPIAs or working within a private-sector environment would be beneficial.

What’s in It for You

  • A senior consultancy role with genuine exposure to a varied client portfolio.
  • The chance to work on complex privacy, governance, risk and AI-related challenges.
  • Regular interaction with senior decision-makers and business leaders.
  • The opportunity to shape and operationalise privacy programmes using OneTrust.
  • A role where your expertise directly influences client strategy, compliance and business performance.
  • Hybrid working, balanced with valuable face-to-face collaboration.
  • Scope to broaden your consultancy, leadership and subject-matter expertise across an evolving privacy landscape.
