title: Director Clinical Operations - Virtual Health
location: HM Texas Medical Center - Smith Tower
description:
At Houston Methodist, the Director Clinical Operations position is responsible for providing the overall strategic direction for the clinical management of the Specialty Physician Group and Primary Care Group operations. The Director Clinical Operations position will work in conjunction with Physician Organization (PO) executive management to implement and manage efficient clinical workflow, processes and patient safety, clinical education, and quality. As an engaged leader, this position will be responsible for the assessment, implementation, oversight, and expansion of nursing and medical assistant education and provide oversight for centralized clinical support services across the PO. The Director Clinical Operations position will actively participate in the PO's quality committee and contribute to the achievement of institutional goals and objectives. This position will also create standardized performance expectations and training for each clinical job function in the clinic and expand/implement standard operational and clinical metrics to track and monitor performance and competency. The Director Clinical Operations position will facilitate performance improvement activities linked to overall strategic goals of the PO.

The Director position responsibilities include overseeing the activities of the department staff, ensuring quality, productivity, functional excellence, and efficiency to accomplish strategic and operational objectives. In addition, this position is accountable for employee engagement, adequate staffing levels, budget development and compliance, staffing decisions such as hiring and terminating employment, coaching and counseling employees on work related performance, and developing and implementing policies and procedures to ensure a safe and effective work environment. This position also ensures training, monitoring and operations initiatives are implemented which secure compliance with ethical and legal business practices and accreditation/regulatory/government regulations.

FLSA STATUS
Exempt

QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION
  • Master’s degree in business, health care or related field or within six months of completing degree. For internal applicants, if no Master’s degree must obtain within two years; must be enrolled in a degree program at time of transfer/hire.

EXPERIENCE
  • Seven years experience in a clinical setting, two of those years with people management experience.

LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS
Required
  • RN - Registered Nurse - Texas State Licensure - Texas Board of Nursing_PSV Compact Licensure – Must obtain permanent Texas license within 60 days (if establishing Texas residency)

SKILLS AND ABILITIES
  • Demonstrates the skills and competencies necessary to safely perform the assigned job, determined through on-going skills, competency assessments, and performance evaluations
  • Sufficient proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing the English language necessary to perform the essential functions of this job, especially about activities impacting patient or employee safety or security
  • Demonstrates the ability to interact with others in a way that gives them confidence in one’s intentions and those of the organization
  • Ability to use appropriate interpersonal styles and techniques to gain acceptance of ideas or plans; modifying one’s own behavior to accommodate tasks, situations and individuals involved
  • Demonstrates leadership qualities and critical thinking through self-direction initiative and effective interpersonal skills and oral/written communication skills
  • Ability to identify and understand issues, problems and opportunities, comparing data from different sources to draw conclusions; using effective approaches for choosing a course of action or developing appropriate solutions; taking action that is consistent with available facts, constraints and probable consequences
  • Extensive knowledge of regulatory and accreditation agency requirements that impact department; stays abreast of industry changes
  • Demonstrates highly effective communication skills—strong written communications and platform presentation abilities
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment
  • Demonstrates flexibility and adaptability in the workplace
  • Capable of leading teams/facilitating groups, building consensus and garnering highest confidence in professionalism and work product by senior leadership
  • Ability to work under pressure and balance many competing priorities; highly responsive and solution/action oriented
  • Proficiency in spreadsheet, word processing, and presentation software
  • Maintains a positive and supportive attitude and demeanor
  • Professional handling of exposure to confidential/sensitive information
  • Experience in developing and executing clinical education and training programs
  • Experience in managing and tracking adherence to clinical best practices and competency
  • Working knowledge of organizational policies and procedures, medical billing, coding, and insurance coverage


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

PEOPLE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Directs, develops and implements strategic and operational/high level projects and processes either through independent/highly autonomous work or through the facilitation of work teams to enable the effective and efficient completion of objectives.
  • Oversees management of and ensures development for staff to meet overall objectives in terms of quality, service and cost effectiveness. Provides timely guidance and feedback to help others strengthen specific knowledge/skill areas needed to accomplish a task or solve a problem. Directs management responsibilities of selection, scheduling, supervision, retention, and evaluation of employees.
  • Meets or exceeds threshold goal for department turnover and/or system metrics on employee engagement indicators.
  • Provides leadership and communication to maintain a competent and engaged employee group by conducting regular department meetings to review policies and procedures and operational matters, rounding on all employees, completing performance appraisals, conducting new hire feedback sessions, coaching/corrective counseling, and providing recognition/commendations to achieve desired outcomes.
  • Identifies opportunities and takes action to build strategic relationships between one’s area and other areas, teams, departments, and units to achieve business goals. Drives the promotion of teamwork within and between departments; participates and/or leads and facilitates department process improvements as needed.
  • Proactively leads and facilitates interprofessional team’s formation and implementation.
  • Directs nursing service performance improvement activities and actively participates in organizational leadership functions.
  • Directs, plans, and implement orientation and educational programs to promote staff training and development.

SERVICE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Oversees department operations, designated projects, schedules and activities as needed to ensure that goals or objectives are accomplished within the prescribed time frame. Sets priorities and functional standards, giving direction to staff as necessary to ensure the best possible delivery of service and high customer/patient satisfaction.
  • Drives department service standards and activities to impact department and/or system score for patient/customer-based satisfaction, through role modeling and fostering accountability. Serves and actively participates on various entity committees as a voice for the department.
  • Ensures clinical and nursing standards, practices, policies, and procedures are administered in accordance with all applicable laws, regulatory and accreditation requirements and are consistent with current research findings and national professional standards.
  • Develops and leads a system clinical council in the PO that would provide input and support to troubleshoot clinic-based issues.
  • Evaluates and implements new care delivery models in PO, including telemedicine, nurse triage, NP-based clinics, video visits, Corporate clinics, and concierge medicine.
  • Maintains effective, positive communication with department administrators by holding regular monthly meetings, explaining new policies and procedures, seeking input and participation regarding clinical operations.

QUALITY/SAFETY ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Ensures a safe and effective working environment; monitors and/or revises the department safety plan and/or any specific accreditation/regulatory required safety guidelines. Responsible for staff maintenance of credentials and competencies, per accrediting/ licensing agency and/or department guidelines as applicable.
  • Employs a proactive approach in the optimization of safe outcomes and information systems by monitoring and improving the department workflow and enhancing operations, using peer-to-peer accountability and identifying solutions via collaboration. Implements process improvements utilizing tools such as lean principles. Role models situational awareness, using teachable moments to improve safety.
  • Responsible for employee compliance to policies and procedures and performs associated actions upon non-compliance (i.e., licensure/certification compliance, focal point review requirements, disaster plan, in-services, influenza immunization, wage and hour, standard hours, timely termination submission, timely timecard approval, etc.).
  • Develops, implements, and interprets nursing and patient care policies, objectives, and standards for measurement and maintenance of quality clinic care as it relates clinical systems and data analytics platform with the PO.
  • Leads all quality initiatives with the Physician Organization including but not limited to TAPS review, creating polices/procedures to address quality initiatives and work in collaboration with Chief Quality Officer to head committee.
  • Develops clinical standards/measures for clinical support staff to ensure operating at top licensure and competency (MA/nurse assistant, RN, and mid-levels).

FINANCE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Develops and manages department operational and capital budgets, approvals, and ongoing maintenance of the department(s), ensuring operation in a cost-effective manner. Proactively identifies and plans for capital needs related to current equipment and future department projects. Ensures staffing plans and schedules meet department needs that reflect understanding of the importance of cost-effectiveness.
  • Creates department strategies to achieve financial target and staffing needs, through optimizing productivity, supply/resource efficiency, minimizing incidental overtime and overtime percentage, and other areas according to department specifications.
  • Develops, implements, administers, presents, and manages nursing services budget and expense control.
  • Develops a medical equipment purchasing/replacement strategy for all clinics that ensures EMR compatibility and best in class ambulatory equipment is being purchased. Develops a clinic supply management program including pharmaceutical supply orders and management, i.e., vaccines, infusions, drug sample management, pharmaceutical drug rep management.

GROWTH/INNOVATION ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
  • Identifies and implements innovative solutions for practice or workflow changes to improve department, entity or system operations by leading unit projects and/or other department/ system-directed activities. Proactively leads task forces and committees. May represent HM at assigned community or professional organization meetings.
  • Drives change initiatives, maintaining effectiveness when experiencing major changes in work responsibilities or environment; adjusts effectively to work within new work structures, processes, requirements or cultures. Partners effectively with stakeholders as appropriate.
  • Ensures own career discussions occur with appropriate management. Completes and updates the My development plan on an on-going basis. Conducts conversations with staff on their development.
  • Represents clinical practices in health care programs and professional organizations of associates to serve in a public relations capacity and to stimulate professional growth.
  • Researches and evaluates changing market forces and competitive trends to evaluate and develop or revise programs and services provided.


SUPPLEMENTAL REQUIREMENTS
    WORK ATTIRE
    • Uniform: No
    • Scrubs: No
    • Business professional: Yes
    • Other (department approved): No

    ON-CALL*
    *Note that employees may be required to be on-call during emergencies (ie. Disaster, Severe Weather Events, etc) regardless of selection below.
    • On Call* Yes

    TRAVEL**
    **Travel specifications may vary by department**
    • May require travel within the Houston Metropolitan area Yes
    • May require travel outside Houston Metropolitan area Yes



Work Shift:

1 - Day (United States of America)



Job Category:

Non-clinical

Houston Methodist is one of the nation’s leading health systems and academic medical centers. The health system consists of eight hospitals: Houston Methodist Hospital, its flagship academic hospital in the Texas Medical Center, seven community hospitals and one long-term acute care hospital throughout the Greater Houston metropolitan area. Houston Methodist also includes a research institute; a comprehensive residency program; international patient services; freestanding comprehensive care clinics, emergency care and imaging centers; and outpatient facilities. Come lead with us!

Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Together with our partners, we’re helping customers break free from the restrictive, overpriced legacy solutions that hold them back, and blaze forward with the full power of the open cloud in their hands.

Founded in 2007, we scaled the business with less than $3 million in outside funding until 2021, when we did a traditional IPO on the Nasdaq stock exchange. title: Trainer
description:
TMI is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Trainer to deliver industry-aligned, competency-based vocational training across its diploma programs.

The role combines classroom instruction with hands-on training, workplace simulations, practical assessments, and industry-based learning to prepare students for successful employment in Saudi Arabia’s growing tourism and service sectors.

Trainers may support delivery across TMI’s Luxury Hospitality, Food & Beverage, Health & Wellness, and Tourism Security programs, while specialized technical training will be delivered only within the trainer’s demonstrated qualifications, professional expertise, and approved training scope.

The position requires a strong industry background, practical teaching ability, and commitment to developing students’ professional and employability skills in accordance with TVTC requirements and industry expectations.

Key Responsibilities

Training Delivery & Instruction

  • Deliver competency-based vocational training aligned with approved TVTC curricula, program specifications, and learning outcomes.
  • Deliver practical sessions, demonstrations, workshops, role-plays, simulations, and other applied learning activities reflecting authentic workplace environments.
  • Support training delivery across TMI programs according to professional qualifications and approved training scope.
  • Deliver relevant cross-program subjects such as customer service, professional conduct, workplace communication, service excellence, health and safety, teamwork, and employability skills.
  • Integrate current industry practices, standard operating procedures, technology, and service standards into training.
  • Apply appropriate adult-learning and student-centered teaching methodologies.

Practical & Workplace-Based Training

  • Coordinate and supervise on-the-job training (OJT), internships, field visits, and workplace placements.
  • Liaise with relevant employers and industry partners, including hotels, resorts, restaurants, tourism establishments, wellness facilities, and security operations.
  • Monitor student attendance, performance, professionalism, safety practices, and competency development during workplace training.
  • Provide coaching and corrective guidance during practical and workplace-based activities.
  • Serve as an academic–industry liaison during assigned training placements.

Assessment & Student Development

  • Develop and administer practical assessments, observation checklists, workplace tasks, and performance evaluations.
  • Ensure assessments are aligned with approved competency requirements and appropriately documented.
  • Provide timely and constructive feedback and coaching to students.
  • Identify students requiring additional academic, practical, or behavioral support.
  • Support the development and implementation of remedial training plans.
  • Maintain accurate assessment records, student portfolios, attendance records, and training logs.

Curriculum & Training Materials

  • Contribute to the development and review of curricula, lesson plans, practical activities, simulations, assessment tools, and training materials.
  • Ensure training content remains relevant to employer expectations, industry developments, and national workforce priorities.
  • Collaborate with subject-matter specialists when technical expertise outside the trainer’s primary field is required.
  • Participate in curriculum mapping, program reviews, and continuous-improvement activities.
  • Support new program implementation and cohort expansions.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Deliver training in accordance with applicable TVTC requirements, accreditation standards, institutional policies, and approved program documents.
  • Maintain complete and accurate documentation for training delivery, assessment, attendance, practical activities, and industry placements.
  • Support internal and external audits, inspections, moderation activities, and accreditation reviews.
  • Comply with institutional requirements related to health and safety, ethics, confidentiality, and student conduct.
  • Report safety, compliance, or student-welfare concerns through the appropriate channels.

Professional & Institutional Responsibilities

  • Model professional behavior, workplace ethics, service excellence, and appropriate industry standards.
  • Collaborate effectively with program leadership, specialist trainers, support teams, and industry partners.
  • Participate in meetings, professional-development activities, workshops, and institutional events.
  • Maintain current industry knowledge through continuous professional development and industry engagement.
  • Support TMI’s mission of delivering high-quality vocational education aligned with Saudi Vision 2030.


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Hospitality Management, Tourism, Food & Beverage, Culinary Arts, Health & Wellness, Safety or Security Management, or another relevant discipline.
  • The Bachelor’s degree must align with the candidate’s primary area of training responsibility.
  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on industry experience in hospitality, food & beverage, tourism, wellness, safety, security, or a closely related service-sector environment.
  • Practical experience in at least two of TMI’s program areas, or in an operational environment connecting multiple program areas.
  • Advanced spoken and written English proficiency, preferably equivalent to CEFR C1 or above.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct practical instruction, demonstrations, workplace simulations, and student coaching.
  • TVTC Trainer Approval, institutional trainer approval, or eligibility for the approval applicable to the assigned training area.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous teaching or training experience with students, employees, apprentices, or adult learners.
  • Training-of-Trainers (TOT) certification or another recognized teaching, training, or assessment qualification.
  • Experience within luxury hotels, resorts, restaurants, visitor destinations, wellness facilities, or tourism operations.
  • Practical experience across three or more TMI program areas.
  • Relevant professional certifications such as Food Safety, First Aid, Occupational Health & Safety, Security, Wellness, or Hospitality Operations.
  • Experience developing competency-based assessments and practical training materials.
  • Familiarity with Learning Management Systems (LMS), educational technology, and simulation-based training.
  • Arabic-language ability is an advantage.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong practical and operational expertise within the candidate’s primary professional field.
  • Broad understanding of hospitality, tourism, guest service, food & beverage, wellness, and workplace safety environments.
  • Ability to translate real-world industry practices into structured vocational learning.
  • Strong practical teaching, demonstration, assessment, coaching, and classroom-management skills.
  • Excellent English communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong organizational, record-keeping, and documentation capabilities.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively in a multi-program training environment.
  • Cultural awareness and ability to work effectively with students from diverse backgrounds.
  • Professionalism, integrity, adaptability, and a hands-on approach.
  • Strong commitment to student success, safety, training quality, and continuous professional development.

title: Physiatrist
description:

Position Overview
We are seeking a skilled & compassionate Physiatry/Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Physician to join our team as a Staff Physician. This position provides direct patient care to outpatient patients with medical & rehabilitation needs & plays an integral
role in developing & managing individualized rehabilitation plans.

The Staff Physician will collaborate closely with other healthcare providers to assess patients, make appropriate medical decisions, determine rehabilitative treatment pathways & provide ongoing rehabilitation care management to achieve optimal patient outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

* Provide comprehensive outpatient medical & rehabilitation care.

* Assess, evaluate, diagnose & treat patients using evidence-based best practices.

* Develop & implement individualized plans of care based on patient needs & rehabilitation goals.

* Coordinate patient care with other clinic providers, specialists & outside medical offices.

* Provide rehabilitation-related medical services across a variety of diagnostic categories.

* Perform appropriate medical injections, including injections related to injured-worker care.

* Evaluate & manage patients with concussions across a variety of age groups.

* Perform EMG & nerve conduction studies (NCS).

* Interpret electrodiagnostic findings & correlate results with the patient's clinical presentation.

* Complete accurate & timely EMG/NCS reports & related clinical documentation.

* Communicate clinically significant electrodiagnostic findings to appropriate providers & patients when indicated.

* Participate in the care of pediatric patients, as appropriate.

* Manage medical-legal responsibilities, including:

* Preparation of medical narratives & reports.

* Dispositions.

* Expert testimony.

* Collaboration & communication with attorney offices.

* Maintain accurate, thorough & timely medical records.

* Collaborate with the interdisciplinary care team to support quality outcomes & continuity of care.

* Stay current with PM&R best practices, clinical guidelines & applicable regulatory requirements.

Qualifications

title: Director of Enterprise Architecture - Information Technology
description:
Alberta Blue Cross® is an Alberta based organization dedicated to delivering exceptional customer experience and community leadership. We’re committed to providing the best health coverage to over 1.8 million members and take an active role in promoting wellness. We believe in what we do—and place trust in our employees to deliver our vision.


Working at Alberta Blue Cross® means having a career where you’ll be recognized for your contributions. We value diversity, encourage our team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance and provide opportunities for career growth.

OVERVIEW:

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director of Enterprise Architecture to provide senior enterprise architecture leadership for Alberta Blue Cross. Reporting to the Chief Architect, the Director of Enterprise Architecture leads and operates the Enterprise Architecture function, provides people leadership to Domain Architects, and plays a key role in EA governance. The role translates enterprise architecture strategy and executive direction into practical operating practices, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, compliance measures, and governance outcomes across the organization.

This senior leadership role establishes and matures the enterprise architecture framework that enables strategy execution, modernization, disciplined investment, risk management, and consistent decision-making across portfolios and domains. The role works closely with business, technology, security, privacy, risk, finance, EPMO, portfolio, solution, and domain architecture stakeholders to ensure enterprise architecture guidance is clear, credible, actionable, and consistently applied. The Director of Enterprise Architecture advises senior leaders by translating complex architectural implications into clear options, risks, dependencies, and recommendations that balance business outcomes, cost, complexity, resiliency, compliance, and long-term sustainability.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture is a senior people leadership and architecture governance role focused on enterprise-wide architecture direction, architecture discipline, domain alignment, and executive decision support. The role directly leads Domain Architects and coordinates federated design authority across business, data and AI, application, integration, cloud, security, identity, experience, and technology domains.

Success in this role is achieved by:

  • Operating and maturing the enterprise architecture function in alignment with IT strategy, EA mandate, governance expectations, and executive decision-making needs.

  • Setting and enforcing enterprise-level architecture principles, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, compliance expectations, and governance practices across domains and portfolios.

  • Providing people leadership, coaching, performance support, and prioritization guidance for Domain Architects as direct reports.

  • Establishing architecture as a trusted advisory and governance function with clear OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, and value indicators.

  • Driving coherent, reusable, resilient, secure, compliant, and sustainable architecture decisions across the enterprise.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

  • Lead and operate the Enterprise Architecture function, ensuring architecture practices, standards, governance forums, and decision processes are consistently applied across the organization.

  • Set, evolve, and steward enterprise architecture principles, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, compliance expectations, and governance practices that guide enterprise-wide decisions.

  • Translate corporate strategy, business priorities, technology trends, regulatory expectations, and enterprise risks into actionable architecture guidance.

  • Chair, guide, or support senior architecture governance forums, including decision rights, review processes, compliance expectations, escalation paths, and transparent decision records.

  • Establish and monitor enterprise architecture OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, and value indicators to demonstrate adoption, effectiveness, risk reduction, and enterprise value.

  • Develop and steward enterprise reference architectures that guide business, information, application, integration, cloud, security, identity, data, AI, experience, and technology decisions.

  • Provide enterprise architecture oversight for major programs, platforms, partnerships, modernization initiatives, and strategic investments.

  • Partner with Portfolio Architects to ensure portfolio target architectures and modernization roadmaps align to enterprise strategy, principles, reference architectures, guardrails, and governance expectations.

  • Lead Domain Architects as direct reports, providing coaching, prioritization guidance, performance support, role clarity, and alignment across domain-specific design authority.

  • Coordinate Domain Architects so federated design authority remains aligned to enterprise direction while avoiding duplication with business, data, security, digital, delivery, and operations teams.

  • Identify enterprise-level architectural risks, duplication, fragmentation, technical debt, capability gaps, and architectural drift, and recommend priorities for leadership action.

  • Advise senior business and technology leaders on architecture options, risks, dependencies, enterprise implications, and recommended courses of action in clear business terms.

  • Escalate unresolved cross-domain conflicts, material exceptions, or enterprise-level trade-offs through formal governance forums as appropriate.

POSITION SCOPE:

  • Reports to the Chief Architect and leads the operational execution, EA governance, and people leadership of the Enterprise Architecture function.

  • Provides enterprise-wide architecture discipline, domain alignment, and governance practices that guide strategic technology decisions.

  • Owns enterprise architecture principles, reference architectures, guardrails, standards, governance practices, OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, and architecture effectiveness reporting.

  • Provides direct leadership, coaching, prioritization guidance, performance support, and development for Domain Architects, who report to the Director of Enterprise Architecture.

  • Works across senior business, technology, security, privacy, risk, finance, EPMO, portfolio, solution, domain architecture, delivery, and operations stakeholders.

  • Acts as a trusted senior advisor to business and technology leaders by shaping enterprise technology direction, risk visibility, investment confidence, and strategic decision quality.

  • Provides senior architecture oversight and governance for major enterprise decisions, while remaining distinct from initiative-level solution design, delivery-team management, and operational execution.

ACCOUNTABILITY BOUNDARIES AND ROLE CLARITY:

The Director of Enterprise Architecture reports to the Chief Architect and is accountable for leading, operating, and maturing the Enterprise Architecture function, including playing a key role in EA governance. The role translates enterprise architecture strategy into clear operating practices, governance forums, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, compliance measures, and domain-level execution.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture provides direct people leadership for Domain Architects and is accountable for ensuring domain-specific design authority is coordinated, consistent, and aligned to enterprise direction. Domain Architects remain federated design authorities for their areas of specialty, including business, data and AI, experience, application, integration and API, cloud, security, identity, and technology architecture. This role ensures these domain accountabilities operate as one coherent enterprise capability rather than as isolated specialty functions.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture does not replace or duplicate Portfolio Architect accountabilities. Portfolio Architects own portfolio target architectures, transition states, and 2–3 year modernization roadmaps. They translate enterprise direction into portfolio-specific sequencing, investment alignment, roadmaps, and architecture runway priorities. The Director of Enterprise Architecture governs the enterprise architecture framework within which those portfolio decisions are made and ensures cross-portfolio consistency, standards compliance, and escalation of enterprise-level risks.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture does not replace or duplicate Solution Architect accountabilities. Solution Architects own initiative-level solution architecture and design within approved enterprise and portfolio guardrails. The Director of Enterprise Architecture clarifies standards, decision constraints, exception paths, and governance expectations so solution decisions remain aligned to the approved enterprise and portfolio target states.

This separation of accountabilities ensures clear decision rights: the Director of Enterprise Architecture leads the EA function, governance model, domain architecture capability, and people leadership; Portfolio Architects translate enterprise direction into portfolio roadmaps; Domain Architects provide federated design authority; and Solution Architects design delivery-ready solutions within approved guardrails.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

  • Lead, operate, and mature the Enterprise Architecture function, including playing a key role in EA governance, in alignment with the enterprise architecture mandate and executive direction.

  • Own the enterprise architecture operating model, principles, reference architectures, guardrails, governance practices, standards, compliance expectations, and architecture effectiveness measures.

  • Provide direct people leadership for Domain Architects, including coaching, prioritization guidance, performance support, development planning, and coordination of domain-level work.

  • Maintain enterprise architecture OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, decision records, and executive-level reporting that demonstrate value, adoption, governance effectiveness, and risk reduction.

  • Ensure architecture governance is pragmatic, transparent, authoritative, and consistently applied across portfolios, domains, major initiatives, and enterprise decision forums.

  • Provide enterprise architecture oversight for major platform, modernization, integration, cloud, security, data, AI, identity, experience, and application decisions with organization-wide implications.

  • Promote consistency, reuse, interoperability, security, compliance, resiliency, cost discipline, and long-term sustainability across enterprise solutions.

  • Identify architectural risks, gaps, duplication, capability constraints, technical debt, and cross-domain conflicts, and guide senior leadership on enterprise-level remediation priorities.

  • Facilitate architecture decision-making across Portfolio Architects, Solution Architects, Domain Architects, delivery teams, business leaders, and enterprise stakeholders without assuming their distinct delivery, roadmap, or solution design accountabilities.

  • Partner with executive, business, and technology leaders to embed architecture-by-design into strategy, planning, investment, governance, and delivery decisions.

  • Escalate unresolved enterprise architecture conflicts, material exceptions, and strategic trade-offs through formal governance forums.

KEY SUCCESS MEASURES:

  • Enterprise architecture principles, guardrails, standards, reference architectures, and governance practices are adopted and consistently used to guide major decisions.

  • Architecture OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, and executive reporting demonstrate measurable adoption, quality, risk reduction, governance effectiveness, and enterprise value.

  • Domain Architects are aligned, effective, well-led, and operating as a coordinated enterprise capability with clear priorities, accountabilities, and development support.

  • Portfolio, domain, and solution architecture decisions are materially better aligned to enterprise direction, strategic priorities, reference architectures, and approved guardrails.

  • Reduced architectural fragmentation, duplication, unmanaged complexity, avoidable technical debt, and enterprise risk exposure across domains and portfolios.

  • Senior business and technology leaders view enterprise architecture as a credible, strategic, practical, and trusted advisory and governance function.

  • Enterprise architecture guidance enables business outcomes, regulatory compliance, resiliency, modernization, cost discipline, and long-term sustainability.

  • Role boundaries between the Chief Architect, Director of Enterprise Architecture, Portfolio Architects, Domain Architects, Solution Architects, and delivery leaders are clear and consistently understood.

WHAT YOU WILL HAVE:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience; advanced education is considered an asset.

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise architecture, technology strategy, business architecture, solution architecture, domain architecture, or senior technology leadership roles.

  • Demonstrated success establishing or maturing enterprise architecture operating models, principles, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, governance practices, and compliance measures in complex organizations.

  • Proven people leadership experience, including leading, coaching, aligning, developing, and performance-supporting senior architecture talent or comparable senior specialist teams.

  • Experience defining and reporting architecture OKRs, KPIs, compliance expectations, risk indicators, decision records, and enterprise value measures.

  • Senior-level understanding of business, information, application, integration, data, AI, cloud, security, identity, infrastructure, experience, and technology architecture domains.

  • Proven ability to work with senior business leaders as a trusted advisor on strategic architecture decisions, investment implications, enterprise risks, trade-offs, and technology direction.

  • Experience influencing enterprise planning, portfolio management, EPMO, Finance, risk, security, privacy, legal, delivery, and operations decisions through clear architecture guidance.

  • Demonstrated ability to clarify decision rights and role boundaries across enterprise, portfolio, domain, solution, delivery, and operations accountabilities.

  • Exceptional executive communication, facilitation, governance, negotiation, stakeholder management, and decision-framing skills.

COMPETENCY MATRIX:

Enterprise Architecture Stewardship

  • Description: Leads the enterprise architecture function, operating model, principles, reference architectures, guardrails, governance practices, and compliance expectations.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Adopted architecture standards, principles, governance outcomes, and compliance reporting across portfolios and domains.

People Leadership

  • Description: Leads, coaches, aligns, develops, and performance-supports Domain Architects as direct reports.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Domain Architects operate as a coordinated enterprise capability with clear priorities, role clarity, and consistent delivery of domain guidance.

Governance & Compliance

  • Description: Maintains architecture OKRs, KPIs, controls, decision rights, formal governance paths, exception processes, and compliance expectations.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Transparent governance reporting, clear decision records, improved adherence to enterprise guardrails, and timely escalation of material exceptions.

Strategic Thinking

  • Description: Connects enterprise strategy, investment priorities, architecture direction, risk posture, and long-term sustainability.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Executive decision support, enterprise architecture direction, strategic trade-off recommendations, and enterprise-level risk insight.

Collaboration & Influence

  • Description: Leads through influence across federated architecture, business, technology, EPMO, Finance, risk, security, privacy, delivery, and operations stakeholders.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Aligned decisions across Portfolio Architects, Domain Architects, Solution Architects, and senior stakeholders.

Role Clarity & Decision Framing

  • Description: Clarifies accountability boundaries across enterprise, portfolio, domain, solution, delivery, and operations roles.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Reduced role overlap, clearer escalation paths, more consistent governance outcomes, and stronger stakeholder understanding.

Communication

  • Description: Translates complex enterprise architecture considerations into clear options, recommendations, decisions, and executive-ready materials.

  • Proficiency Level: Advanced

  • Evidence: Clear executive materials, architecture decisions, stakeholder alignment, and improved confidence in enterprise architecture guidance.

BEHAVIORAL INDICATORS:

Strategic Thinking

  • Anticipates enterprise impacts and downstream implications of architecture principles, standards, and governance decisions.

  • Balances strategic ambition, modernization, compliance, risk, cost, and long-term sustainability.

Leadership

  • Provides credible enterprise architecture leadership and trusted advisory support to senior leaders in areas of ambiguity, competing priorities, cross-domain tension, and organizational change.

  • Leads Domain Architects as direct reports by setting clear priorities, clarifying accountabilities, coaching senior talent, supporting performance, and building a coordinated enterprise architecture capability.

  • Sets clear enterprise direction while empowering Portfolio Architects, Domain Architects, Solution Architects, delivery teams, and business partners to operate within approved guardrails and formal governance paths.

  • Escalates strategic architecture decisions, material exceptions, and unresolved enterprise trade-offs through formal governance forums when appropriate.

Analytical Skills

  • Uses structured thinking to assess enterprise trade-offs, dependencies, constraints, risks, and architectural options.

  • Simplifies complex enterprise architecture topics to enable executive understanding, alignment, and action.

Collaboration

  • Builds trust across portfolios, architecture roles, business functions, and enterprise governance forums.

  • Resolves architectural tension by focusing on enterprise outcomes, reuse, risk reduction, and sustainable decision-making.

title: Lung Cancer Specialist-Center-North
description:
Job Title: Lung Cancer Specialist-Center-North

Introduction to roleAre you ready to change the trajectory of lung cancer by turning cutting-edge science into real-world impact? Do you thrive in a fast-moving environment where bold ideas and crisp execution accelerate better outcomes for patients and the business?

In this field-based role, you will lead the commercial strategy and execution for our lung cancer portfolio across the Center-North territory, translating brand priorities into measurable results. You will uncover opportunities across the patient journey, remove barriers to optimal care, and ensure that the right patients receive the right medicine at the right time. Working closely with cross-functional partners, you will bring clarity, urgency and precision to a complex market.

This position is designed for impact from day one. Expect four days per week in the field building relationships and driving performance, and one day focused on planning, learning and project work. Your ownership of the territory will help shape care pathways and fuel launches that redefine standards of care.

Accountabilities- Sales Excellence and Territory Leadership: Achieve or exceed lung cancer portfolio targets by building and executing a territory plan aligned to brand and therapy-area priorities. Focus resources where they will create the greatest clinical and commercial impact and manage budgets for maximum return.- Insight-Driven Execution: Use sales, market and customer data to map the patient journey, quantify gaps and risks, and set clear priorities. Continuously adapt plans to changes in competition, guidelines and local treatment dynamics to sustain momentum.- Customer Engagement and Omnichannel Impact: Build trusted, long-term relationships with oncologists and wider care teams. Deliver relevant, personalized engagements across face-to-face, digital and omnichannel channels. Lead or support customer initiatives that address bottlenecks in diagnosis, testing and treatment, and feed insights into territory and cross-functional planning.- Oncology Knowledge and Cross-Functional Collaboration: Maintain deep understanding of disease biology, treatment pathways, our medicines and the competitive landscape. Communicate approved scientific and product information clearly. Partner with Brand, Medical, Market Access and Diagnostics to align opportunities and execute launches and strategic initiatives with excellence.- Compliance and Professional Standards: Conduct all activities in line with AstraZeneca’s Code of Ethics, policies, local regulations and industry standards. Uphold integrity, transparency and professionalism in every interaction.- Immediate to Long-Term Impact: In your first 90 days, establish a sharp territory plan, map priority accounts and secure early wins. Over time, shape pathway adoption, enable successful indications and launches, and contribute to repeatable commercial excellence across the portfolio.

Essential Skills/Experience- Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, healthcare, business or a related field.- Proven experience in pharmaceutical or specialty-care sales.- Demonstrated success in achieving sales and business objectives.- Strong communication, influencing, negotiation and presentation skills.- Strong relationship-building and stakeholder-management capabilities.- Ability to interpret data and translate insights into actions.- Ability to manage a complex territory independently and work effectively in a cross-functional environment.- Proficiency with CRM systems, digital tools and data-driven decision-making.

Desirable Skills/Experience- Previous oncology or specialty-care experience.- Understanding of cancer care pathways and treatment guidelines.- Experience launching new products or indications in a competitive market.- Experience in strategic account management.- Omnichannel customer-engagement experience.

Why AstraZenecaJoin a team where science and enterprise move in lockstep to deliver transformative medicines to people living with cancer. You will operate at pace, trusted to make smart, data-grounded decisions and encouraged to challenge convention when it accelerates patient impact. Expect unexpected teams in the same room—medical experts, data minds and commercial leaders—co-creating solutions and acting quickly. Our pipeline is deep and advancing fast, creating meaningful opportunities to lead launches, shape care environments and see the results of your work in clinics. We value kindness alongside ambition, empowering you to take ownership, speak up and grow as you deliver for patients.

Call to ActionIf you are ready to turn bold science into better outcomes for people with lung cancer across the Center-North territory, step forward and apply to shape what comes next!

title: Global Compliance & Ethics, Director
description:
At Feed the Children, we recognize the value of outstanding people, and we are looking for compassionate changemakers to join our team. We pride ourselves on cultivating a collaborative workplace where employees experience meaningful and rewarding employment and feel engaged in our mission to end childhood hunger. Our passionate team shares a deep sense of purpose, and we dream big to solve complex problems and create positive impact in communities in the U.S. around the world.

Reporting to the Chief Legal Officer, the Global Compliance & Ethics, Director is a key leadership role responsible for ensuring that Feed the Children’s global operations are conducted with integrity, transparency, and in full compliance with applicable laws, donor requirements, and internal policies. This role provides strategic leadership to design and implement a unified global compliance program aligned with U.S. and international standards. This position supports the mission of Feed the Children by fostering a culture of ethical behavior and accountability across diverse geographics while also coordinating cross border regulatory compliance, and providing clear, risk-based reporting to executive leadership and the Board of Directors.

NOTE: The ideal candidate for this position will work from our corporate office in Oklahoma City, OK, however qualified remote candidates residing in the DMV area (District of Columbia, Maryland, and Virginia) or other approved states will also be considered.

Job Requirements:

Education

Bachelor’s degree in law, International Relations, Public Administration, or a related field required. Master’s degree, Juris Doctor (JD), or advanced compliance and ethics certification (e.g. CCEP) strongly preferred.

Experience

7+ years of experience in compliance, legal, or risk management roles – preferably within international NGOs or humanitarian/development-related organizations.

Strong knowledge of U.S. and international regulatory frameworks and donor compliance requirements.

Demonstrated experience developing and managing enterprise-wide Codes of Conduct and core global compliance policies.

Proven ability to lead cross-cultural teams and manage compliance programs in complex, multi-country environments, including designing globally aligned systems and monitoring structures.

Excellent communication, training, and stakeholder engagement skills.

Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate across diverse teams and senior leadership; proficiency with data analytics for monitoring and reporting.

High ethical standards, sound judgment, and commitment to the values of the nonprofit sector.

Advanced skills using Microsoft Office products Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook required.

Experience with dashboarding/ BI and data analytics required.

Any combination of education, training and experience which provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the essential functions of this job may be considered.

Licenses and Certifications

Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional (CCEP) or equivalent strongly preferred

Essential Functions:

Global Compliance Program & Policy Framework

  • Lead the development, implementation, and maintenance of enterprise-wide compliance policies, procedures, controls, and standards aligned with global regulations and best practices.
  • Lead the development, periodic review, and global rollout of the organization’s Code of Conduct.
  • Develop, maintain, and update core global compliance policies to ensure consistent application across all entities and geographies.
  • Partner with global and local leadership to contextualize, translate, communicate, and embed the Code of Conduct and related compliance policies into organizational culture.
  • Establish and maintain ethics and compliance governance structures for all Feed the Children entities.

Hotline Administration, Risk Assessment & Reporting

  • Serve as the global hotline administrator, ensuring timely investigation of concerns, effective and confidential reporting channels, trend analysis, and continuous improvement of reporting mechanisms.
  • Maintain and update the global Enterprise Risk Assessment (ERA) and risk registers, including ownership of ERA tools, mitigation planning, ongoing risk reporting, and escalation of high-risk issues.

Monitoring, Regulatory Alignment & Program Updates

  • Monitor regulatory, donor, and industry changes to ensure compliance policies, training, and controls remain current.
  • Collaborate with Legal to horizon scan regulatory developments and coordinate cross-border compliance updates.
  • Oversee compliance monitoring and assessment activities, ensuring appropriate remediation and program updates.

Data, Technology & Dashboard Reporting

  • Develop and maintain compliance dashboards for executive and Board reporting, including quarterly compliance check-ins and risk-based monitoring indicators.
  • Utilize compliance technology and data analytics to produce timely dashboards, heat maps, and KPI/KRI metrics.

Training, Awareness & Capacity Building

  • Design and deliver global compliance training, including onboarding, annual refreshers, and targeted modules for high‑risk roles and geographies.
  • Champion a culture of ethics, integrity, respectful conduct, and ethical decision-making across the organization.

Program Evaluation & Continuous Improvement

  • Conduct periodic maturity assessments of the Ethics & Compliance Program, identify gaps, and implement improvement plans with measurable outcomes.
  • Support reporting to management and the Board on program effectiveness, remediation status, and culture indicators.

About Feed the Children:

As a leading anti-hunger organization, Feed the Children is committed to ending childhood hunger. For children everywhere, we believe that having enough to eat is a fundamental right.

Feed the Children is a global movement focused on ending childhood hunger in the U.S. and around the world. Working alongside communities, we provide food, essentials, and opportunities to children and families who need them most so every child can survive and thrive.

We are committed to helping families experiencing hunger and hardship so children have what they need to stay healthy, learn, and grow. By uniting people and inspiring action, we work to create a world where no child goes to bed hungry. Compassion has no borders. We believe that every child deserves a chance to thrive.

We are driven by a shared sense of PURPOSE. At Feed the Children, our commitment to the mission is at the heart of what we do and fuels our collective impact in the communities where we serve.

We cannot achieve our bold vision without our talented PEOPLE. We are passionate about fostering a best-in-class workforce that is engaged, respected, and empowered to deliver results.

We believe in CURIOSITY and continued learning. Success requires a culture of discovery, curiosity and continued learning to expand our knowledge, seek new perspectives and challenge the status quo.

We know COLLABORATION is the only way to end childhood hunger. We cannot succeed alone. It will take all of us – our employees, donors, partners, volunteers – working together to accomplish our ambitious goals.

We DREAM big. When we work together, we collectively reimagine what is possible. We dream big to solve complex problems and create deep impact in communities around the world.

We VALUE every donor. We respect our donors’ intentions and promote responsible stewardship of the resources they entrust to us.

Join Feed the Children and help create a world where no child goes to bed hungry.

title: Tank Inspection Technician
description:
About Us

Family-owned and operated since 1970, we are an industry-leading gas distributor founded on unparalleled customer service. Our industrial, medical, food, and specialty gas products support a variety of industries that work daily to improve the world we live in, and our ongoing commitment to serve spans the southwestern United States with locations across California and Arizona. Discover the most interesting industry you’ve never heard of!


Position Overview

The Technician is responsible for safely inspecting, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing bulk and microbulk liquid and gaseous cryogenic supply systems at customer locations. This position ensures systems operate safely, reliably, and in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, industry standards, and company procedures.

The Technician works independently in the field and communicates professionally with customers, project managers, sales representatives, contractors, engineers, inspectors, and other internal and external partners.


Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Perform annual, periodic, and preventive maintenance inspections of bulk and microbulk systems to verify safe operation and compliance with applicable codes, regulations, manufacturer specifications, and company standards.
  • Inspect, troubleshoot, maintain, and repair cryogenic liquid and gaseous supply systems and associated components.
  • Install, repair, test, and troubleshoot system telemetry and monitoring equipment.
  • Identify and repair system leaks using approved testing methods and safety procedures.
  • Repair or replace pressure regulators, pressure-relief devices, valves, gauges, fittings, piping components, and other system equipment.
  • Perform tube bending, fitting installation, and minor piping repairs in accordance with applicable specifications and procedures.
  • Complete tank cleaning, washing, refurbishment, surface preparation, and painting.
  • Install and maintain the required decals, labels, and warning signs that identify hazards, ownership, operating settings, and emergency contact information.
  • Conduct operational and safety checks following repairs to confirm system integrity and proper performance.
  • Accurately complete inspection reports, service records, work orders, parts documentation, and other required records.
  • Communicate service findings, safety concerns, repair recommendations, and work status promptly and professionally.
  • Maintain an appropriate inventory of tools, replacement parts, and supplies needed to support the assigned customer base.
  • Keep company vehicles, tools, and equipment clean, organized, secure, and in safe operating condition.
  • Follow all company safety policies, customer-site requirements, and applicable regulatory standards, including the proper use of personal protective equipment.
  • Safely operate forklifts, scissor lifts, boom lifts, and other equipment required to perform assigned work.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

title: Director of Finance
description:
Neyer Properties is a Cincinnati-based real estate development and asset management company with a diversified portfolio of commercial, industrial, and mixed-use properties. We provide complete commercial real estate solutions through our unique approach of enhancing the value of local real estate assets, commitment to excellence, adaptability to change, and cultivation of relationships. Our expertise and experience touch all facets of commercial real estate, having developed more than 3,500 acres of land and hundreds of projects totaling over $3 billion in construction and development throughout Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana, North Carolina, and Tennessee.


The Director of Finance leads financial performance analysis and reporting across the company's acquisition/disposition prospects, and active developments. This role owns the company's debt strategy, including loan requests, renewals, and portfolio-wide risk management, as well as leads equity and capital formation efforts and coordinates financial modeling and due diligence for loan and transaction closings. The Director of Finance is also responsible for company-wide cash management, ensuring capital is fully utilized across the portfolio while all financial obligations are met.


This position reports to Neyer Properties' President & CEO and directly supervises the Financial Analyst.


Key Responsibilities

Debt Strategy & Banking Relationships

  • Review the existing loan portfolio and develop a strategy for modifications based on maturities, loan balances, risk, guarantees, and other critical factors that support continued growth while reducing overall risk
  • Present and implement loan strategy in response to changing economic conditions, including minimizing recourse obligations and eliminating personal guarantees from the CEO
  • Maintain and cultivate banking relationships; deliver timely due diligence materials to banks in support of financing requests
  • Prepare all documentation required for loan requests and renewals, including global cash flow analysis, collateral analysis, industry analysis, management analysis, and overall repayment capacity
  • Ensure business terms and structure are accurately captured in loan documentation to protect the company's interests and reduce risk
  • Ensure prompt delivery of, and compliance with, financial statements and loan covenants
  • Increase capacity and efficiency with lenders, expanding the company's lending relationships over time

Equity & Capital Formation

  • Lead equity and capital-raising strategy to support continued growth in acquisitions and development
  • Develop and implement a plan for raising equity through both private placement memoranda (PPMs) and larger institutional equity providers
  • Coordinate with legal counsel to ensure equity offerings comply with applicable securities regulations

Financial Planning, Modeling & Reporting

  • Manages the financial cash flow models and develop sensitivity analyses across the company
  • Develop and manage financial proforma models and assumptions for acquisitions/dispositions, new developments, and existing projects, updating as required
  • Deliver the Portfolio/Company Fair Market Value (FMV) Balance Sheet annually and as needed
  • Deliver quarterly loan summary reports
  • Explore strategies to maximize the long-term value of the overall real estate portfolio

Transaction & Due Diligence Support

  • Work with the Acquisitions/Dispositions and Development teams to coordinate and perform due diligence for loan closings, including review of loan documents, funding statements, and appraisal reports
  • Oversee debt and equity structuring on new transactions to reduce risk and increase returns

Cash Management

  • Manage company-wide cash to ensure capital is fully utilized and all financial obligations are met
  • Partner with Development and Acquisitions/Dispositions on cash needs, sale strategy, and deployment of available cash to maintain the company's target operating (“peg”) balance

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Support

  • Manage and develop the Financial Analyst
  • Other duties as assigned


Qualifications

Experience & Education

  • At least 15 years of commercial real estate and finance experience
  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Real Estate, or a related field required
  • Demonstrated experience negotiating commercial real estate debt (construction, permanent, and mezzanine financing) and managing institutional banking relationships
  • Experience leading or supporting private placement equity offerings (PPMs) and institutional capital relationships
  • Advanced financial modeling skills; proficiency in Excel required, Argus experience preferred
  • Working knowledge of GAAP and fair value accounting concepts as applied to real estate assets

Professional Attributes

  • Independent, self-directed, and takes initiative
  • Proactive, assertive, and decisive
  • Thrives in a rapid-paced, dynamic work environment
  • Organized, timely, and focused on achieving results
  • Strong communication and reporting skills
  • Strategic in approach, with demonstrated ability to multitask
  • Appropriately risk-taking and flexible
